    fn platform_state_transitions_are_validated() {
        let mut state = PlatformState::new();
        assert_eq!(state.lifecycle(), Lifecycle::Starting);
        // The full valid chain: Starting → Running → Suspended → Running →
        // ShuttingDown → Stopped.
        state.transition(Lifecycle::Running).unwrap();
        state.transition(Lifecycle::Suspended).unwrap();
        state.transition(Lifecycle::Running).unwrap();
        state.transition(Lifecycle::ShuttingDown).unwrap();
        state.transition(Lifecycle::Stopped).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(state.lifecycle(), Lifecycle::Stopped);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_platform_state_transitions_are_rejected() {
        let mut state = PlatformState::new();
        // Starting → Suspended (skips Running) is invalid.
        assert!(state.transition(Lifecycle::Suspended).is_err());
        // Starting → ShuttingDown is invalid.
        assert!(state.transition(Lifecycle::ShuttingDown).is_err());
        state.transition(Lifecycle::Running).unwrap();
        // Running → Running is invalid.
        assert!(state.transition(Lifecycle::Running).is_err());
        state.transition(Lifecycle::Suspended).unwrap();
        // Suspended → ShuttingDown is valid (shutdown from suspension);
        // Suspended → Suspended is not.
        assert!(state.transition(Lifecycle::Suspended).is_err());
        state.transition(Lifecycle::ShuttingDown).unwrap();
        // ShuttingDown → Running is invalid.
        assert!(state.transition(Lifecycle::Running).is_err());
        state.transition(Lifecycle::Stopped).unwrap();
        // Stopped is terminal.
        assert!(state.transition(Lifecycle::Running).is_err());
        assert!(state.transition(Lifecycle::Stopped).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn suspension_blocks_requests_and_resume_restores_them() {
        let mut platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
        // Running: the Request → Response round-trip succeeds.
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                )
                .is_ok()
        );
        // Suspend: the backbone gate rejects normal service requests.
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(platform.state.lifecycle(), Lifecycle::Suspended);
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        // Resume: the round-trip succeeds again.
        platform.resume().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(platform.state.lifecycle(), Lifecycle::Running);
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                )
                .is_ok()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn suspend_and_resume_are_validated() {
        let mut platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
        // Double suspension is rejected (Running → Running is not a
        // transition; the state gate fires before any authority moves).
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        assert!(platform.suspend().is_err());
        // Resume on a suspended platform is the only way back to Running.
        platform.resume().unwrap();
        // Resuming a running platform is rejected.
        assert!(platform.resume().is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn domain_state_survives_suspend_and_resume() {
        let (_dir, mut platform) = temp_platform();
        // Open the workspace through the real path (Phase 7F.3 state).
        platform
            .invoke_service(
                crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
            )
            .unwrap();
        // Suspend is pause, not shutdown: no domain state is destroyed.
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        platform.resume().unwrap();
        // The same domain state remains available after resume.
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            response.payload(),
            crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected(summary)
                if summary == "workspace: ra-main"
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn shutdown_stops_the_platform_state() {
        // The handle is consumed by shutdown; the deterministic teardown
        // ordering (ShuttingDown → kernel shutdown → Stopped) completes.
        let platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
        assert!(platform.shutdown().is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn shutdown_from_suspension_completes() {
        let mut platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        // Shutdown is valid from Suspended as well as from Running.
        assert!(platform.shutdown().is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn shutdown_consumes_the_platform_handle() {
        // Single-owner shutdown: the handle is moved into shutdown and can
        // never be reused — a second shutdown is a compile-time error, and
        // no request can be made through a shut-down platform.
        let platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
        assert!(platform.shutdown().is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_requests_round_trip_with_correlation() {
        let platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
        // Phase 7G: a storage inspection travels the full Request → Response
        // round-trip — Request + target + operation + correlation id →
        // Backbone → Storage Authority → Storage Service → ServiceResult →
        // ResponsePayload → Response → Backbone reply → caller.
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
            )
            .unwrap();
        // The correlation survives the storage round-trip: the Response
        // answers exactly the Request that was sent.
        assert!(response.correlation().is_some());
        response
            .verify_answers(response.correlation().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        // The Response is addressed back to the requesting caller with the
        // storage service's real state summary.
        assert_eq!(response.kind(), crate::hub::BackboneMessageKind::Response);
        assert_eq!(response.source(), crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_eq!(response.target(), Some(crate::hub::HubId::DEVICE));
        assert!(matches!(
            response.payload(),
            crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected(summary)
                if summary == "storage: stack=syss,pss,recovery; categories=8"
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_requests_follow_the_platform_lifecycle() {
        let mut platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
        // Running: storage requests succeed.
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                )
                .is_ok()
        );
        // Suspended: the backbone gate rejects the storage request; no
        // storage operation executes and no domain state is destroyed.
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        // Resumed: storage is available again.
        platform.resume().unwrap();
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                )
                .is_ok()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_storage_error_crosses_the_service_boundary_as_a_rejection() {
        let platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
        // A Request carrying a non-Inspect operation is an invalid storage
        // invocation: the Storage Service rejects it, and the rejection
        // travels back through the round-trip as a Rejected Response — the
        // storage error crosses the service/communication boundary, not the
        // transport layer (no fabricated delivery).
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Accept,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(response.payload(), &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Rejected);
    }

    /// A `TempDir`-backed platform over the given storage root.
    fn storage_platform() -> (crate::test_support::TempDir, SySS) {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-platform");
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        (dir, platform)
    }

    /// A `TempDir`-backed platform over an isolated storage root.
    ///
    /// Tests that **open** active objects use this instead of the default
    /// root so their persisted state never touches the repository's
    /// `ra-data` directory and never leaks between runs.
    fn temp_platform() -> (crate::test_support::TempDir, SySS) {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-platform");
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        (dir, platform)
    }

    fn save_artifact(platform: &SySS, name: &str, text: &str) -> crate::hub::Response {
        platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Save {
                    category: crate::StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: name.to_owned(),
                    artifact: ra_persistence::Artifact::Program(ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new(
                        name, text,
                    )),
                },
            )
            .unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn initialize_establishes_the_platform_storage_root() {
        // Phase 7G.1: platform startup establishes the storage root — the
        // root and every storage category directory exist, and the platform
        // owns the Syss handle over the root.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-root");
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        assert!(dir.path().is_dir());
        for category in crate::StorageCategory::ALL {
            assert!(
                platform.storage.category_dir(category).is_dir(),
                "{category} dir missing"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn startup_runs_crash_recovery_over_the_storage_root() {
        // Phase 7G.1: an interrupted atomic write left before startup is
        // resolved by the startup recovery pass.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-startup-recovery");
        std::fs::write(dir.path().join("stale.ra.ra-tmp"), b"let x = 1;").unwrap();
        // The platform startup pass runs recovery over the root before the
        // platform is Ready.
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(platform.state.lifecycle(), Lifecycle::Running);
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(dir.path().join("stale.ra")).unwrap(),
            b"let x = 1;"
        );
        assert!(!dir.path().join("stale.ra.ra-tmp").exists());
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_storage_root_fails_initialization_safely() {
        // Phase 7G.1: an invalid root fails the boot through the existing
        // error boundary — never silently ignored.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-invalid-root");
        let file = dir.path().join("blocker");
        std::fs::write(&file, b"x").unwrap();
        // A file in the place of the root: creating the root must fail.
        let bad_root = file.join("ra-data");
        assert!(SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(bad_root).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_save_and_load_round_trip_through_the_backbone() {
        // Phase 7G.1 proof: Request → Backbone → StorageAuthority →
        // StorageService → Syss/Pss → ServiceResult → Response → caller.
        let (dir, platform) = storage_platform();
        // Save: the artifact is persisted through the existing stack.
        let save = save_artifact(&platform, "main.ra", "let x = 1;");
        assert_eq!(save.payload(), &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Completed);
        save.verify_answers(save.correlation().unwrap()).unwrap();
        // The entry exists in the artifacts category with the PSS `.ra`
        // serialization (the real persistence path, not a fabricated one).
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(dir.path().join("artifacts/main.ra")).unwrap(),
            b"let x = 1;"
        );
        // Load: the entry is read back and deserialized through the same
        // stack, answered as a correlated Response.
        let load = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Load {
                    category: crate::StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: "main.ra".to_owned(),
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            load.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Loaded("loaded main.ra: program: let x = 1;".to_owned())
        );
        load.verify_answers(load.correlation().unwrap()).unwrap();
        // The save and load responses are distinct correlated exchanges.
        assert_ne!(save.correlation(), load.correlation());
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_recovery_round_trips_through_the_backbone() {
        let (dir, platform) = storage_platform();
        // An interrupted atomic write is left behind.
        std::fs::write(dir.path().join("main.ra.ra-tmp"), b"let x = 1;").unwrap();
        let recover = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Recover,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            recover.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Recovered(
                "recovery: scanned=1, restored=1, removed=0, failed=0".to_owned()
            )
        );
        recover
            .verify_answers(recover.correlation().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(dir.path().join("main.ra")).unwrap(),
            b"let x = 1;"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_errors_cross_the_boundary_as_rejections() {
        let (_dir, platform) = storage_platform();
        // Loading a missing entry: the transport succeeded (delivered and
        // acknowledged) but the storage operation failed — the Load is
        // answered with a Rejected Response, never a fabricated success.
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Load {
                    category: crate::StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: "missing.ra".to_owned(),
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(response.payload(), &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Rejected);
        response
            .verify_answers(response.correlation().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_operations_follow_the_platform_lifecycle() {
        let (dir, mut platform) = storage_platform();
        // Running: Save and Load succeed.
        save_artifact(&platform, "main.ra", "let x = 1;");
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Load {
                        category: crate::StorageCategory::Artifact,
                        name: "main.ra".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .is_ok()
        );
        // Suspended: normal storage operations are rejected by the backbone
        // gate; no storage operation executes.
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Save {
                        category: crate::StorageCategory::Artifact,
                        name: "main.ra".to_owned(),
                        artifact: ra_persistence::Artifact::Program(
                            ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new("main.ra", "x")
                        ),
                    },
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::STORAGE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Recover,
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        // Resumed: storage is available again.
        platform.resume().unwrap();
        save_artifact(&platform, "main.ra", "let x = 1;");
        // No data is destroyed by suspension or shutdown: the persisted
        // entry survives on disk.
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert!(dir.path().join("artifacts/main.ra").is_file());
    }

    // ── Phase 7H: document round-trips ────────────────────────

    #[test]
    fn document_operations_round_trip_through_the_backbone() {
        let (dir, platform) = storage_platform();
        let source = dir.path().join("main.ra");
        std::fs::write(&source, "let x = 1;").unwrap();
        // Phase 7H proof: Request → Backbone → Workspace Authority →
        // Workspace Service → Document active object → ServiceResult →
        // Response → caller, correlation preserved.
        let opened = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::OpenDocument { source },
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            opened.payload(),
            crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Opened(summary) if summary == "opened main.ra"
        ));
        opened
            .verify_answers(opened.correlation().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        // The document reads its current state through the round-trip.
        let inspected = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::InspectDocument,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            inspected.payload(),
            crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected(summary)
                if summary == "document: main.ra: let x = 1;"
        ));
        inspected
            .verify_answers(inspected.correlation().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        // Save and close complete as correlated Responses.
        let saved = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::SaveDocument,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(saved.payload(), &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Completed);
        saved.verify_answers(saved.correlation().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let closed = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::CloseDocument,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(closed.payload(), &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Completed);
        closed
            .verify_answers(closed.correlation().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        // Distinct exchanges carry distinct correlation identifiers.
        assert_ne!(opened.correlation(), inspected.correlation());
        assert_ne!(inspected.correlation(), saved.correlation());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_document_rejection_round_trips_as_a_rejected_response() {
        let (_dir, platform) = storage_platform();
        // Saving with no document open is a deterministic service rejection:
        // the transport succeeded, the document operation did not — the
        // Rejected response is the honest communication outcome.
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::SaveDocument,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(response.payload(), &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Rejected);
        response
            .verify_answers(response.correlation().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_operations_follow_the_platform_lifecycle() {
        let (dir, mut platform) = storage_platform();
        let source = dir.path().join("main.ra");
        std::fs::write(&source, "let x = 1;").unwrap();
        // Running: the document round-trip succeeds.
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::OpenDocument {
                        source: source.clone(),
                    },
                )
                .is_ok()
        );
        // Suspended: the backbone gate rejects the document request; no
        // document operation executes and no state is destroyed.
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::InspectDocument,
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::SaveDocument,
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        // Resumed: the same document state is preserved and available again.
        platform.resume().unwrap();
        let inspected = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::InspectDocument,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            inspected.payload(),
            crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected(summary)
                if summary == "document: main.ra: let x = 1;"
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn project_association_flows_through_the_backbone() {
        let (_dir, platform) = temp_platform();
        // Phase 7H: OpenIn travels as a Command through the backbone to the
        // Project Authority's service, which opens the real project object
        // inside its workspace.
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::PROJECT,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::OpenIn {
                        name: "ra-lib".to_owned(),
                        parent: "ra-main".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // The association is observable through the Request → Response path.
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::PROJECT,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("project: ra-lib in ra-main".to_owned())
        );
    }

        );
    }

    // ── Phase 7H.1: persisted domain state through the platform ──

    #[test]
    fn persisted_domain_state_survives_a_platform_restart() {
        // Phase 7H.1: workspace/project/package state is persisted through
        // the existing Syss/PSS stack, so after a full platform shutdown and
        // restart over the same storage root the objects reopen with their
        // state and associations restored.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-restart");
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::PROJECT,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::OpenIn {
                        name: "ra-lib".to_owned(),
                        parent: "ra-main".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::PACKAGE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::OpenIn {
                        name: "ra-pkg".to_owned(),
                        parent: "ra-lib".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Shutdown does not delete the persisted state.
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert!(dir.path().join("workspaces/ra-main").is_file());
        assert!(dir.path().join("projects/ra-lib").is_file());
        assert!(dir.path().join("packages/ra-pkg").is_file());

        // A fresh platform over the same root restores everything through
        // the normal open path.
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Reopening the project standalone restores its workspace
        // association from the persisted state.
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::PROJECT,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-lib".to_owned()),
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::PROJECT,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("project: ra-lib in ra-main".to_owned())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::PACKAGE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-pkg".to_owned()),
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::PACKAGE,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("package: ra-pkg in ra-lib".to_owned())
        );
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_conflicting_persisted_association_is_rejected_after_restart() {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-conflict");
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            platform

            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );

        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        // The recorded association is authoritative: requesting a different

        assert_eq!(
            platform

                    crate::hub::HubId::PROJECT,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::OpenIn {

                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Rejected
        );

    }

    #[test]
    fn suspended_platform_rejects_persisted_opens_and_resume_restores_them() {
        let (_dir, mut platform) = temp_platform();
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Suspended: the backbone Active gate rejects object operations
        // before any persistence or lifecycle work runs.
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        assert!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("other".to_owned()),
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        assert!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::PROJECT,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-lib".to_owned()),
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        // Resumed: operations (and persistence) work again; the state opened
        // before suspension is preserved.
        platform.resume().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Close,
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::WORKSPACE,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("other".to_owned()),
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
    }

    // ── Phase 7H.2: settings / history / log through the platform ──

    #[test]
    fn settings_history_and_log_persist_through_the_platform() {
        // Phase 7H.2: the platform-state domains ride the full path —
        // Request → Backbone → Authority → Service → Syss/PSS → Response —
        // and survive a platform restart.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h2-restart");
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        // Settings: set + retrieve through the round-trip.
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Set {
                        key: "theme".to_owned(),
                        value: "dark".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("dark".to_owned())
        );
        // History: record.
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::HISTORY,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Record("open workspace".to_owned()),
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Log: a structured record.
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::LOG,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::RecordLog {
                        severity: crate::hub::LogSeverity::Warning,
                        source: "platform".to_owned(),
                        message: "slow boot".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Shutdown does not delete the persisted state.
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert!(dir.path().join("settings/theme").is_file());
        assert!(dir.path().join("history/history").is_file());
        assert!(dir.path().join("logs/log").is_file());

        // A fresh platform over the same root restores everything.
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("dark".to_owned())
        );
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::HISTORY,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected(
                "history: 1 entries [open workspace]".to_owned()
            )
        );
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::LOG,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("log: 1 entries [slow boot]".to_owned())
        );
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn theme_and_view_are_settings_state_through_the_platform() {
        let (_dir, platform) = temp_platform();
        // Deterministic defaults before any update.
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("light".to_owned())
        );
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Get("view".to_owned()),
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("editor".to_owned())
        );
        // Valid updates complete and persist.
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Set {
                        key: "theme".to_owned(),
                        value: "dark".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Set {
                        key: "view".to_owned(),
                        value: "terminal".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Invalid values are rejected.
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Set {
                        key: "theme".to_owned(),
                        value: "blue".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn suspended_platform_rejects_settings_operations_and_resume_restores_them() {
        let (_dir, mut platform) = temp_platform();
        assert_eq!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Set {
                        key: "theme".to_owned(),
                        value: "dark".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .unwrap(),
            crate::hub::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Suspended: the backbone Active gate rejects settings operations
        // before any persistence or state work runs.
        platform.suspend().unwrap();
        assert!(
            platform
                .invoke_service(
                    crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Set {
                        key: "view".to_owned(),
                        value: "terminal".to_owned(),
                    },
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        assert!(
            platform
                .request(
                    crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                    crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
                )
                .is_err()
        );
        // Resumed: settings operations work again and the pre-suspension
        // state is preserved.
        platform.resume().unwrap();
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Inspected("dark".to_owned())
        );
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn corrupt_settings_are_rejected_through_the_platform() {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h2-corrupt-settings");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("settings")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.path().join("settings/theme"), b"\xff\xfe not utf-8").unwrap();
        let platform = SySS::initialize_with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned()).unwrap();
        // Startup succeeds (loading is lazy); the first settings operation
        // rejects deterministically.
        let response = platform
            .request(
                crate::hub::HubId::SETTINGS,
                crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(response.payload(), &crate::hub::ResponsePayload::Rejected);
        platform.shutdown().unwrap();
    }
}

=== SERVICE CONTRACT ===
//! Platform services (Phases 7F.1–7F.3).
//!
//! The common, domain-neutral **service abstraction** owned by each SySS
//! Authority, and the **Platform Services** of the platform.
//!
//! # Authority → Service
//!
//! The platform ownership chain is fixed: `Authority → State → Services →
//! Events → Policies`. An authority owns its domain's **services**; a
//! service never owns its authority. Services are reached **through their
//! owning authority, never directly** — the Platform Backbone transports
//! communication to the authority, and the authority forwards to the service
//! it owns (Phase 7F.1: [`HubAuthority::invoke`](crate::hub::HubAuthority::invoke)).
//!
//! # Backbone vs Authority vs Service
//!
//! The layers of the communication path have distinct responsibilities:
//!
//! * **Backbone** — communication / delivery (the `backbone` module); its
//!   [`DeliveryReceipt`](crate::hub::backbone::DeliveryReceipt) is the
//!   message transport / delivery result;
//! * **Authority** — domain ownership (the `authority` module);
//! * **Service** — domain work (this module); its [`ServiceResult`] is the
//!   service execution result.
//!
//! # Lifecycle relationship
//!
//! Service availability is synchronized with the owning authority's
//! lifecycle (Phase 7F.5):
//!
//! `Authority Registered → Initialized → Active → Service Ready`
//!
//! * **Authority Active** → service ready and executable;
//! * **Authority Suspended** → service unavailable for normal execution
//!   (its domain state is preserved for resume);
//! * **Authority Shutdown** → service unavailable permanently.
//!
//! The authority's invocation boundary
//! ([`HubAuthority::invoke`](crate::hub::HubAuthority::invoke)) is the **single
//! availability gate**: it refuses to invoke a service on any authority that
//! is not [`HubLifecycle::Active`](crate::hub::HubLifecycle) — including
//! Suspended and Shutdown authorities (rejecting with
//! [`HubError::InactiveTarget`](crate::hub::HubError)). The service lifecycle
//! stays minimal ([`ServiceLifecycle::Ready`]) by design: the Authority owns
//! the domain lifecycle, the Service owns availability/readiness, and the
//! two are synchronized through the authority gate rather than duplicated
//! service lifecycle state.
//!
//! # Service binding
//!
//! Services are bound to their owning authorities by composition: each
//! concrete authority owns exactly the service of its domain (Phase 7F.2),
//! exposed through [`HubAuthority::service`](crate::hub::HubAuthority::service).
//! There is **no second registry**: the hub [`Registry`](crate::hub::Registry)
//! registers hubs/authorities; service binding is the authority-ownership
//! model itself, and the two responsibilities stay separate.
//!
//! # The Platform Services (Phases 7F.2–7F.3)
//!
//! Phase 7F.2 populated the 7F.1 foundation with the seven domain services,
//! one per domain; Phase 7F.3 converts them from proof-only operations into
//! the first real domain-state services:
//!
//! | Service | Owned by | Domain state (7F.3; 7H active objects; 7H.1 persistence) |
//! |---------|----------|----------------------|
//! | [`WorkspaceService`] | Workspace Authority | the real [`Workspace`] and [`Document`] objects, persisted through Syss/PSS (`workspaces/`, `files/`) |
//! | [`ProjectService`] | Project Authority | the real [`Project`] object (workspace association), persisted through Syss/PSS (`projects/`) |
//! | [`PackageService`] | Package Authority | the real [`Package`] object (project association), persisted through Syss/PSS (`packages/`) |
//! | [`SettingsService`] | Settings Authority | in-memory key/value map |
//! | [`HistoryService`] | History Authority | in-memory operation entries |
//! | [`LogService`] | Log Authority | in-memory log entries (7F.1 proof behavior preserved) |
//! | [`StorageService`] | Storage Authority | the real storage stack (Syss/Pss/Recovery over the platform storage root, Phase 7G.1) |
//! | [`DeviceService`] | Device Authority | platform device capability |
//!
//! Every service owns its domain **state privately** (private state types,
//! controlled operations only), and the state is mutated through the single
//! [`Service::invoke`] boundary alone. No service holds a reference to any
//! other service or to the backbone — one service can never mutate another
//! service's state, and cross-domain communication is the backbone's job.
//!
//! # Interior mutability (Phase 7F.3)
//!
//! The invocation boundary is `&self` ([`Service::invoke`]); changing it to
//! `&mut self` would ripple through the frozen authority and kernel
//! boundaries. Services therefore carry their mutable domain state behind
//! [`std::cell::RefCell`]. This is safe in the frozen architecture: the
//! platform is single-threaded and deterministic-synchronous, and no borrow
//! is ever held across a service-call boundary — `borrow()`/`borrow_mut()`
//! cannot conflict.
//!
//! # Operation / kind relationship (Phase 7F.3)
//!
//! Real operations travel as the payload
//! [`BackbonePayload::Operation`](crate::hub::backbone::BackbonePayload) —
//! the explicit domain-neutral [`ServiceOperation`] vocabulary (`Open`,
//! `Close`, `Set`, `Record`, `Clear`, `Probe`, `Inspect`, `Accept`). No
//! untyped maps, no serialization, no `ra-persistence` coupling. The
//! per-service contract is documented on each service; the common shape:
//!
//! | Message kind | Operation | Result |
//! |--------------|-----------|--------|
//! | Command | the domain's mutating operation (`Open`/`Close`/`Set`/`Record`/`Clear`/`Probe`) or the generic `Accept` | `Completed` |
//! | Request | `Inspect` | `Inspected(summary)` — the synchronous Response |
//! | Notification | any | informational (`Accepted`; the Log service preserves its 7F.1 `Completed`) |
//! | Command | `Inspect` | `Rejected` — a directive is not an inspection |
//! | Request | anything but `Inspect` | `Rejected` — a question is not a directive |
//! | Response / Event / Broadcast / LifecycleSignal | any | `Rejected` — not a service request |
//!
//! **Storage service contract (Phase 7G.1):** the storage service is the
//! platform's **request/response storage service** — its real operations
//! (`Save`, `Load`, `Recover`) travel as Requests and are answered with the
//! typed result of the operation (`Completed`, `Loaded(representation)`,
//! `Recovered(report summary)`), or `Rejected` when the operation cannot be
//! performed. A storage failure is a deterministic **service rejection**,
//! never a fabricated success: the transport receipt and the storage result
//! are never conflated (the underlying `ra-syss` storage error stays at the
//! Syss/Pss/Recovery layer).
//!
//! # Request → Response (Phase 7F.4)
//!
//! The Request → Response round-trip is complete: a `Request` carrying
//! `Inspect` is answered with [`ServiceResult::Inspected`], and the
//! round-trip orchestrator (the `platform` module's
//! [`SySS::request`](crate::SySS::request)) converts the service result into
//! a correlated [`Response`](crate::hub::Response) message delivered back
//! over the backbone to the caller (`Request → Backbone → Authority →
//! Service → ServiceResult → Response → Backbone → caller`).
//!
//! Services stay **domain-pure**: they operate on the message kind and the
//! domain operation only ([`ServiceInvocation`]) and return a
//! [`ServiceResult`]; they never see the correlation identifier, the
//! registry, the graph, the router, the kernel or the backbone, and they
//! never build the Response themselves. The ServiceResult → Response
//! conversion is the explicit
//! [`ResponsePayload::from_service_result`](crate::hub::backbone::ResponsePayload::from_service_result)
//! boundary owned by the communication layer.
//!
//! # Storage boundary (Phase 7G → 7G.1)
//!
//! The Storage Service ([`StorageService`]) is the platform-facing storage
//! service. Phase 7G established the boundary: its domain state represents
//! the existing storage architecture — the storage stack
//! ([`StorageStackService`]: the [`crate::Syss`] storage space, the
//! [`crate::Pss`] serialization service and the [`crate::Recovery`]
//! crash-recovery service) over the storage vocabulary
//! ([`crate::StorageCategory`]) — built on the `ra-persistence` codec
//! layer. FSS is not a separate component in the implementation: `Syss` is
//! the file/storage-system boundary.
//!
//! **Phase 7G.1** wires the live operations: the Storage Service now owns
//! the **real storage stack** — a [`Syss`] handle over the platform storage
//! root, the fully wired [`Pss`] codec registry and the [`Recovery`]
//! crash-recovery service — and performs the real storage operations
//! through them: `Save` stores an artifact (validated and serialized by
//! PSS, written by Syss), `Load` reads and deserializes an entry back, and
//! `Recover` runs crash recovery over the root. The service implements no
//! persistence: it calls the existing stack, and the `ra-persistence` codec
//! architecture, PSS and Recovery are untouched. It is reached only through
//! the Platform Backbone and the Storage Authority:
//! `PlatformInterface → Request → Backbone → StorageAuthority →
//! StorageService → Syss / Pss / Recovery → ra-persistence`.
//!
//! # Active-object persistence (Phase 7H.1)
//!
//! Since Phase 7H.1 the **workspace / project / package** active objects are
//! persisted through the same existing stack — no second persistence
//! system. The separation stays explicit:
//!
//! * **Active object** = domain/runtime state (identity + lifecycle +
//!   association), no filesystem access;
//! * **Service** = domain operation + persistence orchestration (load
//!   persisted state, reconstruct the object, persist on open);
//! * **Syss / PSS** = storage / serialization (the `.ra` text codec writes a
//!   small deterministic state text; [`Syss::save`] writes it atomically);
//! * **Recovery** = crash recovery (interrupted `*.ra-tmp` writes are
//!   resolved at startup, before any service sees the root).
//!
//! Persisted state format per object (stored under its own category —
//! `workspaces/`, `projects/`, `packages/`):
//!
//! ```text
//! workspace: <name>
//! project:  <name>          (+ optional `in: <workspace>` line)
//! package:  <name>          (+ optional `in: <project>` line)
//! ```
//!
//! Persistence semantics: opening an object loads and verifies the persisted
//! state when present (missing state opens fresh), then writes the state
//! atomically (the object is persisted by the open). The recorded parent
//! association is **authoritative** on reopen (reopening restores it); a
//! requested parent that conflicts with it is rejected deterministically.
//! Closing never deletes persisted state; shutdown never deletes it either —
//! after a restart the state is restored through the normal open path.
//! Corrupt or mismatched persisted state is a deterministic rejection, never
//! a fabricated success.
//!
//! # Platform-state domains (Phase 7H.2)
//!
//! Phase 7H.2 completes the remaining SySS application-state foundation —
//! **Settings**, **History** and **Log** — as real, persisted platform-state
//! domains (not Active Objects; they remain platform services/state
//! domains). All three persist through the existing stack, exactly like the
//! active objects:
//!
//! * **Settings** ([`SettingsService`]): a controlled key/value map with
//!   deterministic defaults (`theme` → `light`, `view` → `editor`) and
//!   validated values, persisted as one file per key in `settings/`. Theme
//!   and view are settings-backed **platform state** — no rendering, no UI;
//!   the Frontend consumes them later. Values with a fixed set (`theme` ∈
//!   `light`/`dark`, `view` ∈ `editor`/`terminal`/`ide`) are validated;
//!   generic keys accept any non-empty value free of line breaks/NUL.
//! * **History** ([`HistoryService`]): an ordered list of recorded platform
//!   operations — application/platform history, **not** RA runtime/execution
//!   history — persisted as one line per entry in `history/history`. The
//!   service never inspects another service's state; the caller provides the
//!   entry explicitly.
//! * **Log** ([`LogService`]): the smallest real platform logging subsystem
//!   — an ordered list of structured [`LogRecord`]s (deterministic sequence,
//!   [`LogSeverity`], source/domain, message), persisted as one
//!   `<severity> <source> <message>` line per record in `logs/log`. The log
//!   is a SySS/application concern, **not** an RA language/runtime logger.
//!   The Phase 7F.1 proof behavior is preserved. Loading is **lazy** (on the
//!   first operation), so corrupt persisted state never fails the boot — it
//!   rejects the first access deterministically.
//!
//! Persistence is lazy-loaded and written through [`Syss::save`] (atomic);
//! recovery is the existing startup pass. Suspended/Shutdown authorities
//! reject through the existing backbone `Active` gate; resume restores the
//! preserved state.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fmt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use ra_persistence::Artifact;

use super::backbone::{BackboneMessage, BackboneMessageKind, BackbonePayload};
use super::{
    ActiveObjectId, ActiveObjectKind, Document, HubId, HubResult, Package, Project, Workspace,
};
use crate::{Pss, Recovery, RecoveryReport, StorageCategory, Syss};

/// The storage category that holds loaded documents (Phase 7H).
///
/// Documents are "files currently loaded into the IDE" — the SySS `files`
/// category — persisted through the existing Syss/PSS stack.
const DOCUMENT_CATEGORY: StorageCategory = StorageCategory::LoadedFile;

/// The storage categories that hold the persisted domain state of the
/// active objects (Phase 7H.1): workspaces in `workspaces/`, projects in
/// `projects/` and packages in `packages/` — the existing SySS categories,
/// written atomically through the existing Syss/PSS stack.
const WORKSPACE_CATEGORY: StorageCategory = StorageCategory::Workspace;
const PROJECT_CATEGORY: StorageCategory = StorageCategory::Project;
const PACKAGE_CATEGORY: StorageCategory = StorageCategory::Package;

/// The storage categories of the platform-state domains (Phase 7H.2):
/// settings in `settings/`, history in `history/`, logs in `logs/` — the
/// existing SySS categories, written atomically through the existing
/// Syss/PSS stack.
const SETTINGS_CATEGORY: StorageCategory = StorageCategory::Settings;
const HISTORY_CATEGORY: StorageCategory = StorageCategory::History;
const LOG_CATEGORY: StorageCategory = StorageCategory::Logs;

/// The persisted file names of the history and log stores inside their
/// categories (Phase 7H.2): a single deterministic file per domain, holding
/// the ordered entries as text lines.
const HISTORY_FILE: &str = "history";
const LOG_FILE: &str = "log";

/// The stable identity of a platform service.
///
/// A service is identified by its stable name within its owning domain
/// ("workspace", "project", ..., "log"). Identity is fixed at creation and
/// never reused.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ServiceId(String);

impl ServiceId {
    /// Creates a service identity from a stable name.
    pub(crate) fn new(name: &str) -> ServiceId {
        ServiceId(name.to_owned())
    }

    /// Returns the stable name of this service.
    pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for ServiceId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.name())
    }
}

/// The minimal lifecycle vocabulary of a platform service.
///
/// Kept minimal by design (Phases 7F.1–7F.5): the only state is
/// [`ServiceLifecycle::Ready`]. Service **availability** — ready, suspended
/// (unavailable, state preserved) or shut down (unavailable permanently) —
/// is synchronized with the owning authority's lifecycle at the invocation
/// boundary ([`HubAuthority::invoke`](crate::hub::HubAuthority::invoke)):
/// a service executes domain operations only while its authority is
/// [`HubLifecycle::Active`](crate::hub::HubLifecycle). The authority owns
/// the domain lifecycle; the service owns readiness — the two are never
/// duplicated.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ServiceLifecycle {
    /// The service is ready to perform domain work.
    Ready,
}

/// The common state every platform service carries.
///
/// Service identity ([`ServiceId`]), the owning authority's hub ([`HubId`])
/// and the service lifecycle ([`ServiceLifecycle`]). Domain-neutral — reused
/// by every domain service through composition, never inheritance.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ServiceCore {
    id: ServiceId,
    owner: HubId,
    lifecycle: ServiceLifecycle,
}

impl ServiceCore {
    /// Creates a service core owned by the authority of `owner`, born
    /// [`ServiceLifecycle::Ready`].
    ///
    /// The service is only *reachable* once its owning authority is
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Active`](crate::hub::HubLifecycle) — that gate lives
    /// on the authority's invocation boundary, not here (a service never
    /// owns its authority).
    pub(crate) fn new(id: ServiceId, owner: HubId) -> ServiceCore {
        ServiceCore {
            id,
            owner,
            lifecycle: ServiceLifecycle::Ready,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the identity of this service.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests inspect service
    /// identity; future service registries and lookups consume it
    /// (TODO(Phase7F.4)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn id(&self) -> &ServiceId {
        &self.id
    }

    /// Returns the hub whose authority owns this service.
    pub(crate) fn owner(&self) -> HubId {
        self.owner
    }

    /// Returns the lifecycle state of this service.
    pub(crate) fn lifecycle(&self) -> ServiceLifecycle {
        self.lifecycle
    }

    /// Returns whether this service is [`ServiceLifecycle::Ready`].
    pub(crate) fn is_ready(&self) -> bool {
        self.lifecycle() == ServiceLifecycle::Ready
    }
}

/// The common Service contract — the domain-neutral service abstraction.
///
/// Every platform service implements this contract: it carries a
/// [`ServiceCore`] (identity, owning authority, readiness) and exposes the
/// single invocation boundary ([`Service::invoke`]) through which its owning
/// authority forwards platform requests. **No domain-specific operations
/// live here** — those live on the concrete services.
pub(crate) trait Service {
    /// Returns the common service state.
    fn core(&self) -> &ServiceCore;

    /// Returns the identity of this service.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests inspect service
    /// identity; future service registries and lookups consume it
    /// (TODO(Phase7F.4)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    fn id(&self) -> &ServiceId {
        self.core().id()
    }

    /// Returns the hub whose authority owns this service.
    fn owner(&self) -> HubId {
        self.core().owner()
    }

    /// Returns whether this service is ready to perform domain work.
    fn is_ready(&self) -> bool {
        self.core().is_ready()
    }

    /// The service invocation boundary.
    ///
    /// Called by the owning authority
    /// ([`HubAuthority::invoke`](crate::hub::HubAuthority::invoke)) with the
    /// platform request; returns the [`ServiceResult`] of the execution.
    fn invoke(&self, invocation: &ServiceInvocation) -> HubResult<ServiceResult>;
}

/// The real domain-neutral service operation vocabulary (Phase 7F.3).
///
/// The smallest explicit domain operation payloads the real services
/// require — an explicit enum, never an untyped map. Each service interprets
/// only the operations of its domain; an operation outside the domain is
/// rejected. The vocabulary is domain-neutral (`Open`/`Close`/`Set`/
/// `Record`/`Clear`/`Probe`): the per-domain meaning is decided by the
/// service that owns the operation. Carried by the message payload
/// ([`BackbonePayload::Operation`]); the payload owns its arguments, so the
/// message envelope is no longer `Copy` (see the `backbone` module).
///
/// The lib build constructs `Inspect` and `Accept` (the platform-entry and
/// probe operations) and [`crate::SySS::invoke_service`] accepts any
/// operation; the real operations (`Open`, `Close`, `Set`, `Record`,
/// `Clear`, `Probe`) are constructed by the tests and by the future
/// Frontend-facing interface operations — the allowance is the documented
/// contract-first trade-off, removed as those operations land.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ServiceOperation {
    /// Inspect the service's current domain state; answered with
    /// [`ServiceResult::Inspected`] — the synchronous Response.
    Inspect,
    /// The generic directive of the Phase 7F.2 proof contract: perform the
    /// minimal domain operation. Preserved for back-compatibility with the
    /// proof paths and the readiness probes.
    Accept,
    /// Open/select a domain item by name (workspace, project, package).
    Open(String),
    /// Open a project/package **inside** a parent object (Phase 7H): `name`
    /// is the project/package name and `parent` is the containing
    /// workspace/project. The opened object records the association — the
    /// `Workspace → Project → Package` containment of the SySS storage
    /// model.
    OpenIn { name: String, parent: String },
    /// Close the currently open/selected domain item (workspace, project,
    /// package).
    Close,
    /// Update a controlled setting value (settings domain).
    Set { key: String, value: String },
    /// Retrieve a controlled setting value (settings domain, Phase 7H.2).
    /// Travels as a Request and is answered with
    /// [`ServiceResult::Inspected`] carrying the value — the persisted value
    /// or the deterministic default for a known setting (or `Rejected` when
    /// the key is unknown).
    Get(String),
    /// Record a platform operation entry (history domain; log domain via
    /// the back-compatible message path).
    Record(String),
    /// Record a **structured** log record (log domain, Phase 7H.2): a
    /// severity, the source/domain and the message. Travels as a Command and
    /// is answered with `Completed` (or `Rejected` when the record is
    /// invalid).
    RecordLog {
        /// The severity of the record.
        severity: LogSeverity,
        /// The source/domain that produced the record.
        source: String,
        /// The record message.
        message: String,
    },
    /// Clear the recorded entries (history, log domains) — including their
    /// persisted state.
    Clear,
    /// Perform the domain capability probe (storage, device domains).
    Probe,
    /// Save an artifact into the storage space under the given category and
    /// name (storage domain, Phase 7G.1). Travels as a Request and is
    /// answered with [`ServiceResult::Completed`] (or `Rejected` when the
    /// operation cannot be performed).
    Save {
        /// The storage category the artifact is stored in.
        category: StorageCategory,
        /// The storage entry name.
        name: String,
        /// The existing artifact representation to persist — serialized by
        /// PSS, stored by Syss (the `ra-persistence` artifact model).
        artifact: Artifact,
    },
    /// Load the named storage entry from the given category (storage domain,
    /// Phase 7G.1). Travels as a Request and is answered with
    /// [`ServiceResult::Loaded`] carrying the loaded artifact representation
    /// (or `Rejected` when the operation cannot be performed).
    Load {
        /// The storage category the entry is stored in.
        category: StorageCategory,
        /// The storage entry name.
        name: String,
    },
    /// Run crash recovery over the platform storage root (storage domain,
    /// Phase 7G.1). Travels as a Request and is answered with
    /// [`ServiceResult::Recovered`] carrying the recovery report summary (or
    /// `Rejected` when the operation cannot be performed).
    Recover,
    /// Open a device file as the platform's active document (Phase 7H).
    /// Travels as a Request and is answered with [`ServiceResult::Opened`]
    /// carrying the opened document summary (or `Rejected` when the file
    /// cannot be brought into the platform).
    OpenDocument {
        /// The device file to open.
        source: PathBuf,
    },
    /// Close the platform's active document (Phase 7H). Answered with
    /// `Completed` (or `Rejected` when no document is open).
    CloseDocument,
    /// Save the platform's active document into the files category (Phase
    /// 7H). Answered with `Completed` (or `Rejected` when no document is
    /// open or the write fails).
    SaveDocument,
    /// Save the platform's active document under a new device path (Phase
    /// 7H). Answered with `Completed` (or `Rejected` when no document is
    /// open or the target is invalid).
    SaveDocumentAs {
        /// The destination device file.
        destination: PathBuf,
    },
    /// Import a device file into the platform's files category (Phase 7H),
    /// without opening it. Answered with `Completed` (or `Rejected` when the
    /// source cannot be imported).
    ImportDocument {
        /// The source device file.
        source: PathBuf,
    },
    /// Export the platform's active document to a device file (Phase 7H).
    /// Answered with `Completed` (or `Rejected` when no document is open or
    /// the target is invalid).
    ExportDocument {
        /// The destination device file.
        destination: PathBuf,
    },
    /// Inspect the platform's active document — read its current state
    /// (Phase 7H). Answered with [`ServiceResult::Inspected`] carrying the
    /// document summary (or `Rejected` when no document is open).
    InspectDocument,
    /// Replace the current content of the platform's active document (Phase
    /// 7H). Answered with `Completed` (or `Rejected` when no document is
    /// open).
    SetDocumentContent(String),
}

/// The minimal domain-neutral invocation representation.
///
/// The invocation carries the backbone message the owning authority forwards
/// to the service (Phase 7F.1) and the [`ServiceOperation`] it requests
/// (Phase 7F.2). Deliberately **domain-neutral** — the invocation itself has
/// no workspace, project, compiler or runtime shape; the requested
/// operation (Phase 7F.3 domain operations, Phase 7G.1 storage operations)
/// carries the domain arguments.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct ServiceInvocation<'a> {
    message: &'a BackboneMessage,
}

impl<'a> ServiceInvocation<'a> {
    /// Wraps the backbone message being invoked.
    pub(crate) fn new(message: &'a BackboneMessage) -> ServiceInvocation<'a> {
        ServiceInvocation { message }
    }

    /// Returns the backbone message being invoked.
    pub(crate) fn message(&self) -> &BackboneMessage {
        self.message
    }

    /// Returns the kind of the invoked message.
    pub(crate) fn kind(&self) -> BackboneMessageKind {
        self.message.kind()
    }

    /// Returns the operation this invocation requests.
    ///
    /// Derived from the message payload. A payload-less message falls back to
    /// the natural reading of its kind: a payload-less request is a bare
    /// question (inspect), every other payload-less message is a bare
    /// directive (accept).
    pub(crate) fn operation(&self) -> ServiceOperation {
        match self.message.payload() {
            BackbonePayload::Operation(operation) => operation,
            // A message carrying no service operation — or a Response
            // payload, which is never forwarded to a service — falls back to
            // the natural reading of its kind: a payload-less request is a
            // bare question (inspect), every other payload-less message is a
            // bare directive (accept).
            BackbonePayload::None | BackbonePayload::Response(_) => match self.message.kind() {
                BackboneMessageKind::Request => ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                _ => ServiceOperation::Accept,
            },
        }
    }
}

/// The result of a service execution.
///
/// Distinct from the backbone's
/// [`DeliveryReceipt`](crate::hub::backbone::DeliveryReceipt): the receipt
/// records the message **transport / delivery** result, while a
/// `ServiceResult` records the **domain service execution** result.
///
/// Phases 7F.1–7F.2 carried only the three outcomes; Phase 7F.3 adds
/// [`ServiceResult::Inspected`] — the synchronous **Response** to a
/// `Request` carrying `Inspect`, carrying a deterministic summary of the
/// domain state. The result is not `Copy`: it may own the inspected
/// summary.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ServiceResult {
    /// The service accepted the request; nothing was performed (an
    /// informational notification).
    Accepted,
    /// The service completed the requested operation.
    Completed,
    /// The service rejected the request.
    Rejected,
    /// The answer to a `Request` carrying `Inspect` — the synchronous
    /// Response: a deterministic summary of the service's domain state.
    Inspected(String),
    /// The answer to a storage `Request` carrying `Load` (Phase 7G.1): a
    /// deterministic representation of the loaded artifact. The real
    /// round-trip is proven for the `.ra` text codec; binary formats
    /// (`.rab`/`.raf`/`.rap`) still report `EncodingNotSpecified` at the Pss
    /// codec layer, so a binary load is honestly `Rejected` — rich binary
    /// load results are deferred until the binary encodings are defined.
    Loaded(String),
    /// The answer to a storage `Request` carrying `Recover` (Phase 7G.1): a
    /// deterministic summary of the recovery report.
    Recovered(String),
    /// The answer to a document `Request` carrying `OpenDocument` (Phase
    /// 7H): a deterministic representation of the opened document.
    Opened(String),
}

// ── Domain state (Phase 7H active objects) ────────────────────

/// Derives the validated storage name of a device file from its path.
///
/// The storage name is **always** the bare file name of the device path — a
/// path can never smuggle separators or traversal into the storage space,
/// and the name is validated through the platform's single name-validation
/// rule. Fails with [`crate::Error::InvalidName`] when the path carries no
/// usable file name (e.g. `/` or a non-UTF-8 name).
fn storage_name_from(path: &Path) -> crate::Result<String> {
    let name = path
        .file_name()
        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
        .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error::InvalidName(format!("{path:?} has no usable file name")))?;
    crate::syss::validate_name(name)?;
    Ok(name.to_owned())
}

/// Maps an active-object operation result to the service outcome (Phase 7H).
///
/// `Ok(())` completes; every failure — invalid identity, lifecycle
/// rejection, missing document, persistence failure — is a deterministic
/// service rejection, matching the storage boundary pattern (the underlying
/// [`crate::Error`] detail stays at the active-object layer).
fn active_object_outcome(result: crate::Result<()>) -> ServiceResult {
    match result {
        Ok(()) => ServiceResult::Completed,
        Err(_) => ServiceResult::Rejected,
    }
}

// ── Active-object persistence (Phase 7H.1) ───────────────────
//
// Workspace / project / package domain state is persisted through the
// existing stack: the `.ra` text codec of [`Pss`] serializes a small
// deterministic state text, and [`Syss::save`] writes it atomically into the
// existing storage category (`workspaces/`, `projects/`, `packages/`). The
// state text of an object is the canonical record of what is required to
// reopen it: its kind and name (line 1) and, for projects and packages, the
// parent association (an optional `in: <parent>` line). Missing persisted
// state is the normal "never opened" case and opens fresh; corrupt or
// mismatched state is a deterministic rejection.

/// The persisted state text of a workspace: `workspace: <name>`.
fn workspace_state_text(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("workspace: {name}")
}

/// The persisted state text of a project: `project: <name>` plus an optional
/// `in: <workspace>` line carrying the recorded association.
fn project_state_text(name: &str, workspace: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match workspace {
        Some(workspace) => format!("project: {name}\nin: {workspace}"),
        None => format!("project: {name}"),
    }
}

/// The persisted state text of a package: `package: <name>` plus an optional
/// `in: <project>` line carrying the recorded association.
fn package_state_text(name: &str, project: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match project {
        Some(project) => format!("package: {name}\nin: {project}"),
        None => format!("package: {name}"),
    }
}

/// Serializes persisted object state text through the existing `.ra` text
/// codec and writes it into `category` under `name` through the existing
/// Syss atomic-write path (Phase 7H.1).
fn persist_state(
    pss: &Pss,
    syss: &Syss,
    category: StorageCategory,
    name: &str,
    text: &str,
) -> crate::Result<()> {
    let program = ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new(name, text);
    let bytes = pss.serialize_program(ra_persistence::Format::Ra, &program)?;
    syss.save(category, name, &bytes)
}

/// Loads the persisted state text of the entry `name` in `category` through
/// the existing stack (Syss read + `.ra` codec decode).
///
/// Missing persisted state is `Ok(None)` — an object that was never opened
/// before opens fresh. A read failure or a state that cannot be decoded
/// through the existing codec is a deterministic rejection.
fn load_state_text(
    pss: &Pss,
    syss: &Syss,
    category: StorageCategory,
    name: &str,
) -> crate::Result<Option<String>> {
    let bytes = match syss.load(category, name) {
        Ok(bytes) => bytes,
        Err(crate::Error::NotFound { .. }) => return Ok(None),
        Err(err) => return Err(err),
    };
    let program = pss.deserialize_program(ra_persistence::Format::Ra, &bytes)?;
    Ok(Some(program.text().to_owned()))
}

/// The deterministic corrupt-state error of the persistence layer.
fn corrupt_state(kind: &str, name: &str) -> crate::Error {
    crate::Error::ActiveObject(format!("corrupt persisted {kind} state for {name:?}"))
}

/// Verifies persisted workspace state: exactly the line `workspace: <name>`.
/// Any other content — a different kind, a different name, extra lines — is
/// corrupt state and rejected deterministically.
fn parse_workspace_state(text: &str, name: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
    if text == workspace_state_text(name) {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(corrupt_state("workspace", name))
    }
}

/// Parses persisted project state back into the recorded workspace
/// association (Phase 7H.1): line 1 must be `project: <name>`, and an
/// optional line 2 must be `in: <workspace>` carrying a valid workspace
/// name. Any structural mismatch is corrupt state.
fn parse_project_state(text: &str, name: &str) -> crate::Result<Option<String>> {
    let mut lines = text.lines();
    match (lines.next(), lines.next(), lines.next()) {
        (Some(first), second, None) if first == format!("project: {name}") => match second {
            None => Ok(None),
            Some(parent) => {
                let parent = parent
                    .strip_prefix("in: ")
                    .ok_or_else(|| corrupt_state("project", name))?;
                ActiveObjectId::new(ActiveObjectKind::Workspace, parent)
                    .map_err(|_| corrupt_state("project", name))?;
                Ok(Some(parent.to_owned()))
            }
        },
        _ => Err(corrupt_state("project", name)),
    }
}

/// Parses persisted package state back into the recorded project association
/// (Phase 7H.1): line 1 must be `package: <name>`, and an optional line 2
/// must be `in: <project>` carrying a valid project name. Any structural
/// mismatch is corrupt state.
fn parse_package_state(text: &str, name: &str) -> crate::Result<Option<String>> {
    let mut lines = text.lines();
    match (lines.next(), lines.next(), lines.next()) {
        (Some(first), second, None) if first == format!("package: {name}") => match second {
            None => Ok(None),
            Some(parent) => {
                let parent = parent
                    .strip_prefix("in: ")
                    .ok_or_else(|| corrupt_state("package", name))?;
                ActiveObjectId::new(ActiveObjectKind::Project, parent)
                    .map_err(|_| corrupt_state("package", name))?;
                Ok(Some(parent.to_owned()))
            }
        },
        _ => Err(corrupt_state("package", name)),
    }
}

/// The workspace-domain state (Phase 7H; persisted since 7H.1): the real
/// [`Workspace`] and [`Document`] active objects, plus the storage stack
/// they persist through (the `workspaces/` category for the workspace
/// object, the `files/` category for the document).
///
/// The state is owned privately by the Workspace Service; the objects are
/// only reachable through the single service invocation boundary. The
/// document belongs to the workspace domain — the existing hub set has no
/// Document hub, and the workspace owns the loaded document (the SySS
/// storage vocabulary's "files currently loaded into the IDE").
#[derive(Debug)]
struct WorkspaceState {
    /// The storage space over the platform storage root: the existing Syss
    /// stack, reused for document persistence (no second filesystem
    /// abstraction).
    syss: Syss,
    /// The serialization service: the existing Pss stack, reused to
    /// validate and (de)serialize document content.
    pss: Pss,
    /// The open workspace active object, if any. Absence **is** the Closed
    /// lifecycle state.
    workspace: Option<Workspace>,
    /// The open document active object, if any.
    document: Option<Document>,
}

impl WorkspaceState {
    /// Creates the workspace-domain state over the given storage root.
    fn new(root: PathBuf) -> WorkspaceState {
        WorkspaceState {
            syss: Syss::new(root),
            pss: Pss::new(),
            workspace: None,
            document: None,
        }
    }

    /// Opens the workspace named `name` (Phase 7H; persisted since 7H.1).
    ///
    /// The workspace object is born `Closed` and transitions to `Open`
    /// through the validated lifecycle. Persisted state (if any) is loaded
    /// and verified through the existing stack before the object is opened;
    /// the workspace state is then persisted atomically into the
    /// `workspaces/` category, so reopening after a close restores it. Fails
    /// when a workspace is already open (duplicate-open rejection), the name
