/// Errors reported by the hub graph contracts.
///
/// The hub graph is internal to `ra-syss`; its errors are reported through
/// this type. As the Platform Backbone and Platform Services wire the graph
/// into the platform surface, these errors are converted into [`crate::Error`]
/// (via the `From<HubError>` bridge).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(crate) enum HubError {
    /// A hub with the same identifier is already registered.
    AlreadyRegistered(HubId),
    /// The hub is not registered and cannot be unregistered.
    NotRegistered(HubId),
    /// A route from a hub to itself was requested; a hub never routes to
    /// itself.
    SelfRoute(HubId),
    /// A lifecycle transition was requested from a state that does not allow
    /// it.
    InvalidTransition {
        /// The lifecycle state the hub was in.
        from: HubLifecycle,
        /// The lifecycle state the transition requested.
        to: HubLifecycle,
    },
    /// The platform kernel could not be verified ready.
    KernelNotReady,
    /// A backbone message references a hub that is not registered.
    UnregisteredTarget(HubId),
    /// A backbone message targets a hub that is not active (only active hubs
    /// are routed to).
    InactiveTarget(HubId),
    /// Routing and dispatch require a concrete target hub; broadcasts carry
    /// none.
    TargetRequired,
    /// A broadcast message carried a single target; broadcasts address the
    /// whole platform.
    TargetedBroadcast,
    /// A message kind does not fit the backbone operation it was offered to.
    ///
    /// E.g. a command (always targeted) offered to
    /// [`Backbone::broadcast`](backbone::Backbone::broadcast), or a
    /// non-response offered to [`Backbone::reply`](backbone::Backbone::reply).
    InvalidMessageKind {
        /// The kind of message that was offered.
        kind: backbone::BackboneMessageKind,
        /// The backbone operation the message was offered to.
        operation: &'static str,
    },
    /// The authority owns no ready service to invoke.
    ServiceUnavailable(HubId),
    /// A Response does not answer the Request it was expected to answer: its
    /// correlation identifier does not match (or is missing).
    CorrelationMismatch {
        /// The correlation identifier of the Request the Response should
        /// answer.
        expected: CorrelationId,
        /// The correlation identifier the Response actually carries, if any.
        actual: Option<CorrelationId>,
    },
}

impl fmt::Display for HubError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            HubError::AlreadyRegistered(id) => {
                write!(f, "hub {id} is already registered")
            }
            HubError::NotRegistered(id) => write!(f, "hub {id} is not registered"),
            HubError::SelfRoute(id) => write!(f, "hub {id} cannot route to itself"),
            HubError::InvalidTransition { from, to } => {
                write!(f, "hub cannot transition from {from} to {to}")
            }
            HubError::KernelNotReady => write!(f, "platform kernel is not ready"),
            HubError::UnregisteredTarget(id) => {
                write!(f, "message references unregistered hub {id}")
            }
            HubError::InactiveTarget(id) => {
                write!(f, "hub {id} is not active and cannot be dispatched to")
            }
            HubError::TargetRequired => write!(f, "routing requires a concrete target hub"),
            HubError::TargetedBroadcast => {
                write!(f, "broadcast messages carry no single target")
            }
            HubError::InvalidMessageKind { kind, operation } => {
                write!(f, "a {kind} message cannot be {operation}")
            }
            HubError::ServiceUnavailable(id) => {
                write!(f, "hub {id} has no ready service to invoke")
            }
            HubError::CorrelationMismatch { expected, actual } => match actual {
                Some(actual) => write!(
                    f,
                    "response correlation mismatch: expected request #{expected}, got request #{actual}"
                ),
                None => write!(
                    f,
                    "response correlation mismatch: expected request #{expected}, got none"
                ),
            },
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for HubError {}

/// Convenience alias for [`Result`](std::result::Result) fixed to [`HubError`].
pub(crate) type HubResult<T> = std::result::Result<T, HubError>;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn hub_errors_display() {
        let err = HubError::AlreadyRegistered(HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "hub workspace is already registered");
        let err = HubError::NotRegistered(HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "hub log is not registered");
        let err = HubError::SelfRoute(HubId::DEVICE);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "hub device cannot route to itself");
        let err = HubError::InvalidTransition {
            from: HubLifecycle::Registered,
            to: HubLifecycle::Active,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "hub cannot transition from registered to active"
        );
        let err = HubError::KernelNotReady;
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "platform kernel is not ready");
        let err = HubError::UnregisteredTarget(HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "message references unregistered hub log");
        let err = HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "hub storage is not active and cannot be dispatched to"
        );
        let err = HubError::TargetRequired;
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "routing requires a concrete target hub");
        let err = HubError::TargetedBroadcast;
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "broadcast messages carry no single target");
        let err = HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
            kind: backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            operation: "broadcast",
        };
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "a command message cannot be broadcast");
        let err = HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
            kind: backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            operation: "sent as a reply",
        };
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "a command message cannot be sent as a reply"
        );
        let err = HubError::ServiceUnavailable(HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "hub log has no ready service to invoke");
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let expected = sequence.next();
        let actual = sequence.next();
        let err = HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
            expected,
            actual: Some(actual),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "response correlation mismatch: expected request #1, got request #2"
        );
        let err = HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
            expected,
            actual: None,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "response correlation mismatch: expected request #1, got none"
        );
    }
}

=== SYSS LIB ===
//! `ra-syss`: the SySS layer of the RA Software Platform.
//!
//! Per the frozen architecture, SySS is the backbone and backend of RA
//! Software: all communication between the Frontend and RA Core passes through
//! it, and it owns the platform lifecycle, workspace, active objects, platform
//! state and platform services.
//!
//! This crate hosts the storage-oriented SySS services migrated from
//! `ra-persistence` and the minimal platform-foundation contracts:
//!
//! * **SySS — System Storage Space** ([`Syss`]): the persistent storage
//!   subsystem. It stores workspaces, projects, packages, loaded files,
//!   settings, logs, history and serialized artifacts, and performs all
//!   writes atomically.
//! * **PSS — Program Serialization Service** ([`Pss`]): the service that
//!   serializes and deserializes RA program artifacts by dispatching to the
//!   codec layer owned by `ra-persistence`.
//! * **Recovery** ([`Recovery`]): crash recovery for interrupted SySS writes.
//! * **Platform foundation** ([`SySS`], [`Lifecycle`], [`PlatformState`]):
//!   the minimal, logic-free contract surface the Bootstrap builds on — the
//!   platform skeleton, the lifecycle phases and the platform state holder.
//! * **Storage categories** ([`StorageCategory`]): the storage vocabulary —
//!   workspaces, projects, packages, loaded files, settings, logs, history
//!   and artifacts — owned by SySS since Phase 7C.1.
//! * **Platform Interface** ([`PlatformInterface`]): the single public
//!   platform API — the only surface exposed to the Bootstrap, the Frontend,
//!   the future IDE, Database and CLI. Contracts only; hub graph, message
//!   backbone and layer internals are never exposed.
//! * **Hub Graph contracts** (Phase 7D.1), **hub authorities** (Phase 7D.2),
//!   the **Platform Kernel** (Phase 7D.3) and the **Platform Backbone**
//!   (Phases 7E–7E.1): the internal `hub` module — hub identifiers, hub domains,
//!   the hub lifecycle vocabulary, the hub registry, the hub graph knowledge,
//!   the routing contracts, the concrete per-domain hub authorities, the
//!   kernel initializer that brings them online (create, register,
//!   initialize, activate, verify readiness) and the communication contracts
//!   the backbone consumes. Architectural scaffolding only, kept strictly
//!   behind the platform interface.
//!
//! # Dependency direction
//!
//! `ra-syss` depends on `ra-persistence` (for the artifact model, the codec
//! layer and the error/format vocabulary). `ra-persistence` does **not**
//! depend back on `ra-syss`, so the crate graph stays acyclic.
//!
//! # Transitional status (Phases 7A–7D)
//!
//! TODO(Phase7A): the platform types ([`SySS`], [`Lifecycle`],
//! [`PlatformState`]) are **contracts only** — no platform logic exists.
//!
//! TODO(Phase7C): the [`PlatformInterface`] is the same kind of contract —
//! every operation is a documented no-op. Since Phase 7C.1 the storage
//! services ([`Syss`], [`Pss`], [`Recovery`]) report errors through
//! [`Error`], and the storage vocabulary and storage-oriented error variants
//! are owned here.
//!
//! TODO(Phase7D): the **SySS Hub Graph** phase realizes the contracts: the
//! message backbone / hub graph, active object management, FSS and the
//! device connector. Phase 7D.1 landed the hub graph **contracts**, Phase
//! 7D.2 the concrete **hub authorities**, Phase 7D.3 the **Platform Kernel**
//! initialization and Phase 7D.3.1 the **stabilization** pass (naming,
//! visibility, ownership and documentation freeze) — all in the internal
//! `hub` module (see above). Phase 7E attaches the **Platform Backbone**
//! communication contracts (vocabulary, envelope and interface) as the first
//! consumer of the kernel's registry, graph, routing and authorities. Phase
//! 7E.1 turns the contracts into the **minimum real backbone runtime** —
//! deterministic synchronous delivery, target resolution and delivery
//! receipts, proven through [`PlatformInterface::probe`]. Phase 7F.1 lands
//! the **service architecture** — the common Service abstraction and the
//! single Log proof service owned by the Log Authority, proven through
//! [`PlatformInterface::probe_service`] (`Backbone → Authority → Service →
//! ServiceResult`). Phase 7F.2 lands the **Platform Services** — the seven
//! domain services (workspace, project, package, settings, history,
//! storage, device) bound to their authorities, performing minimal
//! deterministic domain operations and carrying the minimal
//! service-operation payload; the service accessors of
//! [`PlatformInterface`] (workspace, project, package, settings, history,
//! log) are wired through the backbone. Phase 7F.3 turns the services into
//! the first **real domain-state services**: each service owns private
//! domain state, performs real domain operations (`Open`/`Close`, `Set`,
//! `Record`/`Clear`, `Probe`) and answers a `Request` carrying `Inspect`
//! with the synchronous `ServiceResult::Inspected` Response; the service
//! accessors inspect that real state. Phase 7F.4 completes the **Request →
//! Response round-trip**: a Request carries an opaque correlation
//! identifier, the service result is converted into an explicit `Response`
//! message through the `ResponsePayload::from_service_result` boundary and
//! delivered back over the backbone to the caller. Phase 7F.5 completes the
//! **platform lifecycle & safe shutdown**: the platform state moves through
//! the validated `Starting → Running ⇄ Suspended → ShuttingDown → Stopped`
//! chain ([`Lifecycle`], [`PlatformState`]); [`SySS::suspend`]/
//! [`SySS::resume`] pause and restore the platform while preserving domain
//! state, and [`SySS::shutdown`] performs the deterministic teardown
//! ordering (stop new requests → shut down the kernel's authorities →
//! services stop → backbone participation ends → platform state stopped),
//! keeping the single-owner shutdown semantics through the Bootstrap chain.
//! Phase 7G: the **storage boundary audit & foundation** — the Storage
//! Service's domain state represents the existing storage architecture (the
//! [`Syss`] storage space, [`Pss`] serialization and [`Recovery`] crash
//! recovery over the [`StorageCategory`] vocabulary, built on the
//! `ra-persistence` codec layer), and the storage Request → Response
//! round-trip, correlation, error boundary and lifecycle gates are proven;
//! FSS is not a separate component — `Syss` is the file/storage-system
//! boundary. Phase 7G.1: **storage root + save/load/recovery integration**
//! — [`SySS::initialize`] resolves and establishes the platform storage
//! root (validate, create root + categories, startup crash recovery, fail
//! the boot on error), owns the [`Syss`] handle, and threads the root down
//! the storage boundary; the Storage Service performs the real `Save` /
//! `Load` / `Recover` operations through the existing `Syss`/`Pss`/
//! `Recovery` stack, answered as correlated Responses. Phase 7H: **active
//! objects** — the first genuine application-level objects of the platform
//! (the `hub::active_object` module): real [`Workspace`](crate::hub::Workspace),
//! [`Project`](crate::hub::Project), [`Package`](crate::hub::Package) and
//! [`Document`](crate::hub::Document) runtime objects with stable
//! strongly-typed identities ([`crate::hub::ActiveObjectId`], validated by
//! the platform's single name rule) and the validated `Closed ⇄ Open`
//! lifecycle. The workspace service owns the workspace and the platform's
//! active document; the project/package services own their objects (with
//! the `Workspace → Project → Package` association recorded at open time).
//! The document operations of [`PlatformInterface`] — `open`, `close`,
//! `save`, `save_as`, `import`, `export` — are real: they ride the
//! Request → Response path through the Platform Backbone to the Workspace
//! Authority and its service, which persists through the existing
//! Syss/PSS stack. Phase 7H.1: **workspace/project/package persistence** —
//! the workspace, project and package active objects persist through the
//! same existing stack: their state (identity + the recorded parent
//! association) is serialized with the `.ra` text codec and written
//! atomically by Syss into the existing `workspaces/`, `projects/` and
//! `packages/` categories when the object is opened; reopening restores the
//! state and association, closing and shutdown never delete it, and corrupt
//! or conflicting state is rejected deterministically. Phase 7H.2:
//! **settings/history/log persistence + theme/view foundation** — the
//! Settings, History and Log services become real persisted platform-state
//! domains through the same existing stack (settings as one file per key in
//! `settings/`, history as `history/history`, the smallest real structured
//! platform log as `logs/log`), with lazy loading so corrupt state never
//! fails the boot; [`PlatformInterface::theme`] and
//! [`PlatformInterface::view`] become real settings-backed platform-state
//! operations (deterministic defaults, validated values, persistence;
//! `set_theme`/`get_theme`/`set_view`/`get_view` added additively). Theme
//! and view are application state — no rendering; the Frontend consumes
//! them later. Still missing: the device connector and the RA Core Gateway.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_syss::{Syss, StorageCategory};
//! use std::path::Path;
//!
//! let syss = Syss::new("storage");
//! assert_eq!(syss.root(), Path::new("storage"));
//! assert_eq!(StorageCategory::Artifact.dir_name(), "artifacts");
//! ```
//!
//! # Platform example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_syss::{Lifecycle, PlatformState, SySS};
//!
//! let platform = SySS::initialize().unwrap();
//! let state = PlatformState::new();
//! assert_eq!(state.lifecycle(), Lifecycle::Starting);
//! platform.shutdown().unwrap();
//! ```
//!
//! # Platform Interface example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_syss::PlatformInterface;
//!
//! let platform = PlatformInterface::start().unwrap();
//! platform.shutdown().unwrap();
//! ```

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![deny(missing_docs)]

mod hub;
mod platform;
mod platform_interface;
mod pss;
mod recovery;
mod storage;
mod syss;

pub use platform::{Lifecycle, PlatformState, SySS};
pub use platform_interface::PlatformInterface;
pub use pss::{MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES, Pss};
pub use recovery::{Recovery, RecoveryReport};
pub use storage::StorageCategory;
pub use syss::Syss;

use std::fmt;

/// Convenience alias for [`Result`](std::result::Result) fixed to [`Error`].
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;

/// The error type reported by the SySS platform layer.
///
/// The platform surface reports its own errors and converts errors from the
/// layers it builds on — `ra-persistence` — into this type, so callers
/// handle a single error type. The storage-oriented variants
/// ([`Error::InvalidName`], [`Error::NotFound`], [`Error::AlreadyExists`])
/// are owned here since Phase 7C.1: the storage services ([`Syss`], [`Pss`],
/// [`Recovery`]) report through this type and no longer surface
/// `ra_persistence::Result`.
///
/// The [`PlatformInterface`] operations report through this type: the kernel
/// and backbone failures through [`Error::Kernel`], and the active-object
/// conditions of Phase 7H (duplicate open, close-without-open, missing
/// document, invalid target, persistence failure) through
/// [`Error::ActiveObject`].
#[derive(Debug)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Error {
    /// An error propagated from the `ra-persistence` layer (codec layer,
    /// artifact model).
    Persistence(ra_persistence::Error),
    /// An underlying host I/O failure.
    Io(std::io::Error),
    /// A storage name failed SySS validation.
    InvalidName(String),
    /// A storage entry was not found in the given category.
    NotFound {
        /// The category that was searched.
        category: StorageCategory,
        /// The requested entry name.
        name: String,
    },
    /// A storage entry already exists where one was not expected.
    AlreadyExists {
        /// The category that was searched.
        category: StorageCategory,
        /// The existing entry name.
        name: String,
    },
    /// The platform kernel failed to initialize or verify readiness.
    ///
    /// Opaque: the kernel internals are never exposed outside `ra-syss`; the
    /// caller only receives a description of the failure.
    Kernel(String),
    /// An active-object operation was rejected (Phase 7H).
    ///
    /// Expresses conditions no storage or kernel error can: e.g. opening an
    /// already-open object, closing an object that is not open, or a
    /// document operation offered while no document is open. The detail stays
    /// opaque and deterministic.
    ActiveObject(String),
}

impl fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Error::Persistence(err) => write!(f, "persistence error: {err}"),
            Error::Io(err) => write!(f, "io error: {err}"),
            Error::InvalidName(name) => write!(f, "invalid storage name: {name:?}"),
            Error::NotFound { category, name } => {
                write!(f, "no {category} entry named {name:?}")
            }
            Error::AlreadyExists { category, name } => {
                write!(f, "{category} entry {name:?} already exists")
            }
            Error::Kernel(message) => write!(f, "platform kernel: {message}"),
            Error::ActiveObject(message) => write!(f, "active object: {message}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for Error {}

impl From<ra_persistence::Error> for Error {
    fn from(err: ra_persistence::Error) -> Error {
        Error::Persistence(err)
    }
}

impl From<std::io::Error> for Error {
    fn from(err: std::io::Error) -> Error {
        Error::Io(err)
    }
}

impl From<crate::hub::HubError> for Error {
    fn from(err: crate::hub::HubError) -> Error {
        Error::Kernel(err.to_string())
    }
}

/// Returns the current Unix time in milliseconds.
///
/// Test-only helper shared by the module-level unit tests; mirrors the
/// `ra-persistence` implementation.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn unix_millis() -> u64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// Test helpers shared by the module-level unit tests.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod test_support {
    use std::fs;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

    /// A process-wide counter that makes every temporary directory unique.
    ///
    /// Without it, tests running in parallel in the same process could
    /// collide on a directory name when they start within the same
    /// millisecond, causing one test's cleanup to delete another test's data.
    static NEXT_TEMP_DIR: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

    /// An automatically cleaned-up temporary directory for tests.
    pub(crate) struct TempDir(PathBuf);

    impl TempDir {
        /// Creates a fresh, unique temporary directory.
        pub(crate) fn new(tag: &str) -> TempDir {
            let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
                "ra-syss-{tag}-{}-{}-{}",
                std::process::id(),
                crate::unix_millis(),
                NEXT_TEMP_DIR.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
            ));
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&path);
            fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("failed to create test temp dir");
            TempDir(path)
        }

        /// Returns the root path of this temporary directory.
        pub(crate) fn path(&self) -> &Path {
            &self.0
        }
    }

    impl Drop for TempDir {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn persistence_errors_convert() {
        let err: Error = ra_persistence::Error::InvalidData("x".into()).into();
        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Persistence(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn io_errors_convert() {
        let err: Error = std::io::Error::other("boom").into();
        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn platform_errors_display() {
        let err = Error::Io(std::io::Error::other("boom"));
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("io error"));
        let err = Error::Persistence(ra_persistence::Error::InvalidData("x".into()));
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("persistence error"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hub_errors_convert_to_kernel_errors() {
        let err: Error = crate::hub::HubError::KernelNotReady.into();
        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Kernel(_)));
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("platform kernel"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_errors_are_owned_by_syss() {
        let err = Error::NotFound {
            category: StorageCategory::Artifact,
            name: "main.rab".to_owned(),
        };
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("no artifacts entry named"));

        let err = Error::AlreadyExists {
            category: StorageCategory::Settings,
            name: "theme".to_owned(),
        };
        assert!(
            err.to_string()
                .contains("settings entry \"theme\" already exists")
        );

        let err = Error::InvalidName("a/b".to_owned());
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("invalid storage name"));
    }
}

=== RA-MEMORY SOURCE INVENTORY ===

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\active_space.rs
//! Active Space (AS) — the execution-tracking grid of active records.
//!
//! Per the Active Space V1 architecture document, *"Active Space (AS) is
//! RA's temporary execution-tracking memory. It remembers the currently
//! active execution path while an RA program runs."* It answers the
//! execution questions: *which function/scope is currently executing, at
//! which REI position, and which previous context becomes active when the
//! current function closes.*
//!
//! Active Space **owns execution identity**: the live call chain — which
//! scope is current, at which REI position, and what resumes when it closes.
//! It owns no values (those belong to Entity Space) and no executable
//! structure (that belongs to Program Space); REI *execution* belongs to the
//! Runtime, not to this crate.
//!
//! # Grid and blocks
//!
//! Active Space uses the frozen **Grid/Block Method** (§4–§5): each logical
//! grid cell holds one compact **Active Record** (§3) — a
//! [`ScopeId`] (Function/Scope ID) plus an REI execution position. The
//! active grid is bounded per block:
//!
//! * minimum/default grid **3×3 = 9 cells**, maximum **8×8 = 64 cells**;
//! * the grid may scale between those limits as demand grows
//!   (`3×3 → 4×4 → … → 8×8`);
//! * when an 8×8 block is full, Active Space creates **another grid block**
//!   rather than enlarging or relocating the existing one.
//!
//! # Call / return
//!
//! Ordinary synchronous calls follow **logical sequential ordering** (§6):
//! a new call occupies the next logical cell, and when the current function
//! closes, its end cell is released and the previous live cell becomes
//! current. No return pointer is stored per record. Released end/top cells
//! become **reusable immediately** and holes are never reused in the middle
//! of a live chain (§7) — so the live chain is always a prefix of cells and
//! [`ActiveSpace::depth`] is the chain length.
//!
//! # Active Cell ID and scope encoding
//!
//! [`ActiveSpace::call`] returns the **Active Cell ID** of the new record;
//! per §9 the currently active cell id may participate in identifying local
//! invocations (e.g. a `(cell, entity)` local-lookup key) without placing
//! values inside Active Space. The REI **local/global scope state** (0 =
//! local, 1 = global, §8) is an REI-level encoding and is **not** part of
//! Active Records, which hold the compiler-assigned Function/Scope ID only.
//!
//! # Mini-Log
//!
//! Active Space includes the optional fixed-size circular **Mini-Log** (§11)
//! for fast debugging/error tracing: it records only execution transitions
//! (CALL / RETURN / error events), uses a fixed capacity, and overwrites the
//! oldest entry when full. It is not used by normal call/return execution.
//!
//! # No knowledge of Entity Space Value Lists
//!
//! Active Space tracks execution only: active records hold the scope id and
//! REI position, never values, Value List handles or bindings. Active Space
//! has **no knowledge of Entity Space Value Lists**.
//!
//! # Client of the Memory Manager
//!
//! Active Space is a **client of the frozen [`MemoryManager`]**: it
//! registers [`SpaceKind::Active`], and **all** storage — grid blocks, the
//! block directory, and the Mini-Log — lives in manager allocations
//! referenced by [`LogicalAddress`]. Active Space never allocates host
//! memory for storage and never exposes host pointers. It does not own the
//! manager (operations take `&mut MemoryManager`) and does not depend on
//! Program Space, which the architecture permits it to read from but does
//! not require for call/return tracking.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_memory::{ActiveSpace, ScopeId};
//!
//! let mut memory = ra_memory::MemoryManager::new();
//! let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
//!
//! let main = ScopeId::from_u32(1);
//! let calc = ScopeId::from_u32(2);
//! active.call(&mut memory, main, 0).unwrap();
//! active.call(&mut memory, calc, 16).unwrap();
//!
//! assert_eq!(active.current(&memory).unwrap().unwrap().scope_id(), calc);
//!
//! active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(active.current(&memory).unwrap().unwrap().scope_id(), main);
//!
//! active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
//! ```

use std::fmt;

use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::codec::{get_u32, put_u32};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::manager::MemoryManager;
use crate::space::{SpaceId, SpaceKind};

/// Minimum (and default) logical grid side per block: 3×3 = 9 cells.
const MIN_GRID_SIDE: u32 = 3;
/// Maximum logical grid side per block: 8×8 = 64 cells.
const MAX_GRID_SIDE: u32 = 8;
/// Maximum cells per grid block (8×8).
const MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK: u32 = MAX_GRID_SIDE * MAX_GRID_SIDE;
/// Byte size of one active record (scope id + REI position).
const ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE: usize = 8;
/// Byte size of one block record in the block directory.
const BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE: usize = 20;
/// Initial block-directory capacity, in block records.
const INITIAL_DIRECTORY_CAPACITY: usize = 2;
/// Fixed Mini-Log capacity, in entries (§11 — capacity is implementation
/// defined, as is the event encoding).
const MINI_LOG_CAPACITY: u32 = 32;
/// Byte size of one Mini-Log entry (kind + cell + scope).
const MINI_LOG_ENTRY_SIZE: usize = 12;
/// Sentinel value meaning "no cell / no scope" in a Mini-Log entry.
const NONE_ID: u32 = u32::MAX;
/// Block-record field offsets (little-endian). The block storage address
/// occupies three consecutive `u32`s from `BLOCK_ADDRESS_REGION`.
const BLOCK_ADDRESS_REGION: usize = 0;
const BLOCK_SIDE: usize = 12;
const BLOCK_BASE: usize = 16;
/// Mini-Log entry field offsets (little-endian).
const LOG_KIND: usize = 0;
const LOG_CELL: usize = 4;
const LOG_SCOPE: usize = 8;

/// A compact function/scope identifier carried by Active Records.
///
/// Assigned by the compiler; opaque to Active Space. The exact width of a
/// Function/Scope ID is left open by the architecture (§13), so this wraps a
/// `u32`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct ScopeId(u32);

impl ScopeId {
    /// Returns the raw identifier value.
    pub fn as_u32(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Creates an identifier from a raw value.
    pub fn from_u32(value: u32) -> ScopeId {
        ScopeId(value)
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for ScopeId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let id = self.0;
        write!(f, "scope#{id}")
    }
}

/// A logical grid-cell identifier inside Active Space.
///
/// The currently active cell id can participate in identifying a local
/// invocation together with an Entity Space id (§9) — e.g. a `(cell, entity)`
/// local-lookup key. Cells are never moved by grid growth, so a cell id is
/// stable for the lifetime of the Active Space.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct CellId(u32);

impl CellId {
    /// Returns the raw identifier value.
    pub fn as_u32(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Creates an identifier from a raw value.
    pub fn from_u32(value: u32) -> CellId {
        CellId(value)
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for CellId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let id = self.0;
        write!(f, "cell#{id}")
    }
}

/// One compact Active Record: the content of a single live grid cell.
///
/// Per §3 an Active Record is the **Function/Scope ID + REI Execution
/// Position** of the currently executing scope. It deliberately does **not**
/// store local values — runtime values belong to Entity Space and temporary
/// calculations to Work Space.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ActiveRecord {
    scope_id: ScopeId,
    rei_position: u32,
}

impl ActiveRecord {
    /// Creates an active record for `scope_id` at the given REI position.
    pub fn new(scope_id: ScopeId, rei_position: u32) -> ActiveRecord {
        ActiveRecord {
            scope_id,
            rei_position,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the function/scope identifier of the executing scope.
    pub fn scope_id(self) -> ScopeId {
        self.scope_id
    }

    /// Returns the REI execution position within the scope.
    pub fn rei_position(self) -> u32 {
        self.rei_position
    }
}

/// The kind of a Mini-Log execution-transition event (§11).
///
/// Active Space records CALL events when a scope is entered (the
/// ENTER/CALL transitions of §11), RETURN events when a scope closes, and
/// ERROR events for error-relevant transitions reported via
/// [`ActiveSpace::record_error`]. The exact event set and encoding are open
/// in the architecture (§13).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MiniLogEventKind {
    /// A new scope was entered (the ENTER/CALL transition).
    Call = 0,
    /// The current scope closed.
    Return = 1,
    /// An error-relevant execution event was reported.
    Error = 2,
}

/// One Mini-Log entry: a transition kind plus the cell and scope involved.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MiniLogEvent {
    kind: MiniLogEventKind,
    cell: Option<CellId>,
    scope: Option<ScopeId>,
}

impl MiniLogEvent {
    /// Creates a Mini-Log entry.
    fn new(kind: MiniLogEventKind, cell: Option<CellId>, scope: Option<ScopeId>) -> MiniLogEvent {
        MiniLogEvent { kind, cell, scope }
    }

    /// Returns the transition kind of this entry.
    pub fn kind(self) -> MiniLogEventKind {
        self.kind
    }

    /// Returns the grid cell involved, when one applied.
    pub fn cell(self) -> Option<CellId> {
        self.cell
    }

    /// Returns the scope involved, when one applied.
    pub fn scope(self) -> Option<ScopeId> {
        self.scope
    }
}

/// The logical metadata of one grid block (a private directory record).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct BlockMeta {
    /// Logical address of the block's cell storage.
    address: LogicalAddress,
    /// Current logical grid side (`3..=8`).
    side: u32,
    /// The base (first) cell index of this block.
    base: u32,
}

impl BlockMeta {
    /// The number of logical cells currently in this block (`side²`).
    fn capacity(self) -> u32 {
        self.side * self.side
    }
}

/// The block directory: a fixed-slot array of [`BlockMeta`] records held in
/// one manager allocation (the private analogue of the module table).
#[derive(Debug)]
struct BlockDirectory {
    /// The space that owns the directory storage.
    space_id: SpaceId,
    /// The logical address of the directory storage.
    address: LogicalAddress,
    /// The number of block-record slots.
    capacity: usize,
    /// The number of blocks currently registered.
    count: usize,
}

impl BlockDirectory {
    /// Allocates the directory storage for `space_id`.
    fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager, space_id: SpaceId) -> Result<BlockDirectory> {
        let capacity = INITIAL_DIRECTORY_CAPACITY;
        let bytes = capacity * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE;
        let address = memory.allocate(space_id, bytes)?;
        Ok(BlockDirectory {
            space_id,
            address,
            capacity,
            count: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Returns the number of registered blocks.
    fn count(&self) -> usize {
        self.count
    }

    /// Decodes the block record at `index`.
    fn read_meta(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, index: usize) -> Result<BlockMeta> {
        Ok(decode_block_meta(self.read_bytes(memory, index)?))
    }

    /// Encodes and writes the block record at `index`.
    fn write_meta(&self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, index: usize, meta: BlockMeta) -> Result<()> {
        memory.write(
            self.address,
            index * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE,
            &encode_block_meta(meta),
        )
    }

    /// Appends a block record, growing the directory when it is full.
    fn append(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, meta: BlockMeta) -> Result<()> {
        if self.count == self.capacity {
            self.grow(memory)?;
        }
        self.write_meta(memory, self.count, meta)?;
        self.count += 1;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Doubles the directory, copying the block records.
    ///
    /// Only directory metadata moves; the block storage allocations (and the
    /// live Active Records inside them) never move.
    fn grow(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let new_capacity = self.capacity * 2;
        let new_bytes = new_capacity * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE;
        let new_address = memory.allocate(self.space_id, new_bytes)?;
        for index in 0..self.count {
            let bytes = self.read_bytes(memory, index)?;
            memory.write(new_address, index * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE, &bytes)?;
        }
        memory.deallocate(self.address)?;
        self.address = new_address;
        self.capacity = new_capacity;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Deallocates the directory storage.
    fn reclaim(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        memory.deallocate(self.address)
    }

    /// Reads one raw block record.
    fn read_bytes(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, index: usize) -> Result<[u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE]> {
        let mut buf = [0u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE];
        memory.read(self.address, index * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(buf)
    }
}

/// The optional circular Mini-Log (§11): a fixed-capacity transition log in
/// one manager allocation. When full, the oldest entry is overwritten.
#[derive(Debug)]
struct MiniLog {
    /// The logical address of the log storage.
    address: LogicalAddress,
    /// The index of the next entry to write.
    next: u32,
    /// The number of entries currently held (saturates at capacity).
    count: u32,
}

impl MiniLog {
    /// Allocates the log storage for `space_id`.
    fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager, space_id: SpaceId) -> Result<MiniLog> {
        let bytes = MINI_LOG_CAPACITY as usize * MINI_LOG_ENTRY_SIZE;
        let address = memory.allocate(space_id, bytes)?;
        Ok(MiniLog {
            address,
            next: 0,
            count: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Appends an entry, overwriting the oldest when full.
    fn push(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, event: MiniLogEvent) -> Result<()> {
        let mut bytes = [0u8; MINI_LOG_ENTRY_SIZE];
        put_u32(&mut bytes, LOG_KIND, event.kind as u32);
        put_u32(
            &mut bytes,
            LOG_CELL,
            event.cell.map_or(NONE_ID, CellId::as_u32),
        );
        put_u32(
            &mut bytes,
            LOG_SCOPE,
            event.scope.map_or(NONE_ID, ScopeId::as_u32),
        );
        memory.write(
            self.address,
            self.next as usize * MINI_LOG_ENTRY_SIZE,
            &bytes,
        )?;
        self.next = (self.next + 1) % MINI_LOG_CAPACITY;
        if self.count < MINI_LOG_CAPACITY {
            self.count += 1;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Deallocates the log storage.
    fn reclaim(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        memory.deallocate(self.address)
    }
}

/// Active Space (AS) — the execution-tracking grid of active records.
///
/// A client of the [`MemoryManager`]: it registers [`SpaceKind::Active`]
/// and obtains **all** of its storage through manager allocations (grid
/// blocks, the block directory and the Mini-Log). It never allocates host
/// memory for storage and never exposes host pointers.
///
/// The live call chain is a prefix of the logical cells: [`ActiveSpace::call`]
/// appends the next record, [`ActiveSpace::close`] releases the end cell and
/// makes the previous cell current, and released end cells are reused by the
/// next call. Grid blocks scale from 3×3 to 8×8 on demand; a full 8×8 block
/// causes a new block to be created.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ActiveSpace {
    space_id: SpaceId,
    directory: BlockDirectory,
    mini_log: MiniLog,
    depth: u32,
}

impl ActiveSpace {
    /// Creates an Active Space within `memory`.
    ///
    /// Registers [`SpaceKind::Active`] and allocates the first grid block
    /// (default 3×3 logical grid), the block directory and the Mini-Log from
    /// the manager. The space begins with zero live records.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when any of the initial storage cannot be allocated.
    pub fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<ActiveSpace> {
        let space_id = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Active);
        let mut directory = BlockDirectory::new(memory, space_id)?;
        let block = memory.allocate(space_id, MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK as usize * ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE)?;
        directory.append(
            memory,
            BlockMeta {
                address: block,
                side: MIN_GRID_SIDE,
                base: 0,
            },
        )?;
        let mini_log = MiniLog::new(memory, space_id)?;
        Ok(ActiveSpace {
            space_id,
            directory,
            mini_log,
            depth: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Returns the [`SpaceId`] this Active Space registered with the
    /// manager.
    pub fn space_id(&self) -> SpaceId {
        self.space_id
    }

    /// Returns the number of live active records (the call-chain length).
    pub fn depth(&self) -> usize {
        self.depth as usize
    }

    /// Returns the number of grid blocks currently in the active grid.
    pub fn blocks(&self) -> usize {
        self.directory.count()
    }

    /// Returns the total number of logical cells currently available across
    /// all blocks.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when the block directory cannot be read.
    pub fn capacity(&self, memory: &MemoryManager) -> Result<usize> {
        let last = self
            .directory
            .read_meta(memory, self.directory.count() - 1)?;
        Ok((last.base + last.capacity()) as usize)
    }

    /// Returns the cell id of the current (latest live) record, or `None`
    /// when the chain is empty.
    ///
    /// The active cell id can participate in identifying local invocations
    /// together with an Entity Space id (§9).
    pub fn current_cell(&self) -> Option<CellId> {
        (self.depth > 0).then(|| CellId::from_u32(self.depth - 1))
    }

    /// Returns the current (latest live) active record, or `None` when the
    /// chain is empty.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when the current record cannot be read.
    pub fn current(&self, memory: &MemoryManager) -> Result<Option<ActiveRecord>> {
        match self.current_cell() {
            Some(cell) => Ok(Some(self.active_record(memory, cell)?)),
            None => Ok(None),
        }
    }

    /// Returns the active record at `cell`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::CellNotActive`] when `cell` is not currently live (it is
    ///   beyond the live chain).
    /// * Manager errors when the record cannot be read.
    pub fn active_record(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, cell: CellId) -> Result<ActiveRecord> {
        if cell.as_u32() >= self.depth {
            return Err(Error::CellNotActive {
                cell,
                depth: self.depth as usize,
            });
        }
        let (block, slot) = self.locate(memory, cell.as_u32())?;
        let mut buf = [0u8; ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE];
        memory.read(block.address, slot * ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(decode_active_record(buf))
    }

    /// Returns an iterator over the live active records in chain order, from
    /// the first call to the current one.
    ///
    /// Construction cannot fail; the `Result` mirrors the crate's other
    /// iterator constructors and reserves room for future validation.
    pub fn active_path<'a>(&self, memory: &'a MemoryManager) -> Result<ActivePathIter<'a>> {
        Ok(ActivePathIter::new(
            memory,
            self.directory.address,
            self.directory.count(),
            self.depth,
        ))
    }

    /// Enters a new scope: appends an active record for `scope_id` at the
    /// next logical cell and returns that cell's id.
    ///
    /// The grid block scales (3×3 → … → 8×8) when the next cell exceeds the
    /// current logical grid, and a new block is created when an 8×8 block is
    /// full. The chain grows without moving existing live records, and a
    /// released end cell is reused by the next call.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns manager errors when storage cannot be grown or written.
    pub fn call(
        &mut self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        scope_id: ScopeId,
        rei_position: u32,
    ) -> Result<CellId> {
        self.ensure_cell(memory, self.depth)?;
        let cell = CellId::from_u32(self.depth);
        let (block, slot) = self.locate(memory, cell.as_u32())?;
        memory.write(
            block.address,
            slot * ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE,
            &encode_active_record(scope_id, rei_position),
        )?;
        self.depth += 1;
        self.mini_log.push(
            memory,
            MiniLogEvent::new(MiniLogEventKind::Call, Some(cell), Some(scope_id)),
        )?;
        Ok(cell)
    }

    /// Closes the current scope (function return): releases the end cell and
    /// makes the previous live cell current.
    ///
    /// The released end cell is reusable immediately by the next call. A
    /// RETURN event is recorded in the Mini-Log.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::EmptyActiveSpace`] when the chain is already empty.
    /// * Manager errors when the log cannot be written.
    pub fn close(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        if self.depth == 0 {
            return Err(Error::EmptyActiveSpace);
        }
        let cell = CellId::from_u32(self.depth - 1);
        let record = self.active_record(memory, cell)?;
        self.depth -= 1;
        self.mini_log.push(
            memory,
            MiniLogEvent::new(
                MiniLogEventKind::Return,
                Some(cell),
                Some(record.scope_id()),
            ),
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Records an error-relevant transition in the Mini-Log (§11).
    ///
    /// The entry is tagged with the current cell and scope when the chain is
    /// non-empty, and with none otherwise.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns manager errors when the log cannot be written.
    pub fn record_error(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let current = self.current(memory)?;
        let cell = self.current_cell();
        let scope = current.map(ActiveRecord::scope_id);
        self.mini_log.push(
            memory,
            MiniLogEvent::new(MiniLogEventKind::Error, cell, scope),
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Returns an iterator over the Mini-Log entries, oldest first.
    ///
    /// Entries are decoded on demand from Active Space storage. Iteration
    /// stops after the first read failure, which is reported as the final
    /// item. Construction cannot fail; the `Result` mirrors the crate's
    /// other iterator constructors.
    pub fn mini_log<'a>(&self, memory: &'a MemoryManager) -> Result<MiniLogIter<'a>> {
        Ok(MiniLogIter::new(
            memory,
            self.mini_log.address,
            self.mini_log.next,
            self.mini_log.count,
        ))
    }

    /// Destroys Active Space, reclaiming every grid block, the block
    /// directory and the Mini-Log, and unregisters the space.
    ///
    /// After this, the [`SpaceId`] is no longer registered. Dropping an
    /// [`ActiveSpace`] without calling this leaks its allocations until the
    /// owning manager is shut down.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when storage cannot be reclaimed or the space cannot
    /// be unregistered.
    pub fn destroy(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let ActiveSpace {
            space_id,
            directory,
            mini_log,
            ..
        } = self;
        for index in 0..directory.count() {
            let meta = directory.read_meta(memory, index)?;
            memory.deallocate(meta.address)?;
        }
        directory.reclaim(memory)?;
        mini_log.reclaim(memory)?;
        memory.unregister_space(space_id)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    // ---- internals ----

    /// Ensures a grid cell exists for the next write: grows the last block's
    /// logical grid (`3×3 → … → 8×8`) or, when an 8×8 block is full, appends
    /// a new block starting at 3×3.
    fn ensure_cell(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, cell: u32) -> Result<()> {
        loop {
            let index = self.directory.count() - 1;
            let meta = self.directory.read_meta(memory, index)?;
            if cell < meta.base + meta.capacity() {
                return Ok(());
            }
            if meta.side < MAX_GRID_SIDE {
                let grown = BlockMeta {
                    side: meta.side + 1,
                    ..meta
                };
                self.directory.write_meta(memory, index, grown)?;
                continue;
            }
            let block = memory.allocate(
                self.space_id,
                MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK as usize * ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE,
            )?;
            let next = BlockMeta {
                address: block,
                side: MIN_GRID_SIDE,
                base: meta.base + MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK,
            };
            self.directory.append(memory, next)?;
        }
    }

    /// Resolves a cell index to its block and in-block slot.
    fn locate(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, cell: u32) -> Result<(BlockMeta, usize)> {
        for index in 0..self.directory.count() {
            let meta = self.directory.read_meta(memory, index)?;
            if cell < meta.base + meta.capacity() {
                return Ok((meta, (cell - meta.base) as usize));
            }
        }
        Err(Error::InvalidData(
            "active cell lies outside all grid blocks".into(),
        ))
    }
}

/// An iterator over the live active records of one chain, decoded on demand.
///
/// Yields records in chain order (cell 0 to the current cell). Iteration
/// stops after the first read failure, which is reported as the final item.
pub struct ActivePathIter<'a> {
    memory: &'a MemoryManager,
    directory: LogicalAddress,
    block_count: usize,
    depth: u32,
    block: usize,
    cell_in_block: u32,
    meta: Option<BlockMeta>,
}

impl fmt::Debug for ActivePathIter<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("ActivePathIter")
            .field("directory", &self.directory)
            .field("block_count", &self.block_count)
            .field("depth", &self.depth)
            .field("block", &self.block)
            .field("cell_in_block", &self.cell_in_block)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl<'a> ActivePathIter<'a> {
    /// Creates a chain iterator over the live records of `depth` cells.
    fn new(
        memory: &'a MemoryManager,
        directory: LogicalAddress,
        block_count: usize,
        depth: u32,
    ) -> ActivePathIter<'a> {
        ActivePathIter {
            memory,
            directory,
            block_count,
            depth,
            block: 0,
            cell_in_block: 0,
            meta: None,
        }
    }

    /// Decodes the block record at `index`.
    fn read_meta(&self, index: usize) -> Result<BlockMeta> {
        let mut buf = [0u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE];
        self.memory
            .read(self.directory, index * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(decode_block_meta(buf))
    }
}

impl Iterator for ActivePathIter<'_> {
    type Item = Result<ActiveRecord>;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
        loop {
            let meta = match self.meta {
                Some(meta) => meta,
                None => {
                    if self.block >= self.block_count {
                        return None;
                    }
                    self.meta = Some(match self.read_meta(self.block) {
                        Ok(meta) => meta,
                        Err(error) => {
                            self.block = self.block_count;
                            return Some(Err(error));
                        }
                    });
                    self.cell_in_block = 0;
                    continue;
                }
            };
            // Live cells of this block are [base, min(base + capacity, depth)).
            let live_end = (meta.base + meta.capacity()).min(self.depth);
            let live_in_block = live_end.saturating_sub(meta.base);
            if self.cell_in_block >= live_in_block {
                self.meta = None;
                self.block += 1;
                continue;
            }
            let mut buf = [0u8; ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE];
            match self.memory.read(
                meta.address,
                self.cell_in_block as usize * ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE,
                &mut buf,
            ) {
                Ok(()) => {
                    self.cell_in_block += 1;
                    return Some(Ok(decode_active_record(buf)));
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    self.block = self.block_count;
                    return Some(Err(error));
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// An iterator over the Mini-Log entries of an Active Space, oldest first.
///
/// Entries are decoded on demand from Active Space storage. Iteration stops
/// after the first read failure, which is reported as the final item.
pub struct MiniLogIter<'a> {
    memory: &'a MemoryManager,
    address: LogicalAddress,
    next: u32,
    count: u32,
    position: u32,
}

impl fmt::Debug for MiniLogIter<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("MiniLogIter")
            .field("address", &self.address)
            .field("next", &self.next)
            .field("count", &self.count)
            .field("position", &self.position)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl<'a> MiniLogIter<'a> {
    /// Creates a log iterator over the `count` entries at `address`, where
    /// `next` is the next write index.
    fn new(
        memory: &'a MemoryManager,
        address: LogicalAddress,
        next: u32,
        count: u32,
    ) -> MiniLogIter<'a> {
        MiniLogIter {
            memory,
            address,
            next,
            count,
            position: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl Iterator for MiniLogIter<'_> {
    type Item = Result<MiniLogEvent>;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
        if self.position >= self.count {
            return None;
        }
        // Oldest entry first: the slot that is `count` positions behind the
        // next write slot (wrapping).
        let index =
            (self.next + self.position + MINI_LOG_CAPACITY - self.count) % MINI_LOG_CAPACITY;
        let mut buf = [0u8; MINI_LOG_ENTRY_SIZE];
        match self
            .memory
            .read(self.address, index as usize * MINI_LOG_ENTRY_SIZE, &mut buf)
        {
            Ok(()) => {
                self.position += 1;
                Some(decode_log_entry(buf))
            }
            Err(error) => {
                self.position = self.count;
                Some(Err(error))
            }
        }
    }
}

// ---- codecs ----

/// Encodes an active record as eight little-endian bytes.
fn encode_active_record(scope_id: ScopeId, rei_position: u32) -> [u8; ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, 0, scope_id.as_u32());
    put_u32(&mut buf, 4, rei_position);
    buf
}

/// Decodes an active record from eight little-endian bytes.
fn decode_active_record(buf: [u8; ACTIVE_RECORD_SIZE]) -> ActiveRecord {
    ActiveRecord::new(ScopeId::from_u32(get_u32(&buf, 0)), get_u32(&buf, 4))
}

/// Encodes a block record as little-endian bytes.
fn encode_block_meta(meta: BlockMeta) -> [u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, BLOCK_ADDRESS_REGION, meta.address.region());
    put_u32(&mut buf, BLOCK_ADDRESS_REGION + 4, meta.address.slot());
    put_u32(
        &mut buf,
        BLOCK_ADDRESS_REGION + 8,
        meta.address.generation(),
    );
    put_u32(&mut buf, BLOCK_SIDE, meta.side);
    put_u32(&mut buf, BLOCK_BASE, meta.base);
    buf
}

/// Decodes a block record from little-endian bytes.
fn decode_block_meta(buf: [u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE]) -> BlockMeta {
    BlockMeta {
        address: LogicalAddress::from_parts(get_u32(&buf, 0), get_u32(&buf, 4), get_u32(&buf, 8)),
        side: get_u32(&buf, BLOCK_SIDE),
        base: get_u32(&buf, BLOCK_BASE),
    }
}

/// Decodes a Mini-Log entry, validating its kind.
fn decode_log_entry(buf: [u8; MINI_LOG_ENTRY_SIZE]) -> Result<MiniLogEvent> {
    let kind = match get_u32(&buf, LOG_KIND) {
        0 => MiniLogEventKind::Call,
        1 => MiniLogEventKind::Return,
        2 => MiniLogEventKind::Error,
        other => {
            return Err(Error::InvalidData(format!(
                "unknown Mini-Log event kind {other}"
            )));
        }
    };
    let cell_id = get_u32(&buf, LOG_CELL);
    let scope_id = get_u32(&buf, LOG_SCOPE);
    let cell = (cell_id != NONE_ID).then(|| CellId::from_u32(cell_id));
    let scope = (scope_id != NONE_ID).then(|| ScopeId::from_u32(scope_id));
    Ok(MiniLogEvent::new(kind, cell, scope))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn new_registers_active_space() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            memory.lookup_space(active.space_id()).unwrap().kind(),
            SpaceKind::Active
        );
        assert_eq!(active.depth(), 0);
        assert_eq!(active.blocks(), 1);
        assert_eq!(active.capacity(&memory).unwrap(), 9); // default 3×3
        assert_eq!(active.current_cell(), None);
        assert!(active.current(&memory).unwrap().is_none());
        // Directory + first block + Mini-Log.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(active.space_id()).allocations(), 3);
        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.allocation_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn call_builds_sequential_chain() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let main = ScopeId::from_u32(10);
        let calc = ScopeId::from_u32(20);
        let print = ScopeId::from_u32(30);

        assert_eq!(active.call(&mut memory, main, 0).unwrap().as_u32(), 0);
        assert_eq!(active.call(&mut memory, calc, 16).unwrap().as_u32(), 1);
        assert_eq!(active.call(&mut memory, print, 32).unwrap().as_u32(), 2);

        assert_eq!(active.depth(), 3);
        assert_eq!(active.current_cell(), Some(CellId::from_u32(2)));
        let current = active.current(&memory).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(current.scope_id(), print);
        assert_eq!(current.rei_position(), 32);

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn close_releases_top_cell_and_reuses_it() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let main = ScopeId::from_u32(1);
        let calc = ScopeId::from_u32(2);
        let print = ScopeId::from_u32(3);
        active.call(&mut memory, main, 0).unwrap();
        active.call(&mut memory, calc, 8).unwrap();
        active.call(&mut memory, print, 16).unwrap();

        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(active.depth(), 2);
        assert_eq!(active.current(&memory).unwrap().unwrap().scope_id(), calc);

        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(active.depth(), 0);
        assert!(matches!(
            active.close(&mut memory),
            Err(Error::EmptyActiveSpace)
        ));

        // A released end cell is reused by the next call: it lands at cell 0.
        let again = active.call(&mut memory, print, 32).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(again.as_u32(), 0);
        assert_eq!(active.current_cell(), Some(CellId::from_u32(0)));

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn grid_scales_then_creates_new_block() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        for i in 0..10u32 {
            active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(i), i).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(active.capacity(&memory).unwrap(), 16); // 3×3 → 4×4
        assert_eq!(active.blocks(), 1);

        for i in 10..64u32 {
            active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(i), i).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(active.capacity(&memory).unwrap(), 64); // 8×8
        assert_eq!(active.blocks(), 1);
        assert_eq!(active.depth(), 64);

        // The 65th call creates a second block starting at 3×3.
        active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(64), 64).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(active.blocks(), 2);
        assert_eq!(active.capacity(&memory).unwrap(), 64 + 9);
        assert_eq!(active.depth(), 65);

        // Records read correctly across the block boundary.
        let cross = active.active_record(&memory, CellId::from_u32(64)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(cross.scope_id(), ScopeId::from_u32(64));
        assert_eq!(cross.rei_position(), 64);

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn cell_reads_and_closes_are_checked() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(1), 0).unwrap();
        active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(2), 4).unwrap();

        assert!(matches!(
            active.active_record(&memory, CellId::from_u32(5)),
            Err(Error::CellNotActive { cell, depth: 2 }) if cell.as_u32() == 5
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            active.current(&memory).unwrap().unwrap().scope_id(),
            ScopeId::from_u32(2)
        );

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_path_yields_live_chain_in_order() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let main = ScopeId::from_u32(1);
        let calc = ScopeId::from_u32(2);
        let print = ScopeId::from_u32(3);
        active.call(&mut memory, main, 0).unwrap();
        active.call(&mut memory, calc, 8).unwrap();
        active.call(&mut memory, print, 16).unwrap();

        let path: Vec<_> = active
            .active_path(&memory)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|record| record.unwrap())
            .collect();
        let scopes: Vec<_> = path.iter().map(|record| record.scope_id()).collect();
        assert_eq!(scopes, vec![main, calc, print]);

        // After a close, the path reflects the live chain only.
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let path: Vec<_> = active
            .active_path(&memory)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|record| record.unwrap().scope_id())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(path, vec![main, calc]);

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn mini_log_records_transitions_in_order() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let main = ScopeId::from_u32(1);
        let calc = ScopeId::from_u32(2);
        active.call(&mut memory, main, 0).unwrap();
        active.call(&mut memory, calc, 8).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.record_error(&mut memory).unwrap();

        let events: Vec<_> = active
            .mini_log(&memory)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|event| event.unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(events.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(events[0].kind(), MiniLogEventKind::Call);
        assert_eq!(events[0].cell(), Some(CellId::from_u32(0)));
        assert_eq!(events[0].scope(), Some(main));
        assert_eq!(events[1].kind(), MiniLogEventKind::Call);
        assert_eq!(events[1].cell(), Some(CellId::from_u32(1)));
        assert_eq!(events[1].scope(), Some(calc));
        assert_eq!(events[2].kind(), MiniLogEventKind::Return);
        assert_eq!(events[2].cell(), Some(CellId::from_u32(1)));
        assert_eq!(events[2].scope(), Some(calc));
        // After the close, the error event refers to the current cell 0.
        assert_eq!(events[3].kind(), MiniLogEventKind::Error);
        assert_eq!(events[3].cell(), Some(CellId::from_u32(0)));
        assert_eq!(events[3].scope(), Some(main));

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn mini_log_overwrites_oldest_when_full() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        for i in 0..35u32 {
            active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(i), i).unwrap();
        }
        let events: Vec<_> = active
            .mini_log(&memory)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|event| event.unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(events.len(), MINI_LOG_CAPACITY as usize);
        // The oldest surviving entry is the one at cell 3 (entries 0–2 were
        // overwritten).
        assert_eq!(events[0].cell(), Some(CellId::from_u32(3)));
        assert_eq!(events[31].cell(), Some(CellId::from_u32(34)));

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn destroy_releases_all_storage() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        for i in 0..70u32 {
            active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(i), i).unwrap();
        }
        let space_id = active.space_id();
        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert!(memory.lookup_space(space_id).is_err());
        assert_eq!(memory.allocation_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn scope_and_cell_ids_display() {
        assert_eq!(ScopeId::from_u32(7).to_string(), "scope#7");
        assert_eq!(CellId::from_u32(3).to_string(), "cell#3");
        assert!(ScopeId::from_u32(0) < ScopeId::from_u32(1));
        assert_eq!(CellId::from_u32(9), CellId::from_u32(9));
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn active_space_types_are_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<ActiveSpace>();
        assert_send_sync::<ActivePathIter<'static>>();
        assert_send_sync::<MiniLogIter<'static>>();
        assert_send_sync::<ActiveRecord>();
        assert_send_sync::<CellId>();
        assert_send_sync::<ScopeId>();
        assert_send_sync::<MiniLogEvent>();
        assert_send_sync::<MiniLogEventKind>();
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\address.rs
//! RA logical addresses.
//!
//! A [`LogicalAddress`] identifies one allocation managed by the
//! [`MemoryManager`](crate::MemoryManager). Per the Memory Architecture
//! document (§9 *RA Logical Address Direction*) an address is a compact
//! triple identifying a **region**, a **slot** within it, and a
//! **generation** that detects stale references after a slot is released and
//! reused.
//!
//! An address is a logical value — never a raw native or Rust pointer — so it
//! is always validated against the manager's own state before use.

use std::fmt;

/// The compact triple `[region | slot | generation]` used to address
/// RA-managed memory.
///
/// * `region` — index of the region within the owning manager;
/// * `slot` — index of the first slot of the allocation within the region;
/// * `generation` — the slot generation recorded when the address was issued.
///
/// Addresses are `Copy`, cheap to compare and hash, and are the RA-level
/// representation of a location. The exact packed bit layout is intentionally
/// left open by the Memory Architecture.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct LogicalAddress {
    region: u32,
    slot: u32,
    generation: u32,
}

impl LogicalAddress {
    /// Creates an address from raw parts.
    ///
    /// Addresses are only meaningful to the manager that issued them; an
    /// arbitrary address is safe to construct but is rejected with
    /// [`Error::NotAllocated`](crate::Error::NotAllocated) (or
    /// [`Error::StaleAddress`](crate::Error::StaleAddress)) on lookup unless
    /// it matches a live allocation.
    pub fn from_parts(region: u32, slot: u32, generation: u32) -> LogicalAddress {
        LogicalAddress {
            region,
            slot,
            generation,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the region index of this address.
    pub fn region(self) -> u32 {
        self.region
    }

    /// Returns the first slot index of this address.
    pub fn slot(self) -> u32 {
        self.slot
    }

    /// Returns the generation recorded when the address was issued.
    pub fn generation(self) -> u32 {
        self.generation
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for LogicalAddress {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let (region, slot, generation) = (self.region, self.slot, self.generation);
        write!(f, "@r{region}:s{slot}:g{generation}")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn from_parts_and_accessors() {
        let address = LogicalAddress::from_parts(2, 7, 11);
        assert_eq!(address.region(), 2);
        assert_eq!(address.slot(), 7);
        assert_eq!(address.generation(), 11);
    }

    #[test]
    fn addresses_are_equality_compared_by_parts() {
        assert_eq!(
            LogicalAddress::from_parts(1, 2, 3),
            LogicalAddress::from_parts(1, 2, 3)
        );
        assert_ne!(
            LogicalAddress::from_parts(1, 2, 3),
            LogicalAddress::from_parts(1, 2, 4)
        );
        assert_ne!(
            LogicalAddress::from_parts(1, 2, 3),
            LogicalAddress::from_parts(1, 3, 3)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn addresses_hash_and_display() {
        let address = LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 5, 1);
        assert_eq!(address.to_string(), "@r0:s5:g1");

        let mut set = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        set.insert(address);
        set.insert(address);
        set.insert(LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 6, 1));
        assert_eq!(set.len(), 2);
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn address_is_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<LogicalAddress>();
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\codec.rs
//! Shared little-endian scalar codecs for manager-backed structures.
//!
//! Every manager-backed structure in this crate (module-table records,
//! code-map entries, active records, block records, Mini-Log entries) is a
//! byte layout inside a [`MemoryManager`](crate::manager::MemoryManager)
//! allocation. This private module holds the primitive little-endian `u32`
//! codecs those layouts share; it is **not** part of the public API and may
//! be reorganized without an architecture change.

/// Writes a little-endian `u32` at `offset` of `buf`.
pub(crate) fn put_u32(buf: &mut [u8], offset: usize, value: u32) {
    buf[offset..offset + 4].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
}

/// Reads a little-endian `u32` at `offset` of `buf`.
pub(crate) fn get_u32(buf: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes([
        buf[offset],
        buf[offset + 1],
        buf[offset + 2],
        buf[offset + 3],
    ])
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\entity_space.rs
//! Entity Manager — the Entity Grid of Entity Space (ES), Phase 3D-1.
//!
//! Per the frozen Entity Space V1 architecture document, *"Entity Space (ES)
//! is RA's runtime-data memory. It stores the actual values/entities created
//! and used by an executing RA program, while Active Space tracks
//! execution."* ES answers the question *"what data currently exists?"*.
//!
//! Entity Space **owns execution values**: the Entity Grid cells, their
//! value lists, and the `EntityCell → ValueList` binding — all of it
//! exclusively. It owns no executable structure (that belongs to Program
//! Space) and no execution identity (that belongs to Active Space);
//! REI/runtime execution belongs to the Runtime, not to this crate.
//!
//! The frozen roadmap divides Entity Space into six phases; this module
//! implements ✅ **Phase 3D-1 — Entity Manager (Entity Grid)** only. It
//! builds the container the later phases fill:
//!
//! * ✅ **Indexed Value List** (3D-2) — the per-cell value lists;
//! * ✅ **Extended Value Storage** (3D-3) — sequences, strings, objects;
//! * ✅ **Local Entity Resolution** (3D-4) — local cells via Active Space
//!   cells;
//! * ✅ **Global Entity Area** (3D-5) — the global entity group;
//! * ⏳ **Debug Metadata** (3D-6) — optional name→slot mapping.
//!
//! The **Indexed Value List** (3D-2) and **Extended Value Storage** (3D-3)
//! are implemented in the [`value_list`](crate::value_list) module,
//! **Local Entity Resolution** (3D-4) in the
//! [`local_entity`](crate::local_entity) module, and the **Global Entity
//! Area** (3D-5) in the [`global_entity`](crate::global_entity) module; the
//! remaining phase (3D-6) is not implemented here.
//!
//! # Entity Grid
//!
//! The frozen text specifies that ES *"uses a Grid of Entity Cells"* (§3, §12)
//! and that *"the Grid provides grouped lifetime management"* (§11); grid
//! dimensions, growth policy and limits are left open (§13). This module
//! implements the grid as a sequence of **grid blocks**: each block is one
//! [`MemoryManager`] allocation holding 64 cell records, blocks are appended
//! when the grid needs more cells, and **cells never move** — so an
//! [`EntityCellId`] is stable for the lifetime of the Entity Space. Block
//! storage addresses are tracked in a manager-backed **block directory** that
//! doubles when full (the same pattern as the internal Active Space block
//! directory).
//!
//! # Cell allocation, release and reuse
//!
//! * [`EntitySpace::allocate_cell`] hands out the next free cell: released
//!   cells are reused **before** the grid grows (the memory philosophy:
//!   *"Prefer reuse before requesting more host memory"*), then fresh cells,
//!   then growth.
//! * Released cells are threaded into a **free list** stored inside the cell
//!   records themselves (no host allocation): a free cell's record holds the
//!   id of the next free cell.
//! * A live cell's record holds the cell's **own id as a live marker**, which
//!   makes [`EntitySpace::is_live`], release validation and live-cell
//!   iteration O(1) and unambiguous.
//!
//! The cell record width and the block size are **implementation-defined**
//! (ES grid dimensions, growth and physical layout are open in §13).
//!
//! # Cell ↔ value list binding
//!
//! Entity Space is the **exclusive owner** of the `EntityCell → ValueList`
//! binding: a live cell's record embeds the storage [`LogicalAddress`] and
//! slot capacity of the **exactly one** value list bound to that cell, with
//! no host-side bookkeeping. The Runtime coordinates access through
//! [`EntitySpace::bind_value_list`], [`EntitySpace::value_list`] and
//! [`EntitySpace::destroy_value_list`] but **never owns the binding** and can
//! never fabricate one: a [`ValueList`] handle can only be obtained from a
//! live cell's embedded metadata. Cells are still **allocated unbound**
//! (capacity `0`); local variable resolution — turning an REI local
//! reference into a slot of the current invocation's list — is provided by
//! the [`local_entity`](crate::local_entity) coordinator (Phase 3D-4);
//! REI/runtime execution is not implemented in this crate.
//!
//! Program Space and Active Space have **no knowledge of Value Lists**: they
//! are never passed list handles, addresses or bindings.
//!
//! One invariant is preserved across the layout evolution: a **released cell
//! always keeps its free-list link at record offset 0**, so only the
//! live-cell record carries value-list fields.
//!
//! # Client of the Memory Manager
//!
//! Entity Space is a **client of the frozen [`MemoryManager`]**: it registers
//! [`SpaceKind::Entity`] and obtains **all** storage (grid blocks and the
//! block directory) through manager allocations referenced by
//! [`LogicalAddress`]. It never allocates host memory for storage, never
//! exposes host pointers, and has no dependency on Program Space or Active
//! Space (the local-resolution link to Active Space is provided by the
//! [`local_entity`](crate::local_entity) coordinator, Phase 3D-4).
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_memory::{EntityCellId, EntitySpace, MemoryManager};
//!
//! let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
