//! let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
//!
//! let a = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! let b = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(a.as_u32(), 0);
//!
//! // Released cells are reused before the grid grows.
//! entity.release_cell(&mut memory, a).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap(), a);
//! assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 2);
//!
//! entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
//! ```

use std::fmt;

use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::codec::{get_u32, put_u32};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::manager::MemoryManager;
use crate::space::{SpaceId, SpaceKind};
use crate::value_list::ValueList;

/// Cells per grid block. Implementation-defined: the Entity Space
/// architecture leaves grid dimensions, growth policy and limits open (§13).
const BLOCK_CELLS: usize = 64;
/// Byte size of one entity-cell record. The live-cell record embeds the
/// value-list metadata reserved for the Phase 3D-4 binding: the list's
/// storage [`LogicalAddress`] (region, slot, generation) and its slot
/// capacity. A released cell carries only its free-list link.
const CELL_RECORD_SIZE: usize = 20;
/// Byte size of one grid-block record in the block directory. Only the block
/// storage address is stored; the cell base of block `b` is implicit
/// (`64·b`), so the grid never relocates cells.
const BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE: usize = 12;
/// Initial block-directory capacity, in block records.
const INITIAL_DIRECTORY_CAPACITY: usize = 2;
/// Sentinel: an empty free list, or a free cell with no successor.
const NONE_ID: u32 = u32::MAX;
/// Field offset of the free-list link / live marker within a cell record
/// (little-endian).
const CELL_LINK: usize = 0;
/// Field offset of the embedded value-list storage address — region part.
const CELL_LIST_REGION: usize = 4;
/// Field offset of the embedded value-list storage address — slot part.
const CELL_LIST_SLOT: usize = 8;
/// Field offset of the embedded value-list storage address — generation
/// part.
const CELL_LIST_GENERATION: usize = 12;
/// Field offset of the embedded value-list slot capacity.
///
/// `0` is the sentinel for *no value list bound*: a real list always has
/// non-zero capacity (see
/// [`ValueList::new`](crate::value_list::ValueList::new)).
const CELL_LIST_CAPACITY: usize = 16;

/// A stable handle to one Entity Grid cell.
///
/// A cell id is **stable for the cell it names**: it never changes, never
/// moves (grid growth only appends blocks), and is never reassigned to a
/// different cell — a released cell's id is reused only by that same cell
/// when it is allocated again. An id therefore only ever becomes inactive
/// (its cell is released); it never comes to name a different cell. Per the
/// architecture, the active cell id participates in local entity identity in
/// Phase 3D-4 (the `CellId == EntityCellId` identity pairing).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct EntityCellId(u32);

impl EntityCellId {
    /// Returns the raw identifier value.
    pub fn as_u32(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Creates an identifier from a raw value.
    pub fn from_u32(value: u32) -> EntityCellId {
        EntityCellId(value)
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for EntityCellId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let id = self.0;
        write!(f, "entity-cell#{id}")
    }
}

/// The storage address of one grid block (a private directory record).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct BlockMeta {
    /// Logical address of the block's cell storage.
    address: LogicalAddress,
}

/// The block directory: a fixed-slot array of block storage addresses held in
/// one manager allocation (the private analogue of the Active Space block
/// directory and the module table).
#[derive(Debug)]
struct BlockDirectory {
    /// The space that owns the directory storage.
    space_id: SpaceId,
    /// The logical address of the directory storage.
    address: LogicalAddress,
    /// The number of block-record slots.
    capacity: usize,
    /// The number of blocks currently registered.
    count: usize,
}

impl BlockDirectory {
    /// Allocates the directory storage for `space_id`.
    fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager, space_id: SpaceId) -> Result<BlockDirectory> {
        let capacity = INITIAL_DIRECTORY_CAPACITY;
        let bytes = capacity * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE;
        let address = memory.allocate(space_id, bytes)?;
        Ok(BlockDirectory {
            space_id,
            address,
            capacity,
            count: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Returns the number of registered blocks.
    fn count(&self) -> usize {
        self.count
    }

    /// Decodes the block storage address at `index`.
    fn read_address(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, index: usize) -> Result<LogicalAddress> {
        let mut buf = [0u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE];
        memory.read(self.address, index * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(decode_block_address(buf))
    }

    /// Appends a block record, growing the directory when it is full.
    fn append(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, meta: BlockMeta) -> Result<()> {
        if self.count == self.capacity {
            self.grow(memory)?;
        }
        memory.write(
            self.address,
            self.count * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE,
            &encode_block_address(meta.address),
        )?;
        self.count += 1;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Doubles the directory, copying the block records.
    ///
    /// Only directory metadata moves; the grid-block allocations (and the
    /// cells inside them) never move.
    fn grow(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let new_capacity = self.capacity * 2;
        let new_bytes = new_capacity * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE;
        let new_address = memory.allocate(self.space_id, new_bytes)?;
        for index in 0..self.count {
            let mut buf = [0u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE];
            memory.read(self.address, index * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
            memory.write(new_address, index * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE, &buf)?;
        }
        memory.deallocate(self.address)?;
        self.address = new_address;
        self.capacity = new_capacity;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Deallocates the directory storage.
    fn reclaim(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        memory.deallocate(self.address)
    }
}

/// Entity Space (ES) — the Entity Grid of runtime-data cells (Phase 3D-1).
///
/// A client of the [`MemoryManager`]: it registers [`SpaceKind::Entity`] and
/// obtains **all** of its storage (grid blocks and the block directory)
/// through manager allocations. It never allocates host memory for storage
/// and never exposes host pointers.
///
/// The grid is a sequence of fixed-size blocks; cells never move. Released
/// cells are reused before the grid grows, exactly as the memory philosophy
/// requires. Each live cell is an empty container until the Runtime binds
/// exactly one value list to it through the embedded record metadata
/// (Phase 3D-4 binding); values live in that list, never in the cell record.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct EntitySpace {
    space_id: SpaceId,
    directory: BlockDirectory,
    /// Head of the threaded free list of released cells (`NONE_ID` when
    /// empty). A free cell's record holds the id of the next free cell.
    free_head: u32,
    /// The next never-allocated cell id.
    fresh: u32,
    /// The number of currently live (allocated) cells.
    live: u32,
}

impl EntitySpace {
    /// Creates an Entity Space within `memory`.
    ///
    /// Registers [`SpaceKind::Entity`] and allocates the first grid block
    /// (64 cells) and the block directory from the manager. The space begins
    /// with zero live cells.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when any of the initial storage cannot be allocated.
    pub fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<EntitySpace> {
        let space_id = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);
        let mut directory = BlockDirectory::new(memory, space_id)?;
        let block = memory.allocate(space_id, BLOCK_CELLS * CELL_RECORD_SIZE)?;
        directory.append(memory, BlockMeta { address: block })?;
        Ok(EntitySpace {
            space_id,
            directory,
            free_head: NONE_ID,
            fresh: 0,
            live: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Returns the [`SpaceId`] this Entity Space registered with the manager.
    pub fn space_id(&self) -> SpaceId {
        self.space_id
    }

    /// Returns the number of currently live (allocated) cells.
    pub fn cell_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.live as usize
    }

    /// Returns the number of grid blocks currently in the entity grid.
    pub fn blocks(&self) -> usize {
        self.directory.count()
    }

    /// Returns the total number of cells currently available across all
    /// blocks.
    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.directory.count() * BLOCK_CELLS
    }

    /// Returns `true` when `cell` is currently live (allocated and not
    /// released).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when the cell record cannot be read.
    pub fn is_live(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, cell: EntityCellId) -> Result<bool> {
        let id = cell.as_u32();
        if id >= self.fresh {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let buf = self.read_cell(memory, id)?;
        Ok(get_u32(&buf, CELL_LINK) == id)
    }

    /// Allocates a fresh Entity Grid cell and returns its stable id.
    ///
    /// A released cell is reused when one is available; otherwise the next
    /// never-allocated cell is taken, growing the grid with a new block when
    /// it is exhausted. Growth never moves existing cells. The cell is
    /// allocated with **no value list bound**; binding one through the
    /// embedded record metadata is done by the Runtime with
    /// [`EntitySpace::bind_value_list`] (Phase 3D-4 binding).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns manager errors when the grid cannot grow or the cell record
    /// cannot be written.
    pub fn allocate_cell(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<EntityCellId> {
        let id = if self.free_head != NONE_ID {
            let cell = self.free_head;
            let buf = self.read_cell(memory, cell)?;
            self.free_head = get_u32(&buf, CELL_LINK);
            cell
        } else {
            if self.fresh as usize >= self.capacity() {
                self.grow(memory)?;
            }
            let cell = self.fresh;
            self.fresh += 1;
            cell
        };
        // Mark the cell live by writing its own id into the record.
        self.write_cell(memory, id, &encode_live(id))?;
        self.live += 1;
        Ok(EntityCellId::from_u32(id))
    }

    /// Releases `cell`, making it reusable by a later allocation.
    ///
    /// The released cell is threaded into the grid's free list; the grid does
    /// not shrink and existing cells are unaffected.
    ///
    /// A value list still bound to `cell` must be destroyed first with
    /// [`EntitySpace::destroy_value_list`]: the release rewrites the cell
    /// record as free, wiping the embedded binding, so any bound list storage
    /// becomes orphaned. Such an orphaned allocation is **detectable**, not
    /// silent: [`EntitySpace::destroy`] then fails with
    /// [`Error::SpaceInUse`] and the allocation leaks only until the
    /// owning manager is shut down.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownEntityCell`] when `cell` is not currently live (it
    ///   was never allocated, or has already been released).
    /// * Manager errors when the cell record cannot be read or written.
    pub fn release_cell(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, cell: EntityCellId) -> Result<()> {
        if !self.is_live(memory, cell)? {
            return Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(cell));
        }
        let id = cell.as_u32();
        // Thread the cell into the free list.
        self.write_cell(memory, id, &encode_free(self.free_head))?;
        self.free_head = id;
        self.live -= 1;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Binds `list` to the live cell `cell`, making Entity Space the owner
    /// of the `EntityCell → ValueList` binding.
    ///
    /// The list's storage [`LogicalAddress`] and slot capacity are embedded
    /// in the cell's live record, so the binding needs no host-side
    /// bookkeeping. `list` must have been created under this Entity Space
    /// (see [`ValueList::new`](crate::value_list::ValueList::new)), and the
    /// cell must not already have a bound list.
    ///
    /// The Runtime coordinates binding but never owns it; the list stays
    /// owned by the cell until [`EntitySpace::destroy_value_list`] and
    /// [`EntitySpace::release_cell`] release it.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownEntityCell`] when `cell` is not currently live.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `list` does not belong to this
    ///   Entity Space, or `cell` already has a value list bound.
    /// * Manager errors when the cell record cannot be written.
    pub fn bind_value_list(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        cell: EntityCellId,
        list: &ValueList,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let id = cell.as_u32();
        if !self.is_live(memory, cell)? {
            return Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(cell));
        }
        if list.space_id() != self.space_id {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "value list does not belong to this Entity Space".into(),
            ));
        }
        let capacity = list.capacity();
        if capacity > u32::MAX as usize {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "value list capacity is too large to embed".into(),
            ));
        }
        let record = self.read_cell(memory, id)?;
        if decode_list_metadata(&record).1 != 0 {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "entity cell already has a value list bound".into(),
            ));
        }
        self.write_cell(
            memory,
            id,
            &encode_live_with_list(id, list.address(), capacity as u32),
        )
    }

    /// Resolves the value list bound to the live cell `cell`.
    ///
    /// The `ValueList` view is reconstructed internally from the cell's
    /// embedded metadata; the Runtime must resolve lists only through this
    /// method, never by fabricating handles over raw addresses. The returned
    /// view is for **reads and writes only** — destroying a bound list must
    /// flow through [`EntitySpace::destroy_value_list`], never through
    /// [`ValueList::destroy`](crate::value_list::ValueList::destroy) on the
    /// view, which would leave the cell's embedded binding stale.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownEntityCell`] when `cell` is not currently live.
    /// * [`Error::UnboundCell`] when `cell` is live but has no value list
    ///   bound.
    /// * Manager errors when the cell record cannot be read.
    pub fn value_list(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, cell: EntityCellId) -> Result<ValueList> {
        let id = cell.as_u32();
        if !self.is_live(memory, cell)? {
            return Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(cell));
        }
        let record = self.read_cell(memory, id)?;
        let (address, capacity) = decode_list_metadata(&record);
        if capacity == 0 {
            return Err(Error::UnboundCell(cell));
        }
        Ok(ValueList::adopt(self.space_id, address, capacity as usize))
    }

    /// Destroys the value list bound to the live cell `cell` and clears the
    /// embedded binding metadata.
    ///
    /// The bound list is destroyed through its [`ValueList`] view, so every
    /// extended-value content allocation the slots own (strings, arrays,
    /// objects) is released before the list storage is reclaimed through the
    /// manager; the record is then reset to the unbound sentinel, but **the
    /// cell stays live**: releasing the cell remains a separate operation
    /// ([`EntitySpace::release_cell`]).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownEntityCell`] when `cell` is not currently live.
    /// * [`Error::UnboundCell`] when `cell` has no value list bound (a
    ///   second destroy is detected, not masked).
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be reclaimed or the record
    ///   cannot be written.
    pub fn destroy_value_list(&self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, cell: EntityCellId) -> Result<()> {
        let id = cell.as_u32();
        if !self.is_live(memory, cell)? {
            return Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(cell));
        }
        let record = self.read_cell(memory, id)?;
        let (address, capacity) = decode_list_metadata(&record);
        if capacity == 0 {
            return Err(Error::UnboundCell(cell));
        }
        // Destroy through the list view: the slots' extended content is
        // released before the storage itself is reclaimed.
        ValueList::adopt(self.space_id, address, capacity as usize).destroy(memory)?;
        // The record is reset only after the storage is reclaimed, so a
        // failure leaves the cell still bound to live storage. The reset
        // keeps the live marker and clears the binding fields.
        self.write_cell(memory, id, &encode_live(id))
    }

    /// Returns an iterator over the live cells, in cell-id order.
    ///
    /// Construction cannot fail; the `Result` mirrors the crate's other
    /// iterator constructors and reserves room for future validation.
    pub fn cells<'a>(&self, memory: &'a MemoryManager) -> Result<EntityCellIter<'a>> {
        Ok(EntityCellIter::new(
            memory,
            self.directory.address,
            self.directory.count(),
            self.fresh,
        ))
    }

    /// Destroys Entity Space, reclaiming every grid block and the block
    /// directory, and unregisters the space.
    ///
    /// Every value list bound to a live cell must be destroyed first with
    /// [`EntitySpace::destroy_value_list`]. Destroy is **not atomic**: the
    /// grid blocks and directory are reclaimed before the space is
    /// unregistered, so when the space still owns bound list storage the
    /// [`Error::SpaceInUse`] failure leaves it half-destroyed — its cell
    /// records are gone and the remaining list allocations leak until the
    /// owning manager is shut down (a detectable leak: the manager still
    /// reports the orphaned allocations).
    ///
    /// After a successful destroy the [`SpaceId`] is no longer registered.
    /// Dropping an [`EntitySpace`] without calling this leaks its
    /// allocations until the owning manager is shut down.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::SpaceInUse`] when the space still owns bound list
    ///   storage.
    /// * Returns an error when storage cannot be reclaimed or the space
    ///   cannot be unregistered.
    pub fn destroy(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let EntitySpace {
            space_id,
            directory,
            ..
        } = self;
        for index in 0..directory.count() {
            let address = directory.read_address(memory, index)?;
            memory.deallocate(address)?;
        }
        directory.reclaim(memory)?;
        memory.unregister_space(space_id)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    // ---- internals ----

    /// Appends a new 64-cell grid block.
    fn grow(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let block = memory.allocate(self.space_id, BLOCK_CELLS * CELL_RECORD_SIZE)?;
        self.directory
            .append(memory, BlockMeta { address: block })?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Resolves a cell id to its block index and in-block slot.
    ///
    /// Block `b` covers cells `[64·b, 64·b + 64)`, so resolution is O(1) and
    /// cells never move.
    fn cell_block_slot(id: u32) -> (usize, usize) {
        (id as usize / BLOCK_CELLS, id as usize % BLOCK_CELLS)
    }

    /// Reads the raw record of the cell with `id`.
    fn read_cell(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, id: u32) -> Result<[u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE]> {
        let (block, slot) = Self::cell_block_slot(id);
        let address = self.directory.read_address(memory, block)?;
        let mut buf = [0u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE];
        memory.read(address, slot * CELL_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(buf)
    }

    /// Writes the raw record of the cell with `id`.
    fn write_cell(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        id: u32,
        record: &[u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let (block, slot) = Self::cell_block_slot(id);
        let address = self.directory.read_address(memory, block)?;
        memory.write(address, slot * CELL_RECORD_SIZE, record)
    }
}

/// An iterator over the live cells of an Entity Space, in cell-id order.
///
/// Cells are identified by their live marker (their own id in the record);
/// released and never-allocated cells are skipped. Iteration stops after the
/// first read failure, which is reported as the final item.
pub struct EntityCellIter<'a> {
    memory: &'a MemoryManager,
    directory: LogicalAddress,
    block_count: usize,
    fresh: u32,
    block: usize,
    slot: usize,
    address: Option<LogicalAddress>,
}

impl fmt::Debug for EntityCellIter<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("EntityCellIter")
            .field("directory", &self.directory)
            .field("block_count", &self.block_count)
            .field("fresh", &self.fresh)
            .field("block", &self.block)
            .field("slot", &self.slot)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl<'a> EntityCellIter<'a> {
    /// Creates a live-cell iterator over the cells below `fresh`.
    fn new(
        memory: &'a MemoryManager,
        directory: LogicalAddress,
        block_count: usize,
        fresh: u32,
    ) -> EntityCellIter<'a> {
        EntityCellIter {
            memory,
            directory,
            block_count,
            fresh,
            block: 0,
            slot: 0,
            address: None,
        }
    }
}

impl Iterator for EntityCellIter<'_> {
    type Item = Result<EntityCellId>;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
        loop {
            let address = match self.address {
                Some(address) => address,
                None => {
                    if self.block >= self.block_count {
                        return None;
                    }
                    let mut buf = [0u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE];
                    match self
                        .memory
                        .read(self.directory, self.block * BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)
                    {
                        Ok(()) => {
                            let address = decode_block_address(buf);
                            self.address = Some(address);
                            address
                        }
                        Err(error) => {
                            self.block = self.block_count;
                            return Some(Err(error));
                        }
                    }
                }
            };
            if self.slot >= BLOCK_CELLS {
                self.address = None;
                self.block += 1;
                self.slot = 0;
                continue;
            }
            let id = (self.block * BLOCK_CELLS + self.slot) as u32;
            if id >= self.fresh {
                return None;
            }
            let mut buf = [0u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE];
            match self
                .memory
                .read(address, self.slot * CELL_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)
            {
                Ok(()) => {
                    self.slot += 1;
                    if get_u32(&buf, CELL_LINK) == id {
                        return Some(Ok(EntityCellId::from_u32(id)));
                    }
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    self.block = self.block_count;
                    return Some(Err(error));
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

// ---- codecs ----

/// Encodes a grid-block record: the block storage address.
fn encode_block_address(address: LogicalAddress) -> [u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, 0, address.region());
    put_u32(&mut buf, 4, address.slot());
    put_u32(&mut buf, 8, address.generation());
    buf
}

/// Decodes a grid-block record into the block storage address.
fn decode_block_address(buf: [u8; BLOCK_RECORD_SIZE]) -> LogicalAddress {
    LogicalAddress::from_parts(get_u32(&buf, 0), get_u32(&buf, 4), get_u32(&buf, 8))
}

/// Encodes a free cell record holding the id of the next free cell.
fn encode_free(link: u32) -> [u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, CELL_LINK, link);
    buf
}

/// Encodes a live cell record holding the cell's own id as a live marker.
///
/// The embedded value-list fields are zeroed, so the record carries the
/// unbound sentinel: a freshly allocated cell has no value list yet
/// (capacity `0`). Phase 3D-4 binds a list by writing its storage address
/// and capacity into those fields ([`encode_live_with_list`]).
fn encode_live(id: u32) -> [u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, CELL_LINK, id);
    buf
}

/// Encodes a live cell record that binds one value list to the cell.
///
/// This is the binding primitive behind
/// [`EntitySpace::bind_value_list`]: it embeds the list's storage
/// [`LogicalAddress`] and slot capacity into the live-cell record after the
/// live marker, so a bound list is owned by its cell with no host-side
/// bookkeeping.
fn encode_live_with_list(id: u32, list: LogicalAddress, capacity: u32) -> [u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = encode_live(id);
    put_u32(&mut buf, CELL_LIST_REGION, list.region());
    put_u32(&mut buf, CELL_LIST_SLOT, list.slot());
    put_u32(&mut buf, CELL_LIST_GENERATION, list.generation());
    put_u32(&mut buf, CELL_LIST_CAPACITY, capacity);
    buf
}

/// Decodes the value-list metadata embedded in a live-cell record.
///
/// Returns the list's storage address and slot capacity. A capacity of `0`
/// means no value list is bound (cells are allocated unbound). Used by
/// [`EntitySpace::value_list`] and [`EntitySpace::destroy_value_list`] to
/// reconstruct the owned
/// [`ValueList`](crate::value_list::ValueList) from the record.
fn decode_list_metadata(buf: &[u8; CELL_RECORD_SIZE]) -> (LogicalAddress, u32) {
    let address = LogicalAddress::from_parts(
        get_u32(buf, CELL_LIST_REGION),
        get_u32(buf, CELL_LIST_SLOT),
        get_u32(buf, CELL_LIST_GENERATION),
    );
    (address, get_u32(buf, CELL_LIST_CAPACITY))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::value_list::{Value, ValueList};

    #[test]
    fn new_registers_entity_space() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            memory.lookup_space(entity.space_id()).unwrap().kind(),
            SpaceKind::Entity
        );
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(entity.blocks(), 1);
        assert_eq!(entity.capacity(), 64);
        // Block directory + first grid block.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 2);
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.allocation_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn allocate_hands_out_sequential_cells() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let a = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let b = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let c = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.as_u32(), 0);
        assert_eq!(b.as_u32(), 1);
        assert_eq!(c.as_u32(), 2);
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 3);
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, a).unwrap());
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, b).unwrap());
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, c).unwrap());
        assert!(!entity.is_live(&memory, EntityCellId::from_u32(10)).unwrap());
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn release_makes_cell_reusable() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let a = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let b = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let c = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();

        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, b).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 2);
        assert!(!entity.is_live(&memory, b).unwrap());
        // The other cells are unaffected by the release.
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, a).unwrap());
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, c).unwrap());

        // Released cells are reused (LIFO) before the grid grows.
        let again = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(again, b);
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 3);
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, b).unwrap());

        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn release_validates_liveness() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let a = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();

        // Never allocated.
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.release_cell(&mut memory, EntityCellId::from_u32(9)),
            Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(_))
        ));
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, a).unwrap();
        // Already released.
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.release_cell(&mut memory, a),
            Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(_))
        ));
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn grid_grows_with_new_blocks_without_moving_cells() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut cells = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..64 {
            cells.push(entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap());
        }
        assert_eq!(entity.blocks(), 1);
        assert_eq!(entity.capacity(), 64);

        let extra = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(extra.as_u32(), 64);
        assert_eq!(entity.blocks(), 2);
        assert_eq!(entity.capacity(), 128);

        // Earlier cells are still live at their original ids.
        assert_eq!(cells[0], EntityCellId::from_u32(0));
        assert_eq!(cells[63], EntityCellId::from_u32(63));
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, cells[63]).unwrap());
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn reused_cells_delay_growth() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        for _ in 0..64 {
            entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        }
        for id in 0..5u32 {
            entity
                .release_cell(&mut memory, EntityCellId::from_u32(id))
                .unwrap();
        }
        for _ in 0..5 {
            entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(entity.blocks(), 1); // reuse, not growth
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 64);
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn cells_iterates_live_cells_in_order() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let a = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let b = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let c = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, b).unwrap();

        let live: Vec<_> = entity
            .cells(&memory)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|cell| cell.unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(live, vec![a, c]);
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn destroy_releases_all_storage() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        for _ in 0..130 {
            entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(entity.blocks(), 3);
        let space_id = entity.space_id();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert!(memory.lookup_space(space_id).is_err());
        assert_eq!(memory.allocation_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn live_cells_start_with_unbound_list_metadata() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let cell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();

        let buf = entity.read_cell(&memory, cell.as_u32()).unwrap();
        // The live marker is the cell's own id; the value-list fields carry
        // the unbound sentinel (capacity zero).
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&buf, CELL_LINK), cell.as_u32());
        assert_eq!(
            decode_list_metadata(&buf),
            (LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 0, 0), 0)
        );

        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn bound_list_metadata_round_trips_through_the_record() {
        let list = LogicalAddress::from_parts(2, 7, 11);
        let buf = encode_live_with_list(5, list, 3);
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&buf, CELL_LINK), 5);
        assert_eq!(decode_list_metadata(&buf), (list, 3));

        // Releasing rewrites the record as free, clearing the embedded
        // value-list fields along with the live marker.
        let free = encode_free(17);
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&free, CELL_LINK), 17);
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&free, CELL_LIST_CAPACITY), 0);
    }

    // ---- Phase 3D-4 binding ----

    /// Builds an Entity Space with one live cell bound to a fresh list.
    fn bound_cell(memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> (EntitySpace, EntityCellId, ValueList) {
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(memory).unwrap();
        let cell = entity.allocate_cell(memory).unwrap();
        let list = ValueList::new(memory, entity.space_id(), 3).unwrap();
        entity.bind_value_list(memory, cell, &list).unwrap();
        (entity, cell, list)
    }

    #[test]
    fn bind_value_list_embeds_metadata_in_the_cell_record() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let (mut entity, cell, list) = bound_cell(&mut memory);

        let record = entity.read_cell(&memory, cell.as_u32()).unwrap();
        // The live marker is the cell's own id; the binding metadata is the
        // list's address and capacity.
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&record, CELL_LINK), cell.as_u32());
        assert_eq!(
            decode_list_metadata(&record),
            (list.address(), list.capacity() as u32)
        );
        // Directory + first block + the bound list.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 3);

        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_bind_is_rejected() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let (mut entity, cell, _list) = bound_cell(&mut memory);
        let second = ValueList::new(&mut memory, entity.space_id(), 2).unwrap();

        assert!(matches!(
            entity.bind_value_list(&mut memory, cell, &second),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        // The original binding is untouched.
        assert!(entity.value_list(&memory, cell).is_ok());

        second.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn foreign_space_list_cannot_be_bound() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let cell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let work = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Work);
        let foreign = ValueList::new(&mut memory, work, 2).unwrap();

        assert!(matches!(
            entity.bind_value_list(&mut memory, cell, &foreign),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        // Nothing was embedded.
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.value_list(&memory, cell),
            Err(Error::UnboundCell(_))
        ));

        foreign.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bound_list_resolves_to_a_working_view() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let (mut entity, cell, list) = bound_cell(&mut memory);

        let view = entity.value_list(&memory, cell).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(view.capacity(), list.capacity());
        // The resolved view reads and writes the same storage as the
        // original handle.
        view.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(5)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(5));
        assert_eq!(view.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(5));

        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unbound_and_non_live_cells_fail_resolution() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let cell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();

        // Live but unbound.
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.value_list(&memory, cell),
            Err(Error::UnboundCell(_))
        ));
        // Never allocated.
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.value_list(&memory, EntityCellId::from_u32(7)),
            Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(_))
        ));
        // Binding a list to a non-live cell is rejected too.
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, entity.space_id(), 2).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.bind_value_list(&mut memory, EntityCellId::from_u32(9), &list),
            Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(_))
        ));
        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();

        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        // After release the cell is not live: resolution reports it unknown.
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.value_list(&memory, cell),
            Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(_))
        ));
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn destroy_value_list_releases_storage_and_keeps_cell_alive() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let (mut entity, cell, list) = bound_cell(&mut memory);
        list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(1)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 3);

        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        // The list storage is reclaimed; the cell is still live and unbound.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 2);
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, cell).unwrap());
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.value_list(&memory, cell),
            Err(Error::UnboundCell(_))
        ));
        // The old handle can no longer read the reclaimed storage.
        assert!(list.get(&memory, 0).is_err());

        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn destroy_value_list_releases_extended_content_too() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let (mut entity, cell, list) = bound_cell(&mut memory);
        // The space already owns its directory, grid block and the list
        // storage; the three extended content allocations bring it to 6.
        list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "greeting").unwrap();
        list.set_array(&mut memory, 1, &[Value::Int(1), Value::Int(2)])
            .unwrap();
        list.set_object(&mut memory, 2, &[("k", Value::Float(0.5))])
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 6);

        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        // The extended content allocations are released alongside the list
        // storage, leaving only the space's own directory and grid block.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 2);
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, cell).unwrap());
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.value_list(&memory, cell),
            Err(Error::UnboundCell(_))
        ));

        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn double_destroy_value_list_is_detected() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let (mut entity, cell, _list) = bound_cell(&mut memory);

        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, cell),
            Err(Error::UnboundCell(_))
        ));
        // Destroying on a non-live cell reports the cell as unknown.
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, cell).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, cell),
            Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(_))
        ));
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn release_after_destroy_completes_a_clean_lifecycle() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut cells = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            let cell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
            let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, entity.space_id(), 2).unwrap();
            list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(7)).unwrap();
            entity.bind_value_list(&mut memory, cell, &list).unwrap();
            cells.push(cell);
        }
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 5);

        for cell in &cells {
            entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, *cell).unwrap();
            entity.release_cell(&mut memory, *cell).unwrap();
        }
        // Only the directory and the grid block remain.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 2);
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.allocation_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn forgetting_list_teardown_is_a_detectable_leak() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let (entity, _cell, _list) = bound_cell(&mut memory);

        // The manager refuses to unregister a space that still owns the
        // bound list, so a forgotten teardown leaks detectably.
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.destroy(&mut memory),
            Err(Error::SpaceInUse { .. })
        ));
        // The grid blocks were reclaimed but the list allocation remains.
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn entity_cell_ids_display_and_order() {
        assert_eq!(EntityCellId::from_u32(7).to_string(), "entity-cell#7");
        assert!(EntityCellId::from_u32(0) < EntityCellId::from_u32(1));
        assert_eq!(EntityCellId::from_u32(3), EntityCellId::from_u32(3));
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn entity_space_types_are_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<EntitySpace>();
        assert_send_sync::<EntityCellIter<'static>>();
        assert_send_sync::<EntityCellId>();
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\error.rs
//! Error types for the RA memory manager.
//!
//! [`Error`] describes every failure mode of the memory manager: invalid
//! addresses, stale references, configuration problems and lifecycle
//! violations. The [`Result`] alias fixes the error type for the whole crate.

use std::fmt;

use crate::active_space::CellId;
use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::entity_space::EntityCellId;
use crate::program_space::ModuleId;
use crate::space::SpaceId;

/// The error type used throughout the `ra-memory` crate.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Error {
    /// A zero-length allocation was requested; allocations must be non-empty.
    EmptyAllocation,
    /// An allocation request exceeded what a single region can hold.
    ///
    /// The manager never spans a single allocation across regions.
    AllocationTooLarge {
        /// The number of bytes requested.
        requested: usize,
        /// The number of bytes a single region can hold.
        capacity: usize,
    },
    /// The manager reached its configured region limit while growing.
    RegionLimitReached {
        /// The current number of regions.
        regions: usize,
        /// The configured maximum.
        max: usize,
    },
    /// A [`SpaceId`] was used that is not registered with this manager.
    UnknownSpace(SpaceId),
    /// A space still owns live allocations and cannot be unregistered.
    SpaceInUse {
        /// The space that still owns allocations.
        space: SpaceId,
        /// The number of live allocations owned by the space.
        allocations: usize,
        /// The number of live bytes owned by the space.
        bytes: u64,
    },
    /// An address does not refer to a live allocation of this manager.
    ///
    /// The address may be foreign (a region this manager never created), may
    /// refer to a slot that was never allocated, or may refer to an
    /// allocation that has already been deallocated.
    NotAllocated {
        /// The offending address.
        address: LogicalAddress,
    },
    /// An address carries a stale generation.
    ///
    /// The slot it refers to has been released and reused since the address
    /// was issued, so the address must not be trusted.
    StaleAddress {
        /// The offending address.
        address: LogicalAddress,
        /// The generation currently recorded at that slot.
        current: u32,
    },
    /// A read, write or fill range extends past the end of an allocation.
    OutOfBounds {
        /// The address of the allocation.
        address: LogicalAddress,
        /// The byte offset where the operation started.
        offset: usize,
        /// The number of bytes the operation requested.
        length: usize,
        /// The total size in bytes of the allocation.
        available: usize,
    },
    /// A [`MemoryManagerConfig`](crate::MemoryManagerConfig) failed validation.
    InvalidConfig(String),
    /// An invalid argument was passed to a Program Space operation.
    InvalidArgument(String),
    /// A module was requested that is not loaded in Program Space, or that
    /// has no global entity group registered in the Global Entity Area
    /// (Phase 3D-5).
    UnknownModule(ModuleId),
    /// A module with the same name is already loaded in Program Space.
    DuplicateModule(String),
    /// Stored data was structurally invalid (e.g. a corrupted module record).
    InvalidData(String),
    /// An Active Space operation required a live active record, but the
    /// call chain was empty.
    EmptyActiveSpace,
    /// An Active Space cell was referenced that is not currently live.
    CellNotActive {
        /// The referenced cell.
        cell: CellId,
        /// The number of currently live active records.
        depth: usize,
    },
    /// An Entity Space cell was referenced that is not currently live (it
    /// was never allocated, or has already been released).
    UnknownEntityCell(EntityCellId),
    /// A value-list slot held a different value category than the requested
    /// extended-value read (Phase 3D-3).
    ValueMismatch {
        /// The slot that was read.
        slot: usize,
        /// The category the caller requested, e.g. `"string"`.
        expected: &'static str,
        /// The category actually stored in the slot, e.g. `"int"`.
        found: &'static str,
    },
    /// A live Entity Space cell has no value list bound to it (Phase 3D-4
    /// binding).
    UnboundCell(EntityCellId),
    /// A global entity reference named an index outside a module's allocated
    /// global range (Phase 3D-5).
    UnknownGlobalIndex {
        /// The module whose global group was addressed.
        module: ModuleId,
        /// The compiled global index that was out of range.
        index: usize,
    },
}

impl fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Error::EmptyAllocation => f.write_str("cannot allocate zero bytes"),
            Error::AllocationTooLarge {
                requested,
                capacity,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "allocation of {requested} bytes exceeds the region capacity of {capacity} bytes"
            ),
            Error::RegionLimitReached { regions, max } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "region limit reached: {regions} regions, maximum is {max}"
                )
            }
            Error::UnknownSpace(space) => write!(f, "unknown memory space {space}"),
            Error::SpaceInUse {
                space,
                allocations,
                bytes,
            } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "space {space} still owns {allocations} allocations ({bytes} bytes)"
                )
            }
            Error::NotAllocated { address } => {
                write!(f, "{address} does not refer to a live allocation")
            }
            Error::StaleAddress { address, current } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "{address} is stale: the slot now has generation {current}"
                )
            }
            Error::OutOfBounds {
                address,
                offset,
                length,
                available,
            } => {
                let end = offset + length;
                write!(
                    f,
                    "range {offset}..{end} is out of bounds for {address} (size {available})"
                )
            }
            Error::InvalidConfig(message) => {
                write!(f, "invalid memory manager configuration: {message}")
            }
            Error::InvalidArgument(message) => write!(f, "invalid argument: {message}"),
            Error::UnknownModule(module) => write!(f, "unknown module {module}"),
            Error::DuplicateModule(name) => {
                write!(f, "module {name:?} is already loaded")
            }
            Error::InvalidData(message) => write!(f, "invalid data: {message}"),
            Error::EmptyActiveSpace => f.write_str("no active records in Active Space"),
            Error::CellNotActive { cell, depth } => {
                write!(f, "cell {cell} is not active (depth is {depth})")
            }
            Error::UnknownEntityCell(cell) => {
                write!(f, "unknown entity cell {cell}")
            }
            Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot,
                expected,
                found,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "slot {slot} holds a {found} value, not a {expected} value"
            ),
            Error::UnboundCell(cell) => {
                write!(f, "entity cell {cell} has no bound value list")
            }
            Error::UnknownGlobalIndex { module, index } => {
                write!(f, "unknown global index {index} in module {module}")
            }
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for Error {}

/// Convenience alias for [`Result`](std::result::Result) fixed to [`Error`].
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;

#[cfg(test)]
