            (
                Error::UnknownGlobalIndex {
                    module: ModuleId::from_u32(2),
                    index: 7,
                },
                "unknown global index 7 in module module#2",
            ),
        ];
        for (error, expected) in cases {
            assert_eq!(error.to_string(), expected);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn errors_are_std_errors_and_comparable() {
        let error = Error::EmptyAllocation;
        let boxed: Box<dyn std::error::Error> = Box::new(error.clone());
        assert!(boxed.to_string().contains("zero"));
        assert_eq!(error, Error::EmptyAllocation);
        assert_ne!(
            error,
            Error::NotAllocated {
                address: LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 0, 0)
            }
        );
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\global_entity.rs
//! Global Entity Area — Phase 3D-5.
//!
//! Per the approved Global Entity Area architecture, a **global entity** is an
//! execution value whose lifetime is the **module lifetime** — not an
//! invocation lifetime. Each loaded module owns one **global entity group**
//! inside the program's single Global Entity Area, and global references are
//! module-qualified `(ModuleId, GlobalIndex)` pairs resolved deterministically
//! down the ownership chain:
//!
//! ```text
//! (ModuleId, GlobalIndex) → Global Entity Group → Entity Cell → Value List → Value
//! ```
//!
//! * the **`(ModuleId, GlobalIndex)`** reference is compiled by the compiler —
//!   the module component selects the module's group, the index selects the
//!   global entity inside it (positional, no name or symbol);
//! * the **Global Entity Group** is the module's index→cell mapping, born with
//!   [`GlobalEntityArea::load_module`] and dying with
//!   [`GlobalEntityArea::destroy_module`] — grouped lifetime management
//!   aligned with the frozen module lifecycle (`ProgramSpace::unload_module`);
//! * the **Entity Cell → Value List binding** is owned **exclusively by Entity
//!   Space** and resolved only through
//!   [`EntitySpace::value_list`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::value_list)
//!   — this module never bypasses Entity Space and never exposes binding
//!   metadata;
//! * the **Value** is the primitive or extended value at the compiled slot.
//!
//! # Ownership
//!
//! The frozen ownership rules are preserved exactly:
//!
//! * the **MemoryManager** remains the sole allocator — every allocation this
//!   module makes (the module directory, the per-module group directories, the
//!   global value lists and their extended content) flows through the manager
//!   under the Entity Space's id, so **Entity Space owns all runtime global
//!   values**;
//! * **Program Space** owns executable structure only — this module takes a
//!   [`ModuleId`] as an opaque key and never reads, writes or stores program
//!   data;
//! * **Active Space** is not involved at all — global resolution performs no
//!   Active-record reads (the `CellId == EntityCellId` identity pairing is a
//!   *local* resolution invariant, Phase 3D-4);
//! * the **Runtime coordinates only** — it creates the area, loads modules
//!   into it, allocates globals, and drives teardown; it owns no memory.
//!
//! The **Global Entity Area** itself owns nothing but its own bookkeeping: the
//! module→group directory and the per-module index→cell directories (all
//! Entity Space-scoped). The module→global *layout* (how many globals a module
//! declares) is static, compiler-produced data held by the Runtime Loader and
//! passed in at [`GlobalEntityArea::load_module`]; this module never stores
//! it.
//!
//! # Frozen architectural invariant
//!
//! The following invariant is **frozen** — it binds this module in every
//! version and no implementation may weaken it:
//!
//! * A [`ModuleId`] must never be reused while its **GlobalEntityGroup**
//!   still exists.
//! * The lifetime of a **ModuleGlobalGroup** is **exactly** the lifetime of
//!   the loaded module.
//! * A **ModuleGlobalGroup** must always be **destroyed** before that
//!   [`ModuleId`] can be reused.
//!
//! In this crate's terms, the GlobalEntityGroup / ModuleGlobalGroup of a
//! loaded module is the module's global entity group — born with
//! [`GlobalEntityArea::load_module`] and dying with
//! [`GlobalEntityArea::destroy_module`], exactly as documented above. The
//! group must therefore be destroyed before its [`ModuleId`] may be reused.
//!
//! # Teardown order
//!
//! Because the area's directories are Entity Space-scoped but reclaimed by the
//! area, destruction is a documented Runtime discipline with **detectable**
//! misordering (never silent): destroy each module's group
//! ([`GlobalEntityArea::destroy_module`]), then the area
//! ([`GlobalEntityArea::destroy`]), then the Entity Space. Forgetting a step
//! leaves a detectable [`Error::SpaceInUse`] or leaked allocation, exactly as
//! with bound value lists.
//!
//! # Out of scope
//!
//! This module implements only **deterministic module-qualified global
//! resolution**. It does **not** implement debug metadata (3D-6), reflection,
//! symbol lookup, name lookup, dynamic global search, or REI/runtime execution
//! — those belong to later phases or to the Runtime.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_common::SourcePos;
//! use ra_memory::{
//!     CodeMapEntry, EntitySpace, GlobalEntityArea, LoadedModule, MemoryManager,
//!     ProgramSpace, Value,
//! };
//!
//! let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
//! let mut program = ProgramSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
//!
//! // The Runtime Loader loads a module; Program Space assigns its id.
//! let module = program
//!     .load_module(
//!         &mut memory,
//!         &LoadedModule::new(
//!             "main",
//!             &[0x00],
//!             &[],
//!             &[CodeMapEntry::new(0, SourcePos::from(0u32))],
//!         ),
//!     )
//!     .unwrap();
//!
//! // Module load: one global entity group per module, sized from the
//! // module's static global count.
//! let mut area = GlobalEntityArea::new(&mut memory, &entity).unwrap();
//! area.load_module(&mut memory, module, 2).unwrap();
//!
//! // Deterministic module-qualified resolution: (ModuleId, GlobalIndex).
//! let x = area.allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1).unwrap();
//! let y = area.allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1).unwrap();
//! area
//!     .write_global(&mut memory, &entity, module, x, 0, Value::Int(5))
//!     .unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(
//!     area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, x, 0).unwrap(),
//!     Value::Int(5)
//! );
//!
//! // Module unload: the group's cells and lists are reclaimed.
//! area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module).unwrap();
//! area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! program.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
//! ```

use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::codec::{get_u32, put_u32};
use crate::entity_space::{EntityCellId, EntitySpace};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::manager::MemoryManager;
use crate::program_space::ModuleId;
use crate::space::SpaceId;
use crate::value_list::{Value, ValueList};

/// Byte width of one module-directory record: the module id, the group
/// directory's storage [`LogicalAddress`] (region, slot, generation) and the
/// group's slot capacity and allocated count.
const MODULE_RECORD_SIZE: usize = 24;
/// Byte width of one global-group entry: a single entity cell id.
const GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE: usize = 4;
/// Initial module-directory capacity, in module records.
const INITIAL_DIRECTORY_CAPACITY: usize = 2;
/// Sentinel: a vacant module-directory slot, or a group entry that has no
/// allocated cell. `u32::MAX` is never a live module id or cell id.
const NONE_ID: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// The group metadata of one loaded module: the manager-backed index→cell
/// directory plus its capacity and allocated count.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct GroupMeta {
    /// The logical address of the group's index→cell directory.
    directory: LogicalAddress,
    /// The number of index slots currently available in the directory.
    capacity: u32,
    /// The number of global entities allocated so far (indices `[0, count)`).
    count: u32,
}

/// One module-directory record: a loaded module mapped to its global group.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct ModuleRecord {
    /// The module id (`NONE_ID` marks a vacant slot).
    module: u32,
    /// The module's global group metadata.
    group: GroupMeta,
}

impl ModuleRecord {
    /// A vacant record: no module, no group.
    fn vacant() -> ModuleRecord {
        ModuleRecord {
            module: NONE_ID,
            group: GroupMeta {
                directory: LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 0, 0),
                capacity: 0,
                count: 0,
            },
        }
    }
}

/// The module directory: a fixed-slot array of [`ModuleRecord`]s held in one
/// manager allocation, mapping each loaded module to its global entity group.
///
/// The directory doubles when full; a slot vacated by
/// [`GlobalEntityArea::destroy_module`] is reused by the next loaded module
/// before the directory grows (the memory philosophy: reuse before requesting
/// more host memory).
#[derive(Debug)]
struct ModuleDirectory {
    /// The space that owns the directory storage.
    space_id: SpaceId,
    /// The logical address of the directory storage.
    address: LogicalAddress,
    /// The number of record slots.
    capacity: usize,
    /// The number of records ever appended (the high-water mark; vacant slots
    /// within `[0, count)` are reused before growth).
    count: usize,
}

impl ModuleDirectory {
    /// Allocates the directory storage under `space_id`.
    fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager, space_id: SpaceId) -> Result<ModuleDirectory> {
        let capacity = INITIAL_DIRECTORY_CAPACITY;
        let bytes = capacity * MODULE_RECORD_SIZE;
        let address = memory.allocate(space_id, bytes)?;
        // Every record starts vacant (all bytes 0xFF → module id NONE_ID).
        memory.fill(address, 0, bytes, 0xFF)?;
        Ok(ModuleDirectory {
            space_id,
            address,
            capacity,
            count: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Decodes the record at `index`.
    fn read_record(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, index: usize) -> Result<ModuleRecord> {
        let mut buf = [0u8; MODULE_RECORD_SIZE];
        memory.read(self.address, index * MODULE_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(decode_module_record(buf))
    }

    /// Encodes and writes the record at `index`.
    fn write_record(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        index: usize,
        record: ModuleRecord,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        memory.write(
            self.address,
            index * MODULE_RECORD_SIZE,
            &encode_module_record(record),
        )
    }

    /// Returns the slot of the live record for `module`, or `None`.
    fn find(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, module: u32) -> Result<Option<usize>> {
        for index in 0..self.count {
            if self.read_record(memory, index)?.module == module {
                return Ok(Some(index));
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Appends `record`, reusing a vacant slot before growing.
    fn insert(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, record: ModuleRecord) -> Result<()> {
        // Reuse a vacant slot inside the high-water mark.
        for index in 0..self.count {
            if self.read_record(memory, index)?.module == NONE_ID {
                return self.write_record(memory, index, record);
            }
        }
        if self.count == self.capacity {
            self.grow(memory)?;
        }
        self.write_record(memory, self.count, record)?;
        self.count += 1;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Vacates the record at `index`, keeping its slot for reuse.
    fn remove(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, index: usize) -> Result<()> {
        self.write_record(memory, index, ModuleRecord::vacant())
    }

    /// Doubles the directory, copying the live records.
    fn grow(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let new_capacity = self.capacity * 2;
        let new_bytes = new_capacity * MODULE_RECORD_SIZE;
        let new_address = memory.allocate(self.space_id, new_bytes)?;
        memory.fill(new_address, 0, new_bytes, 0xFF)?;
        for index in 0..self.count {
            let mut buf = [0u8; MODULE_RECORD_SIZE];
            memory.read(self.address, index * MODULE_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
            memory.write(new_address, index * MODULE_RECORD_SIZE, &buf)?;
        }
        memory.deallocate(self.address)?;
        self.address = new_address;
        self.capacity = new_capacity;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Deallocates the directory storage.
    fn reclaim(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        memory.deallocate(self.address)
    }
}

/// The program's Global Entity Area (Phase 3D-5).
///
/// A coordinator over the frozen [`EntitySpace`] that owns the program's
/// global entity groups — one group per loaded module — and resolves
/// module-qualified `(ModuleId, GlobalIndex)` references deterministically
/// down to a [`Value`]. It owns only its own bookkeeping (the module→group
/// directory and the per-module index→cell directories), all allocated under
/// the Entity Space's id through the [`MemoryManager`]. It never owns a cell,
/// a value list, a binding or a value: cells come from the frozen
/// [`EntitySpace::allocate_cell`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::allocate_cell),
/// lists from the frozen
/// [`ValueList`](crate::value_list::ValueList), and every binding is embedded
/// by the frozen
/// [`EntitySpace::bind_value_list`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::bind_value_list).
///
/// The area borrows no component: every operation takes the [`MemoryManager`]
/// and, where an Entity Space operation is needed, the [`EntitySpace`] itself
/// — so the area can coexist with the local resolver
/// ([`LocalEntityResolver`](crate::local_entity::LocalEntityResolver)) and the
/// Runtime coordinates all mutations.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct GlobalEntityArea {
    /// The Entity Space this area serves; every allocation is Entity
    /// Space-scoped.
    space_id: SpaceId,
    /// The module→group directory.
    directory: ModuleDirectory,
}

impl GlobalEntityArea {
    /// Creates the program's global entity group coordinator under `entity`.
    ///
    /// Allocates the module→group directory under the Entity Space's id; no
    /// global groups exist until modules are loaded with
    /// [`GlobalEntityArea::load_module`].
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns manager errors when the directory cannot be allocated.
    pub fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager, entity: &EntitySpace) -> Result<GlobalEntityArea> {
        let space_id = entity.space_id();
        let directory = ModuleDirectory::new(memory, space_id)?;
        Ok(GlobalEntityArea {
            space_id,
            directory,
        })
    }

    /// Returns the [`SpaceId`] of the Entity Space this area serves.
    pub fn space_id(&self) -> SpaceId {
        self.space_id
    }

    /// Registers the global entity group of the loaded `module`.
    ///
    /// The group is sized from the module's static global count (`global_count`
    /// — compiler-produced data the Runtime Loader passes in; Program Space
    /// is never read here). The group's index→cell directory is allocated
    /// immediately; it grows on demand if more globals are allocated than
    /// declared. The module must not already have a group.
    ///
    /// The area treats `module` as an opaque key: whether the module is
    /// actually loaded in Program Space is a Runtime discipline, exactly like
    /// the local `CellId == EntityCellId` identity pairing.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `module` already has a global entity
    ///   group, or when `global_count` is too large to address.
    /// * Manager errors when the group directory cannot be allocated.
    pub fn load_module(
        &mut self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        module: ModuleId,
        global_count: usize,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let module_id = module.as_u32();
        if self.directory.find(memory, module_id)?.is_some() {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(format!(
                "module {module} already has a global entity group"
            )));
        }
        if global_count > u32::MAX as usize {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "module global count is too large to address".into(),
            ));
        }
        // At least one entry so the directory is a valid allocation; the
        // declared count sizes the initial capacity and growth is on demand.
        let entries = global_count.max(1);
        let bytes = entries
            .checked_mul(GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::InvalidArgument("global count is too large".into()))?;
        let directory = memory.allocate(self.space_id, bytes)?;
        // Every entry starts vacant (no allocated cell).
        memory.fill(directory, 0, bytes, 0xFF)?;
        let record = ModuleRecord {
            module: module_id,
            group: GroupMeta {
                directory,
                capacity: entries as u32,
                count: 0,
            },
        };
        self.directory.insert(memory, record)
    }

    /// Allocates one global entity in `module`'s group and returns its
    /// module-local compiled index.
    ///
    /// Allocates the entity cell from the frozen Entity Grid, creates a
    /// `capacity`-slot [`ValueList`] under the Entity Space's id, and binds it
    /// through the frozen Entity Space binding — the same storage chain locals
    /// use. On any failure the fresh cell and list are rolled back, so nothing
    /// leaks.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownModule`] when `module` has no global entity group.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `entity` is not the Entity Space this
    ///   area serves.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be allocated or written.
    pub fn allocate_global(
        &mut self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        entity: &mut EntitySpace,
        module: ModuleId,
        capacity: usize,
    ) -> Result<usize> {
        self.check_entity(entity)?;
        let (index, mut record) = self.require_group_index(memory, module)?;
        let group = record.group;
        let slot = group.count as usize;

        // Grow the group's index→cell directory on demand; the (possibly
        // grown) directory state is committed before any cell is allocated so
        // a later failure cannot leave a stale directory address behind.
        let group = if slot >= group.capacity as usize {
            let (directory, capacity) = grow_group_directory(memory, self.space_id, group)?;
            GroupMeta {
                directory,
                capacity,
                count: group.count,
            }
        } else {
            group
        };
        record.group = group;
        self.directory.write_record(memory, index, record)?;

        // Allocate the entity storage; every failure rolls back cleanly.
        let cell = entity.allocate_cell(memory)?;
        let list = match ValueList::new(memory, self.space_id, capacity) {
            Ok(list) => list,
            Err(error) => {
                entity.release_cell(memory, cell)?;
                return Err(error);
            }
        };
        if let Err(error) = entity.bind_value_list(memory, cell, &list) {
            list.destroy(memory)?;
            entity.release_cell(memory, cell)?;
            return Err(error);
        }
        if let Err(error) = write_group_entry(memory, group.directory, slot, cell.as_u32()) {
            list.destroy(memory)?;
            entity.release_cell(memory, cell)?;
            return Err(error);
        }

        // Commit the allocation: the new index is now resolvable.
        record.group.count += 1;
        self.directory.write_record(memory, index, record)?;
        Ok(slot)
    }

    /// Returns the Entity Cell id of the global entity at `module`'s compiled
    /// `index`.
    ///
    /// This is a lightweight query: it reads the group directory but does
    /// **not** verify the cell is live — the resolution paths
    /// ([`GlobalEntityArea::value_list`] and friends) validate that through
    /// Entity Space.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownModule`] when `module` has no global entity group.
    /// * [`Error::UnknownGlobalIndex`] when `index` is outside the module's
    ///   allocated global range.
    /// * Manager errors when the group directory cannot be read.
    pub fn global_cell(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        module: ModuleId,
        index: usize,
    ) -> Result<EntityCellId> {
        let group = self.require_group(memory, module)?.group;
        if index >= group.count as usize {
            return Err(Error::UnknownGlobalIndex { module, index });
        }
        let cell = read_group_entry(memory, group.directory, index)?;
        if cell == NONE_ID {
            return Err(Error::InvalidData(
                "global group entry is not allocated".into(),
            ));
        }
        Ok(EntityCellId::from_u32(cell))
    }

    /// Resolves the value list bound to the global entity at `module`'s
    /// compiled `index`.
    ///
    /// The list is resolved exclusively through
    /// [`EntitySpace::value_list`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::value_list);
    /// the runtime uses it for full list operations, including extended values
    /// (e.g. [`ValueList::set_string`](crate::value_list::ValueList::set_string)).
    /// The returned view is for reads and writes only — destroying a bound
    /// list must flow through
    /// [`GlobalEntityArea::destroy_module`], never through
    /// [`ValueList::destroy`](crate::value_list::ValueList::destroy) on the
    /// view.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`GlobalEntityArea::global_cell`].
    /// * [`Error::UnknownEntityCell`] when the global's Entity Cell is not
    ///   live.
    /// * [`Error::UnboundCell`] when the global's Entity Cell has no bound
    ///   value list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `entity` is not the Entity Space this
    ///   area serves.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be read.
    pub fn value_list(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        entity: &EntitySpace,
        module: ModuleId,
        index: usize,
    ) -> Result<ValueList> {
        self.check_entity(entity)?;
        let cell = self.global_cell(memory, module, index)?;
        entity.value_list(memory, cell)
    }

    /// Reads the value at the compiled `slot` of the global entity at
    /// `module`'s compiled `index`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`GlobalEntityArea::value_list`].
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the global's bound
    ///   list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidData`] when the stored record is corrupt.
    pub fn read_global(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        entity: &EntitySpace,
        module: ModuleId,
        index: usize,
        slot: usize,
    ) -> Result<Value> {
        self.value_list(memory, entity, module, index)?
            .get(memory, slot)
    }

    /// Writes `value` into the compiled `slot` of the global entity at
    /// `module`'s compiled `index`.
    ///
    /// Extended values must be written through the resolved list's dedicated
    /// methods (see [`GlobalEntityArea::value_list`]).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`GlobalEntityArea::value_list`].
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the global's bound
    ///   list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `value` is an extended handle.
    pub fn write_global(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        entity: &EntitySpace,
        module: ModuleId,
        index: usize,
        slot: usize,
        value: Value,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        self.value_list(memory, entity, module, index)?
            .set(memory, slot, value)
    }

    /// Destroys the global entity group of `module`.
    ///
    /// Every global's bound value list is destroyed first (releasing its
    /// extended content), then its cell is released back to the Entity Grid;
    /// finally the group's index→cell directory is reclaimed and the module's
    /// directory slot is vacated for reuse. The module is no longer resolvable
    /// afterwards.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownModule`] when `module` has no global entity group.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `entity` is not the Entity Space this
    ///   area serves.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be reclaimed or written.
    ///
    /// A failure partway through destroys the lists and cells already
    /// processed while leaving the module record and group directory in
    /// place; the partially torn-down group is then not retryable through
    /// this API. This is a detectable teardown state — exactly like
    /// [`EntitySpace::destroy`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::destroy) —
    /// never silent corruption: the orphaned Entity Space-scoped storage
    /// surfaces at manager shutdown or as [`Error::SpaceInUse`]. In a healthy
    /// system the per-item steps do not fail.
    pub fn destroy_module(
        &mut self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        entity: &mut EntitySpace,
        module: ModuleId,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        self.check_entity(entity)?;
        let (index, record) = self.require_group_index(memory, module)?;
        let group = record.group;
        // Destroy each global's list, then release its cell.
        for slot in 0..group.count as usize {
            let cell = read_group_entry(memory, group.directory, slot)?;
            if cell == NONE_ID {
                continue;
            }
            let cell = EntityCellId::from_u32(cell);
            entity.destroy_value_list(memory, cell)?;
            entity.release_cell(memory, cell)?;
        }
        memory.deallocate(group.directory)?;
        self.directory.remove(memory, index)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Destroys the Global Entity Area, reclaiming the module directory.
    ///
    /// Every module group must be destroyed first with
    /// [`GlobalEntityArea::destroy_module`]; destroying the area while groups
    /// are still loaded fails so that no group directory is orphaned. Because
    /// `destroy` consumes the area, a rejected destroy cannot be retried: the
    /// orphaned Entity Space-scoped storage is then reclaimed only at manager
    /// shutdown, which is detectable ([`Error::SpaceInUse`] or the shutdown
    /// report) and never silent. After a successful destroy the caller may
    /// destroy the Entity Space.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when module groups are still loaded.
    /// * Manager errors when the directory cannot be reclaimed.
    pub fn destroy(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let GlobalEntityArea { directory, .. } = self;
        for index in 0..directory.count {
            let record = directory.read_record(memory, index)?;
            if record.module != NONE_ID {
                return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                    "cannot destroy the global entity area while module groups are still loaded"
                        .into(),
                ));
            }
        }
        directory.reclaim(memory)
    }

    /// Returns the directory slot and live record for `module`.
    fn require_group_index(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        module: ModuleId,
    ) -> Result<(usize, ModuleRecord)> {
        let index = self
            .directory
            .find(memory, module.as_u32())?
            .ok_or(Error::UnknownModule(module))?;
        let record = self.directory.read_record(memory, index)?;
        Ok((index, record))
    }

    /// Returns the live module record for `module`.
    fn require_group(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, module: ModuleId) -> Result<ModuleRecord> {
        Ok(self.require_group_index(memory, module)?.1)
    }

    /// Verifies `entity` is the Entity Space this area serves.
    fn check_entity(&self, entity: &EntitySpace) -> Result<()> {
        if entity.space_id() != self.space_id {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "entity space does not match the global entity area".into(),
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// ---- codecs ----

/// Encodes a module-directory record as little-endian bytes.
fn encode_module_record(record: ModuleRecord) -> [u8; MODULE_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; MODULE_RECORD_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, 0, record.module);
    put_u32(&mut buf, 4, record.group.directory.region());
    put_u32(&mut buf, 8, record.group.directory.slot());
    put_u32(&mut buf, 12, record.group.directory.generation());
    put_u32(&mut buf, 16, record.group.capacity);
    put_u32(&mut buf, 20, record.group.count);
    buf
}

/// Decodes a module-directory record from little-endian bytes.
fn decode_module_record(buf: [u8; MODULE_RECORD_SIZE]) -> ModuleRecord {
    ModuleRecord {
        module: get_u32(&buf, 0),
        group: GroupMeta {
            directory: LogicalAddress::from_parts(
                get_u32(&buf, 4),
                get_u32(&buf, 8),
                get_u32(&buf, 12),
            ),
            capacity: get_u32(&buf, 16),
            count: get_u32(&buf, 20),
        },
    }
}

/// Reads the cell id recorded at global `index` of a group directory.
fn read_group_entry(
    memory: &MemoryManager,
    directory: LogicalAddress,
    index: usize,
) -> Result<u32> {
    let mut buf = [0u8; GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE];
    memory.read(directory, index * GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
    Ok(get_u32(&buf, 0))
}

/// Writes the cell id of global `index` into a group directory.
fn write_group_entry(
    memory: &mut MemoryManager,
    directory: LogicalAddress,
    index: usize,
    cell: u32,
) -> Result<()> {
    let mut buf = [0u8; GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, 0, cell);
    memory.write(directory, index * GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE, &buf)
}

/// Doubles a group's index→cell directory, copying the allocated entries and
/// returning the new storage address and capacity.
fn grow_group_directory(
    memory: &mut MemoryManager,
    space_id: SpaceId,
    group: GroupMeta,
) -> Result<(LogicalAddress, u32)> {
    let new_capacity = (group.capacity as usize)
        .checked_mul(2)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::InvalidArgument("global group is too large".into()))?;
    let bytes = new_capacity
        .checked_mul(GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::InvalidArgument("global group is too large".into()))?;
    let address = memory.allocate(space_id, bytes)?;
    memory.fill(address, 0, bytes, 0xFF)?;
    for index in 0..group.count as usize {
        let mut buf = [0u8; GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE];
        memory.read(group.directory, index * GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        memory.write(address, index * GROUP_ENTRY_SIZE, &buf)?;
    }
    memory.deallocate(group.directory)?;
    Ok((address, new_capacity as u32))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Builds an Entity Space and a fresh area with `module` loaded.
    fn setup() -> (MemoryManager, EntitySpace, GlobalEntityArea, ModuleId) {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut area = GlobalEntityArea::new(&mut memory, &entity).unwrap();
        let module = ModuleId::from_u32(1);
        area.load_module(&mut memory, module, 2).unwrap();
        (memory, entity, area, module)
    }

    #[test]
    fn new_allocates_the_module_directory_under_the_entity_space() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        // Entity Space baseline: directory + first grid block.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 2);

        let area = GlobalEntityArea::new(&mut memory, &entity).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(area.space_id(), entity.space_id());
        // +1 for the area's module directory.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(), 3);

        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn load_module_creates_a_group_and_rejects_duplicates() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut area = GlobalEntityArea::new(&mut memory, &entity).unwrap();
        let module = ModuleId::from_u32(7);
        let before = memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations();

        area.load_module(&mut memory, module, 3).unwrap();
        // +1 for the group's index→cell directory.
        assert_eq!(
            memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(),
            before + 1
        );

        assert!(matches!(
            area.load_module(&mut memory, module, 1),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn allocate_global_binds_cells_and_returns_indices_in_order() {
        let (mut memory, mut entity, mut area, module) = setup();
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 0);

        let x = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 2)
            .unwrap();
        let y = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!((x, y), (0, 1));
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 2);
        // Both cells are live and bound to a list through Entity Space.
        let cx = area.global_cell(&memory, module, x).unwrap();
        let cy = area.global_cell(&memory, module, y).unwrap();
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, cx).unwrap());
        assert!(entity.is_live(&memory, cy).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(entity.value_list(&memory, cx).unwrap().capacity(), 2);
        assert_eq!(entity.value_list(&memory, cy).unwrap().capacity(), 1);

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn read_and_write_resolve_compiled_slots_deterministically() {
        let (mut memory, mut entity, mut area, module) = setup();
        let x = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 2)
            .unwrap();
        let y = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1)
            .unwrap();

        // Compiled slots: x's list holds two fields.
        area.write_global(&mut memory, &entity, module, x, 0, Value::Int(5))
            .unwrap();
        area.write_global(&mut memory, &entity, module, x, 1, Value::Bool(true))
            .unwrap();
        area.write_global(&mut memory, &entity, module, y, 0, Value::Float(1.5))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, x, 0).unwrap(),
            Value::Int(5)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, x, 1).unwrap(),
            Value::Bool(true)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, y, 0).unwrap(),
            Value::Float(1.5)
        );

        // The write flowed through Entity Space's bound list: the resolved
        // view observes the same storage.
        let cell = area.global_cell(&memory, module, x).unwrap();
        let view = entity.value_list(&memory, cell).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(view.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(5));

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn global_slots_are_bounds_checked_and_extended_handles_rejected() {
        let (mut memory, mut entity, mut area, module) = setup();
        let x = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1)
            .unwrap();

        // The global's list has one slot: slot 1 is out of bounds.
        assert!(matches!(
            area.write_global(&mut memory, &entity, module, x, 1, Value::Int(1)),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, x, 7),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));

        // Extended handles cannot be written through the primitive path.
        let cell = area.global_cell(&memory, module, x).unwrap();
        let view = entity.value_list(&memory, cell).unwrap();
        view.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "abc").unwrap();
        let handle = view.get(&memory, 0).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            area.write_global(&mut memory, &entity, module, x, 0, handle),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        // The rejected write left the slot untouched.
        assert_eq!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, x, 0)
                .unwrap()
                .category(),
            "string"
        );

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn extended_values_reach_globals_through_the_resolved_list() {
        let (mut memory, mut entity, mut area, module) = setup();
        let x = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1)
            .unwrap();

        let view = area.value_list(&memory, &entity, module, x).unwrap();
        view.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "greeting").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(view.read_string(&memory, 0).unwrap(), "greeting");
        assert_eq!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, x, 0)
                .unwrap()
                .category(),
            "string"
        );

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_module_and_index_are_detected() {
        let (mut memory, mut entity, mut area, module) = setup();
        let missing = ModuleId::from_u32(99);

        // A module that was never loaded.
        assert!(matches!(
            area.global_cell(&memory, missing, 0),
            Err(Error::UnknownModule(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, missing, 0, 0),
            Err(Error::UnknownModule(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            area.allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, missing, 1),
            Err(Error::UnknownModule(_))
        ));

        // An index outside the module's allocated range.
        assert!(matches!(
            area.global_cell(&memory, module, 2),
            Err(Error::UnknownGlobalIndex { index: 2, .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, 2, 0),
            Err(Error::UnknownGlobalIndex { .. })
        ));

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn multiple_modules_are_isolated() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut area = GlobalEntityArea::new(&mut memory, &entity).unwrap();
        let main = ModuleId::from_u32(1);
        let util = ModuleId::from_u32(2);
        area.load_module(&mut memory, main, 1).unwrap();
        area.load_module(&mut memory, util, 1).unwrap();

        let m = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, main, 1)
            .unwrap();
        let u = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, util, 1)
            .unwrap();
        area.write_global(&mut memory, &entity, main, m, 0, Value::Int(10))
            .unwrap();
        area.write_global(&mut memory, &entity, util, u, 0, Value::Int(20))
            .unwrap();

        // Same index, different modules: independent storage.
        assert_eq!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, main, m, 0).unwrap(),
            Value::Int(10)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, util, u, 0).unwrap(),
            Value::Int(20)
        );
        assert_ne!(
            area.global_cell(&memory, main, m).unwrap(),
            area.global_cell(&memory, util, u).unwrap()
        );

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, main).unwrap();
        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, util).unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn group_directory_grows_on_demand() {
        let (mut memory, mut entity, mut area, module) = setup();
        // load_module declared 2 globals; allocate beyond the declaration.
        for _ in 0..5 {
            area.allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1)
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 5);
        for index in 0..5 {
            area.write_global(
                &mut memory,
                &entity,
                module,
                index,
                0,
                Value::Int(index as i64),
            )
            .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(
                area.read_global(&memory, &entity, module, index, 0)
                    .unwrap(),
                Value::Int(index as i64)
            );
        }

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn destroy_module_releases_cells_lists_and_directories() {
        let (mut memory, mut entity, mut area, module) = setup();
        // `setup` already allocated the area's module directory and the
        // module's group directory, so `before` includes both.
        let before = memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations();
        area.allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1)
            .unwrap();
        area.allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 2)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 2);
        // before + two lists (one per global; the group directory pre-exists).
        assert_eq!(
            memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(),
            before + 2
        );

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        // Lists and the group directory reclaimed: the setup baseline minus
        // the module's group directory (which `before` includes).
        assert_eq!(
            memory.space_usage(entity.space_id()).allocations(),
            before - 1
        );
        assert_eq!(entity.cell_count(), 0);
        // The module is no longer resolvable.
        assert!(matches!(
            area.global_cell(&memory, module, 0),
            Err(Error::UnknownModule(_))
        ));

        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn destroy_rejects_while_groups_are_loaded_and_leaks_detectably() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut area = GlobalEntityArea::new(&mut memory, &entity).unwrap();
        let module = ModuleId::from_u32(1);
        area.load_module(&mut memory, module, 1).unwrap();
        area.allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, module, 1)
            .unwrap();

        // Destroying the area while a module group is loaded is rejected,
        // not silent: the consumed area leaves its Entity Space-scoped
        // storage behind, so the Entity Space refuses to unregister.
        assert!(matches!(
            area.destroy(&mut memory),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            entity.destroy(&mut memory),
            Err(Error::SpaceInUse { .. })
        ));
        // The orphaned storage is exactly the area's module directory, the
        // module's group directory and the bound list (the failed Entity
        // Space destroy already reclaimed the grid blocks).
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn module_directory_reuses_vacant_slots_before_growing() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut area = GlobalEntityArea::new(&mut memory, &entity).unwrap();
        let main = ModuleId::from_u32(1);
        let util = ModuleId::from_u32(2);
        let other = ModuleId::from_u32(3);
        area.load_module(&mut memory, main, 1).unwrap();
        area.load_module(&mut memory, util, 1).unwrap();
        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, main).unwrap();

        // The next load reuses the vacated slot (no directory growth).
        area.load_module(&mut memory, other, 1).unwrap();
        let o = area
            .allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut entity, other, 1)
            .unwrap();
        area.write_global(&mut memory, &entity, other, o, 0, Value::Int(3))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &entity, other, o, 0).unwrap(),
            Value::Int(3)
        );

        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, util).unwrap();
        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, other)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrong_entity_space_is_rejected() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut other = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut area = GlobalEntityArea::new(&mut memory, &entity).unwrap();
        let module = ModuleId::from_u32(1);
        area.load_module(&mut memory, module, 1).unwrap();

        assert!(matches!(
            area.allocate_global(&mut memory, &mut other, module, 1),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            area.read_global(&memory, &other, module, 0, 0),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut other, module),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));

        other.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        area.destroy_module(&mut memory, &mut entity, module)
            .unwrap();
        area.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn module_records_round_trip_through_the_codec() {
        let group = GroupMeta {
            directory: LogicalAddress::from_parts(2, 9, 4),
            capacity: 3,
            count: 2,
        };
        let record = ModuleRecord { module: 7, group };
        assert_eq!(decode_module_record(encode_module_record(record)).module, 7);
        assert_eq!(
            decode_module_record(encode_module_record(record))
                .group
                .directory,
            group.directory
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_module_record(encode_module_record(record))
                .group
                .capacity,
            3
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_module_record(encode_module_record(record))
                .group
                .count,
            2
        );

        let vacant = ModuleRecord::vacant();
        assert_eq!(vacant.module, NONE_ID);
        assert_eq!(vacant.group.count, 0);
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn global_entity_area_is_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<GlobalEntityArea>();
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\lib.rs
//! `ra-memory`: the memory manager of the RA Software Platform.
//!
//! **Phase 3 — Memory Manager · STATUS: FROZEN. Phase 3B — Program Space.
//! Phase 3C — Active Space. ✅ Phase 3D-1 — Entity Manager (Entity Grid).
//! ✅ Phase 3D-2 — Indexed Value List. ✅ Phase 3D-3 — Extended Value
//! Storage. ✅ Phase 3D-4 — Local Entity Resolution. ✅ Phase 3D-5 — Global
//! Entity Area. ⏳ Phase 3D-6 — Debug Metadata (optional).**
//! This crate implements the **Memory Manager** (Phase 3, frozen),
//! **Program Space (PS)** (Phase 3B), **Active Space (AS)** (Phase 3C) and,
//! for **Entity Space (ES)**, the **Entity Manager (Entity Grid)** (Phase 3D-1),
//! the **Indexed Value List** (Phase 3D-2), the **Extended Value Storage**
//! (Phase 3D-3) and **Local Entity Resolution** (Phase 3D-4) of the RA
//! Memory architecture.
//! Only the implementation decisions listed under *Implementation
//! assumptions* below may evolve in future versions.
//!
//! # Frozen architecture
//!
//! RA Memory is organized as a strict hierarchy:
//!
//! ```text
//!                    MEMORY MANAGER            (this crate — sole owner of
//!                             │                 RA Memory)
//!                             ▼
//!             LOGICAL MEMORY CONTROLLER         (logical addresses, allocation,
//!                             │                 deallocation, lookup, ownership)
//!                             ▼
//!     ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
//!     │   PS     │    AS    │    ES    │    WS    │    RS    │
//!     │ Program  │  Active  │  Entity  │   Work   │ Registry │
//!     └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘
//! ```
//!
//! The following ownership rules are **frozen**:
//!
//! * **The Memory Manager is the sole owner of RA Memory.** It owns all host
//!   memory (regions), all allocation metadata, and the space registry.
//! * **The Runtime never allocates host memory directly.** It obtains all
//!   memory through the manager.
//! * **Memory Spaces never allocate host memory directly.** They hold only
//!   logical contents — addresses and the data at those addresses.
//! * **All memory allocation flows through the Memory Manager.**
//!
//! # Frozen architectural invariant
//!
//! The following invariant is **frozen** — it binds every component that
//! assigns or reuses module identifiers, and no implementation may weaken
//! it:
//!
//! * A [`ModuleId`] must never be reused while its **GlobalEntityGroup**
//!   still exists.
//! * The lifetime of a **ModuleGlobalGroup** is **exactly** the lifetime of
//!   the loaded module.
//! * A **ModuleGlobalGroup** must always be **destroyed** before that
//!   [`ModuleId`] can be reused.
//!
//! In this crate's terms, the GlobalEntityGroup / ModuleGlobalGroup of a
//! loaded module is the module's global entity group in the Global Entity
//! Area — created with [`GlobalEntityArea::load_module`] and destroyed with
//! [`GlobalEntityArea::destroy_module`] (see the [`global_entity`] module).
//!
//! # Ownership map
//!
//! The frozen division of ownership:
//!
//! | Owner | Owns |
//! |---|---|
//! | [`MemoryManager`] | all RA memory: host regions, allocation metadata, the space registry |
//! | [`ProgramSpace`] | executable structure: module metadata, REI, constants, the code map |
//! | [`ActiveSpace`] | execution identity: the live call chain, scope ids, REI positions |
//! | [`EntitySpace`] | execution values: the Entity Grid cells, their value lists, and the `EntityCell → ValueList` binding |
//! | the **Runtime** | no memory — it coordinates through the manager and the spaces |
//!
//! Entity Space's ownership of the cells, their [`ValueList`]s and the
//! `EntityCell → ValueList` binding is **exclusive**: a list handle can only
//! be obtained from a live cell's embedded metadata, never fabricated. The
//! `CellId == EntityCellId` identity pairing is a **Runtime invariant**, kept
//! by the Runtime's paired allocate/release discipline (see [`local_entity`]).
//!
//! # Execution flow
//!
//! Runtime memory is consumed along a fixed chain — the program loads into
//! Program Space, Active Space tracks the live execution path, Entity Space
//! holds the current invocation's values, and [`LocalEntityResolver`] turns a
//! compiled slot of the current invocation into a [`Value`]:
//!
//! ```text
//! ProgramSpace → ActiveSpace → EntitySpace → LocalEntityResolver → Value
//! ```
//!
//! Globals follow the same lower half of the chain without an Active Cell
//! anchor: `(ModuleId, GlobalIndex)` → the Global Entity Area
//! ([`global_entity`]) → Entity Cell → Value List → Value.
//!
//! The five memory spaces of the frozen architecture — Program Space (PS),
//! Active Space (AS), Entity Space (ES), Work Space (WS) and Registry Space
//! (RS) — are defined as [`SpaceKind`]s and are registered with the manager.
//! **Program Space** (see the [`program_space`] module), **Active Space**
//! (see the [`active_space`] module) and the **Entity Manager / Entity Grid**
//! of **Entity Space** (see the [`entity_space`] module, Phase 3D-1), the
//! **Indexed Value List** (see the [`value_list`] module, Phase 3D-2), its
//! **Extended Value Storage** — strings, arrays and objects, Phase 3D-3 — and
//! **Local Entity Resolution** (see the [`local_entity`] module, Phase 3D-4)
//! and the **Global Entity Area** (see the [`global_entity`] module, Phase
//! 3D-5) are implemented in this crate as clients of the manager; ⏳ debug
//! metadata (3D-6) of Entity Space, and the internal layouts of Work and
//! Registry Spaces, are **not** implemented here — that is the responsibility
//! of later phases. REI/runtime execution belongs to the Runtime, not to this
//! crate.
//!
//! # Runtime Loader contract
//!
//! Ownership is divided between the Runtime Loader and the Memory Manager.
//! Per the Execution Workflow document, the Runtime Loader is the only
//! component that populates runtime memory:
//!
//! | Owned by the **Runtime Loader** | Owned by the **Memory Manager** |
//! |---|---|
//! | the `MemoryManager` instance | logical addresses |
//! | space creation (`register_space`) | allocation |
//! | space destruction (`unregister_space` / `shutdown`) | deallocation |
//! | | region management (grow / shrink) |
//! | | space registration |
//! | | ownership tracking |
//!
//! Memory Spaces own **logical contents only** — they never own physical
//! memory.
//!
//! # What the manager does
//!
//! The manager owns the lifecycle of all memory spaces: initialization,
//! shutdown, space registration, allocation, deallocation, lookup and
//! ownership tracking. Per the Memory Architecture document it:
//!
//! * begins with **zero** committed regions and **grows on demand**;
//! * **reuses** released memory aggressively before growing;
//! * hands out compact **logical addresses** — `[region | slot | generation]`
//!   ([`LogicalAddress`]) — never raw native pointers, with **generations**
//!   detecting stale references after a slot is reused;
//! * keeps only the metadata required to manage storage safely (size,
//!   liveness, generation, owning space) — **no database relationships**;
//! * returns idle trailing regions to the host when practical
//!   ([`MemoryManager::release_idle_regions`]).
//!
//! # Implementation assumptions (not frozen)
//!
//! The following are **implementation decisions** of this version, not frozen
//! architectural decisions. They may change in a future version without an
//! architecture change:
//!
//! * **first-fit allocation** policy;
//! * **fixed slot size** (default 64 bytes) with slot-granular sizing;
//! * **region size** (default 64 KiB) and the 65 536-region safety cap;
//! * **generation width** (`u32`, wrapping);
//! * **zero-on-free** (default on);
//! * **no cross-region allocations** — an allocation never spans regions.
//!
//! # Future memory objects
//!
//! The byte-oriented allocation interface — [`MemoryManager::allocate`] with
//! `bytes`, plus `read` / `write` / `fill` — is intentionally the **V1
//! implementation interface**. Future versions may expose higher-level
//! allocation APIs (for example typed memory objects or a layout-style
//! interface) **on top of the existing manager, without changing the
//! underlying manager**.
//!
//! # Future region allocator
//!
//! The region allocator behind the manager (the internal `region` module) is
//! currently a **private** component. The architecture allows it to become a
//! separate internal component in a future version without affecting the
//! public API. It is deliberately **not exposed publicly**.
//!
//! # Zero-copy deferral
//!
//! [`MemoryManager::read`] and [`MemoryManager::write`] are copy-based.
//! Zero-copy access is **intentionally deferred** to a future version because
//! safety and deterministic behavior take priority.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_memory::{MemoryManager, SpaceKind};
//!
//! let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
//! let entity = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);
//!
//! let address = memory.allocate(entity, 64).unwrap();
//! memory.write(address, 0, b"hello").unwrap();
//!
//! let mut buf = [0u8; 5];
//! memory.read(address, 0, &mut buf).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(&buf, b"hello");
//! assert_eq!(memory.owner(address).unwrap(), entity);
//!
//! memory.deallocate(address).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
//! ```

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
// Every public item must carry documentation (RA implementation rule 7):
// a missing doc comment is a hard error, not a warning.
#![deny(missing_docs)]

};

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\local_entity.rs
//! ✅ Local Entity Resolution — Phase 3D-4.
//!
//! Per the approved Local Entity Resolution architecture, a local variable
//! access resolves deterministically down the ownership chain:
//!
//! ```text
//! Active Cell  →  Entity Cell  →  Value List  →  Compiled Slot  →  Value
//! ```
//!
//! * the **Active Cell** ([`CellId`]) identifies the current invocation;
//! * under the **identity pairing** the invocation's Entity Cell id equals
//!   the Active Cell id (`EntityCellId == CellId`), maintained by the
//!   Runtime's paired allocate/release discipline;
//! * the **Entity Cell → Value List** binding is owned **exclusively by
//!   Entity Space** (embedded in the live-cell record) and is resolved only
//!   through [`EntitySpace::value_list`] — this module never bypasses Entity
//!   Space and never exposes binding metadata;
//! * the **compiled slot** is chosen by the compiler (§4: source names → slots)
//!   and the [`ValueList`] provides direct positional access (§11) with
//!   bounds checking;
//! * the **Value** is the primitive or extended value stored at that slot.
//!
//! This module implements only **deterministic compiled-slot resolution**:
//! local value reads and writes anchored on the current invocation. It does
//! **not** implement global entities — that is ✅ Phase 3D-5, implemented in
//! the [`global_entity`](crate::global_entity) module — nor name/symbol
//! lookup, dynamic scope search, ⏳ debug metadata (3D-6), reflection, or
//! REI/runtime execution — those belong to later phases or to the Runtime.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_memory::{
//!     ActiveSpace, EntitySpace, LocalEntityResolver, MemoryManager, ScopeId, Value, ValueList,
//! };
//!
//! let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
//! let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
//!
//! // Scope entry: the Runtime enters the scope, allocates its Entity Cell
//! // (identity pairing: the Entity Cell id equals the Active Cell id) and
//! // binds exactly one value list to it.
//! let cell = active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(1), 0).unwrap();
//! let entity_cell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(entity_cell.as_u32(), cell.as_u32());
//! let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, entity.space_id(), 2).unwrap();
//! entity.bind_value_list(&mut memory, entity_cell, &list).unwrap();
//!
//! // Deterministic compiled-slot access on the current invocation.
//! let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);
//! resolver.write_local(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(5)).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(5));
//!
//! // Scope exit: destroy the list, release the cell, close the scope.
//! entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, entity_cell).unwrap();
//! entity.release_cell(&mut memory, entity_cell).unwrap();
//! active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
//!
//! entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
//! ```

use crate::active_space::ActiveSpace;
use crate::entity_space::{EntityCellId, EntitySpace};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::manager::MemoryManager;
use crate::value_list::{Value, ValueList};

/// Local Entity Resolution (Phase 3D-4).
///
/// A borrowed coordinator over the frozen [`ActiveSpace`] and [`EntitySpace`]
/// that resolves a local variable access from the current invocation's
/// Active Cell down to the [`Value`] at a compiled slot. It owns nothing:
/// the `EntityCell → ValueList` binding stays owned by Entity Space, and
/// every access flows through [`EntitySpace::value_list`], so binding
/// metadata is never exposed.
///
/// Resolution is deterministic: the current Active Cell identifies the
/// invocation, the identity pairing maps it to the Entity Cell, the cell
/// record resolves the bound list, and the compiled slot is a direct
/// positional access — no name, symbol or dynamic scope search.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct LocalEntityResolver<'a> {
    /// The Active Space anchoring the current invocation.
    active: &'a ActiveSpace,
    /// The Entity Space owning the cell↔list binding.
    entity: &'a EntitySpace,
}

impl<'a> LocalEntityResolver<'a> {
    /// Creates a resolver over `active` and `entity`.
    pub fn new(active: &'a ActiveSpace, entity: &'a EntitySpace) -> LocalEntityResolver<'a> {
        LocalEntityResolver { active, entity }
    }

    /// Returns the Entity Cell id of the current invocation.
    ///
    /// Under the identity pairing the invocation's Entity Cell id equals its
    /// Active Cell id; `None` when the call chain is empty. This is a
    /// lightweight query: it does **not** verify the Entity Cell is live —
    /// the resolution paths ([`LocalEntityResolver::value_list`] and
    /// friends) validate that through Entity Space.
    pub fn current_cell(&self) -> Option<EntityCellId> {
        self.active
            .current_cell()
            .map(|cell| EntityCellId::from_u32(cell.as_u32()))
    }

    /// Resolves the current invocation's bound value list.
    ///
    /// The list is resolved exclusively through
    /// [`EntitySpace::value_list`]; the runtime uses it for full list
    /// operations, including extended values (e.g.
    /// [`ValueList::set_string`]).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::EmptyActiveSpace`] when there is no live invocation.
    /// * [`Error::UnknownEntityCell`] when the invocation's Entity Cell is
    ///   not live.
    /// * [`Error::UnboundCell`] when the invocation's Entity Cell has no
    ///   bound value list.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be read.
    pub fn value_list(&self, memory: &MemoryManager) -> Result<ValueList> {
        let cell = self.require_cell()?;
        self.entity.value_list(memory, cell)
    }

    /// Reads the local value at the compiled `slot` of the current
    /// invocation.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`LocalEntityResolver::value_list`].
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the bound list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidData`] when the stored record is corrupt.
    pub fn read_local(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, slot: usize) -> Result<Value> {
        self.value_list(memory)?.get(memory, slot)
    }

    /// Writes `value` into the compiled `slot` of the current invocation.
    ///
    /// Extended values must be written through the resolved list's dedicated
    /// methods (see [`LocalEntityResolver::value_list`]).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`LocalEntityResolver::value_list`].
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the bound list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `value` is an extended handle.
    pub fn write_local(&self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, slot: usize, value: Value) -> Result<()> {
        self.value_list(memory)?.set(memory, slot, value)
    }

    /// Returns the current invocation's Entity Cell id, or
    /// [`Error::EmptyActiveSpace`] when the call chain is empty.
    fn require_cell(&self) -> Result<EntityCellId> {
        self.current_cell().ok_or(Error::EmptyActiveSpace)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::active_space::ScopeId;

    /// Enters `scope` and returns the active cell id of the new invocation.
    fn enter_scope(memory: &mut MemoryManager, active: &mut ActiveSpace) -> u32 {
        active
            .call(memory, ScopeId::from_u32(1), 0)
            .unwrap()
            .as_u32()
    }

    /// Binds a `capacity`-slot list to the live Entity Cell `ecell`.
    fn bind_list(
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        entity: &mut EntitySpace,
        ecell: EntityCellId,
        capacity: usize,
    ) -> ValueList {
        let list = ValueList::new(memory, entity.space_id(), capacity).unwrap();
        entity.bind_value_list(memory, ecell, &list).unwrap();
        list
    }

    #[test]
    fn current_cell_reflects_the_identity_pairing() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();

        // No live invocation yet.
        assert_eq!(
            LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity).current_cell(),
            None
        );

        // After a call, the invocation's Entity Cell id equals the Active
        // Cell id.
        let cell = enter_scope(&mut memory, &mut active);
        assert_eq!(
            LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity).current_cell(),
            Some(EntityCellId::from_u32(cell))
        );

        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity).current_cell(),
            None
        );

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn read_and_write_resolve_compiled_slots_deterministically() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();

        let cell = enter_scope(&mut memory, &mut active);
        let ecell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ecell.as_u32(), cell); // identity pairing
        bind_list(&mut memory, &mut entity, ecell, 2);

        let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);

        // Compiled slots: x → 0, y → 1.
        resolver.write_local(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(5)).unwrap();
        resolver
            .write_local(&mut memory, 1, Value::Bool(true))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(5));
        assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 1).unwrap(), Value::Bool(true));

        // The write flowed through Entity Space's bound list: the resolved
        // view observes the same storage.
        let view = entity.value_list(&memory, ecell).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(view.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(5));

        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, ecell).unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, ecell).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn slot_access_is_bounds_checked_through_resolution() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();

        enter_scope(&mut memory, &mut active);
        let ecell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        bind_list(&mut memory, &mut entity, ecell, 2);
        let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);

        assert!(matches!(
            resolver.write_local(&mut memory, 2, Value::Int(1)),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            resolver.read_local(&memory, 7),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));

        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, ecell).unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, ecell).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_local_rejects_extended_handles() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();

        enter_scope(&mut memory, &mut active);
        let ecell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let list = bind_list(&mut memory, &mut entity, ecell, 2);
        let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);

        // Extended values are written through the resolved list's dedicated
        // methods, never through the compiled-slot primitive path.
        list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "abc").unwrap();
        let handle = list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            resolver.write_local(&mut memory, 1, handle),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        // The rejected write left the slot untouched.
        assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 1).unwrap(), Value::Nil);

        entity.destroy_value_list(&mut memory, ecell).unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, ecell).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolution_requires_a_live_invocation() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);

        assert!(matches!(
            resolver.value_list(&memory),
            Err(Error::EmptyActiveSpace)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            resolver.read_local(&memory, 0),
            Err(Error::EmptyActiveSpace)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            resolver.write_local(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(1)),
            Err(Error::EmptyActiveSpace)
        ));

        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolution_fails_when_the_entity_cell_is_missing_or_unbound() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        enter_scope(&mut memory, &mut active);

        // The invocation's Entity Cell was never allocated.
        {
            let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);
            assert!(matches!(
                resolver.read_local(&memory, 0),
                Err(Error::UnknownEntityCell(_))
            ));
        }

        // The Entity Cell is live but has no bound list.
        let ecell = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        {
            let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);
            assert!(matches!(
                resolver.read_local(&memory, 0),
                Err(Error::UnboundCell(_))
            ));
        }

        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, ecell).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn repeated_invocations_of_a_scope_resolve_independently() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();

        // First invocation: x = 1.
        let first_cell = enter_scope(&mut memory, &mut active);
        let first_entity = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(first_entity.as_u32(), first_cell);
        bind_list(&mut memory, &mut entity, first_entity, 1);
        {
            let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);
            resolver.write_local(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(1)).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(1));
        }
        entity
            .destroy_value_list(&mut memory, first_entity)
            .unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, first_entity).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();

        // Second invocation reuses the same cells: a fresh list, so the
        // local resolves to the new value, deterministically.
        let second_cell = enter_scope(&mut memory, &mut active);
        let second_entity = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(second_entity.as_u32(), second_cell); // identity pairing
        assert_eq!(second_entity, first_entity); // reused
        bind_list(&mut memory, &mut entity, second_entity, 1);
        {
            let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);
            // The previous invocation's value is gone.
            assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Nil);
            resolver.write_local(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(2)).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(2));
        }
        entity
            .destroy_value_list(&mut memory, second_entity)
            .unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, second_entity).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();

        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn nested_invocations_resolve_against_the_current_invocation() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut active = ActiveSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let mut entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();

        // Outer invocation (scope 1) lands at active cell 0; identity
        // pairing allocates its Entity Cell at 0 and binds a one-slot list.
        let outer_active = active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(1), 0).unwrap();
        let outer_entity = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(outer_entity.as_u32(), outer_active.as_u32());
        bind_list(&mut memory, &mut entity, outer_entity, 1);
        {
            let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);
            resolver
                .write_local(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(10))
                .unwrap();
        }

        // Inner invocation (scope 2) lands at active cell 1; its Entity Cell
        // is allocated at 1 and gets its own list.
        let inner_active = active.call(&mut memory, ScopeId::from_u32(2), 0).unwrap();
        let inner_entity = entity.allocate_cell(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(inner_entity.as_u32(), inner_active.as_u32());
        bind_list(&mut memory, &mut entity, inner_entity, 1);

        // Resolution anchors deterministically on the current (top-of-chain)
        // invocation: the inner list is fresh, the outer value is untouched.
        {
            let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);
            assert_eq!(resolver.current_cell(), Some(inner_entity));
            assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Nil);
            resolver
                .write_local(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(20))
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(20));
            let outer_view = entity.value_list(&memory, outer_entity).unwrap();
