            assert_eq!(outer_view.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(10));
        }

        // Return from the inner scope: resolution follows the chain back to
        // the outer invocation.
        entity
            .destroy_value_list(&mut memory, inner_entity)
            .unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, inner_entity).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        {
            let resolver = LocalEntityResolver::new(&active, &entity);
            assert_eq!(resolver.current_cell(), Some(outer_entity));
            assert_eq!(resolver.read_local(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(10));
        }

        entity
            .destroy_value_list(&mut memory, outer_entity)
            .unwrap();
        entity.release_cell(&mut memory, outer_entity).unwrap();
        active.close(&mut memory).unwrap();
        entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        active.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn local_entity_resolver_is_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<LocalEntityResolver<'static>>();
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\manager.rs
//! The RA Memory Manager — the **sole owner of RA Memory**.
//!
//! The Memory Manager owns the lifecycle of every memory space:
//!
//! * **initialization** — [`MemoryManager::new`] /
//!   [`MemoryManager::with_config`] create an empty memory system;
//! * **shutdown** — [`MemoryManager::shutdown`] destroys all regions and
//!   reports what was released;
//! * **space registration** — spaces register with
//!   [`MemoryManager::register_space`] and are looked up or unregistered;
//! * **allocation** — [`MemoryManager::allocate`] hands out
//!   [`LogicalAddress`]es;
//! * **deallocation** — [`MemoryManager::deallocate`] reclaims an allocation
//!   and makes its slots immediately reusable;
//! * **lookup** — [`MemoryManager::lookup`], [`MemoryManager::read`] and
//!   [`MemoryManager::write`] resolve addresses to live allocations;
//! * **ownership tracking** — every allocation belongs to exactly one space
//!   ([`MemoryManager::owner`], [`MemoryManager::space_usage`]).
//!
//! Host memory is acquired in **regions** that grow on demand; idle trailing
//! regions can be returned to the host with
//! [`MemoryManager::release_idle_regions`]. This is the `Allocate → Address →
//! Access → Reclaim → Reuse` lifecycle of the Memory Architecture document.
//!
//! # Ownership contract
//!
//! These rules are **frozen**:
//!
//! * The Memory Manager is the **sole owner of RA Memory**. It owns all host
//!   memory (regions), all allocation metadata, and the space registry.
//! * The **Runtime never allocates host memory directly** — it obtains all
//!   memory through this manager.
//! * **Memory Spaces never allocate host memory directly** — they hold only
//!   logical contents.
//! * **All memory allocation flows through this manager.**
//!
//! The **Runtime Loader** owns the `MemoryManager` instance plus space
//! creation and destruction. The **manager** owns logical addresses,
//! allocation, deallocation, region management, space registration and
//! ownership tracking. Memory Spaces own **logical contents only** and never
//! own physical memory.

use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::region::Region;
use crate::space::{SpaceId, SpaceKind, SpaceRecord};

/// Configuration of a [`MemoryManager`].
///
/// The defaults follow the Memory Architecture size policy: memory begins
/// with zero committed regions, grows on demand, and reuses released memory
/// aggressively.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryManagerConfig {
    region_size: usize,
    slot_size: usize,
    max_regions: usize,
    zero_on_deallocate: bool,
}

impl MemoryManagerConfig {
    /// The default configuration: 64 KiB regions divided into 64-byte slots,
    /// up to 65 536 regions, with released bytes zeroed.
    pub fn new() -> MemoryManagerConfig {
        MemoryManagerConfig::default()
    }

    /// Returns the size in bytes of a single region.
    pub fn region_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.region_size
    }

    /// Returns the size in bytes of a single slot.
    pub fn slot_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.slot_size
    }

    /// Returns the maximum number of regions the manager may grow to.
    pub fn max_regions(&self) -> usize {
        self.max_regions
    }

    /// Returns whether released bytes are zeroed on deallocation.
    pub fn zero_on_deallocate(&self) -> bool {
        self.zero_on_deallocate
    }

    /// Sets the region size in bytes.
    pub fn with_region_size(mut self, region_size: usize) -> MemoryManagerConfig {
        self.region_size = region_size;
        self
    }

    /// Sets the slot size in bytes.
    pub fn with_slot_size(mut self, slot_size: usize) -> MemoryManagerConfig {
        self.slot_size = slot_size;
        self
    }

    /// Sets the maximum number of regions.
    pub fn with_max_regions(mut self, max_regions: usize) -> MemoryManagerConfig {
        self.max_regions = max_regions;
        self
    }

    /// Sets whether released bytes are zeroed on deallocation.
    pub fn with_zero_on_deallocate(mut self, zero: bool) -> MemoryManagerConfig {
        self.zero_on_deallocate = zero;
        self
    }

    /// Validates this configuration.
    ///
    /// The region size must be non-zero and a multiple of the slot size, the
    /// slot size must be non-zero, at least one region must be allowed, and
    /// all sizes must fit the internal representations.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.region_size == 0 {
            return Err(Error::InvalidConfig("region size must be non-zero".into()));
        }
        if self.slot_size == 0 {
            return Err(Error::InvalidConfig("slot size must be non-zero".into()));
        }
        if self.region_size % self.slot_size != 0 {
            return Err(Error::InvalidConfig(
                "region size must be a multiple of slot size".into(),
            ));
        }
        if self.max_regions == 0 {
            return Err(Error::InvalidConfig(
                "at least one region must be allowed".into(),
            ));
        }
        if self.region_size > u32::MAX as usize {
            return Err(Error::InvalidConfig(
                "region size exceeds the supported maximum".into(),
            ));
        }
        if self.max_regions > u32::MAX as usize {
            return Err(Error::InvalidConfig(
                "region count exceeds the supported maximum".into(),
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Default for MemoryManagerConfig {
    fn default() -> MemoryManagerConfig {
        MemoryManagerConfig {
            region_size: 64 * 1024,
            slot_size: 64,
            max_regions: 65_536,
            zero_on_deallocate: true,
        }
    }
}

/// The RA Memory Manager — the sole owner of RA Memory.
///
/// The manager owns the lifecycle of all memory spaces. It does not implement
/// the internal layout of Program Space, Active Space, Entity Space, Work
/// Space or Registry Space — those are registered here and implemented in
/// later phases — and it carries only the compact metadata required to manage
/// storage safely (size, liveness, generation, owning space), never database
/// relationships.
///
/// The Runtime never allocates host memory directly, and Memory Spaces never
/// allocate host memory directly: **all allocation flows through this type.**
pub struct MemoryManager {
    config: MemoryManagerConfig,
    spaces: Vec<SpaceRecord>,
    next_space_id: u32,
    regions: Vec<Region>,
}

impl MemoryManager {
    /// Creates a memory manager with the default configuration.
    ///
    /// The manager begins with **zero** committed regions; regions are
    /// created on demand as allocations are made.
    pub fn new() -> MemoryManager {
        MemoryManager::with_config(MemoryManagerConfig::default())
            .expect("the default configuration is valid")
    }

    /// Creates a memory manager with an explicit configuration.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`Error::InvalidConfig`] when the configuration fails
    /// [`MemoryManagerConfig::validate`].
    pub fn with_config(config: MemoryManagerConfig) -> Result<MemoryManager> {
        config.validate()?;
        Ok(MemoryManager {
            config,
            spaces: Vec::new(),
            next_space_id: 0,
            regions: Vec::new(),
        })
    }

    /// Returns the configuration of this manager.
    pub fn config(&self) -> &MemoryManagerConfig {
        &self.config
    }

    // ---- lifecycle ----

    /// Destroys the memory system and reports what was released.
    ///
    /// All regions are returned to the host and all spaces are forgotten.
    /// The returned [`ShutdownReport`] describes the state at shutdown for
    /// diagnostics and tests.
    pub fn shutdown(self) -> ShutdownReport {
        ShutdownReport {
            spaces: self.space_count(),
            regions: self.region_count(),
            capacity_bytes: self.total_capacity(),
            live_allocations: self.allocation_count(),
            live_bytes: self.bytes_in_use(),
        }
    }

    // ---- space registration ----

    /// Registers a space of the given kind and returns its fresh identifier.
    ///
    /// Identifiers are unique and never reused within the manager's lifetime.
    pub fn register_space(&mut self, kind: SpaceKind) -> SpaceId {
        let id = SpaceId::from_u32(self.next_space_id);
        self.next_space_id += 1;
        self.spaces.push(SpaceRecord::new(id, kind));
        id
    }

    /// Unregisters a space.
    ///
    /// The space must not own any live allocations.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownSpace`] when `space` is not registered.
    /// * [`Error::SpaceInUse`] when `space` still owns live allocations.
    pub fn unregister_space(&mut self, space: SpaceId) -> Result<()> {
        let index = match self.spaces.iter().position(|record| record.id() == space) {
            Some(index) => index,
            None => return Err(Error::UnknownSpace(space)),
        };
        let usage = self.space_usage(space);
        if usage.allocations() > 0 {
            return Err(Error::SpaceInUse {
                space,
                allocations: usage.allocations(),
                bytes: usage.bytes(),
            });
        }
        self.spaces.remove(index);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Looks up the registration record of a space.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`Error::UnknownSpace`] when `space` is not registered.
    pub fn lookup_space(&self, space: SpaceId) -> Result<&SpaceRecord> {
        self.spaces
            .iter()
            .find(|record| record.id() == space)
            .ok_or(Error::UnknownSpace(space))
    }

    /// Returns the registration records of all registered spaces.
    pub fn spaces(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &SpaceRecord> {
        self.spaces.iter()
    }

    /// Returns the number of registered spaces.
    pub fn space_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.spaces.len()
    }

    // ---- allocation interface ----

    /// Allocates `bytes` bytes in `space`, returning a logical address.
    ///
    /// This byte-oriented call is the **V1 implementation interface**.
    /// Future versions may layer higher-level allocation APIs (for example
    /// typed memory objects or a layout-style interface) on top of this
    /// method without changing it.
    ///
    /// The allocation is backed by contiguous slots within a single region.
    /// Slots released by earlier deallocations are reused before the manager
    /// grows; growth happens on demand.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownSpace`] when `space` is not registered.
    /// * [`Error::EmptyAllocation`] when `bytes` is zero.
    /// * [`Error::AllocationTooLarge`] when `bytes` exceeds one region.
    /// * [`Error::RegionLimitReached`] when the region limit blocks growth.
    pub fn allocate(&mut self, space: SpaceId, bytes: usize) -> Result<LogicalAddress> {
        if !self.spaces.iter().any(|record| record.id() == space) {
            return Err(Error::UnknownSpace(space));
        }
        if bytes == 0 {
            return Err(Error::EmptyAllocation);
        }
        if bytes > self.config.region_size() {
            return Err(Error::AllocationTooLarge {
                requested: bytes,
                capacity: self.config.region_size(),
            });
        }
        let slots = bytes.div_ceil(self.config.slot_size()) as u32;
        for (region_index, region) in self.regions.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            if let Some((start, generation)) = region.alloc(slots, space) {
                return Ok(LogicalAddress::from_parts(
                    region_index as u32,
                    start,
                    generation,
                ));
            }
        }
        self.grow(slots, space)
    }

    /// Grows the region pool by one region and allocates from it.
    fn grow(&mut self, slots: u32, space: SpaceId) -> Result<LogicalAddress> {
        if self.regions.len() >= self.config.max_regions() {
            return Err(Error::RegionLimitReached {
                regions: self.regions.len(),
                max: self.config.max_regions(),
            });
        }
        let region_index = self.regions.len() as u32;
        self.regions.push(Region::new(
            self.config.region_size(),
            self.config.slot_size(),
            self.config.zero_on_deallocate(),
        ));
        let (start, generation) = self.regions[region_index as usize]
            .alloc(slots, space)
            // A fresh region is empty and `allocate` already rejected
            // requests larger than the region capacity, so this cannot fail.
            .expect("a fresh region always satisfies an in-range allocation");
        Ok(LogicalAddress::from_parts(region_index, start, generation))
    }

    /// Reclaims the allocation at `address`, making its slots reusable.
    ///
    /// The slot generations are bumped so any older address becomes stale.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::NotAllocated`] when the address does not match a live
    ///   allocation.
    /// * [`Error::StaleAddress`] when the address generation is outdated.
    pub fn deallocate(&mut self, address: LogicalAddress) -> Result<()> {
        let region = self
            .regions
            .get_mut(address.region() as usize)
            .ok_or(Error::NotAllocated { address })?;
        region.dealloc(address)
    }

    // ---- lookup interface ----

    /// Resolves an address to its allocation metadata.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::NotAllocated`] when the address does not match a live
    ///   allocation.
    /// * [`Error::StaleAddress`] when the address generation is outdated.
    pub fn lookup(&self, address: LogicalAddress) -> Result<AllocationInfo> {
        let region = self
            .regions
            .get(address.region() as usize)
            .ok_or(Error::NotAllocated { address })?;
        let resolved = region.resolve(address)?;
        Ok(AllocationInfo {
            address,
            space: resolved.space,
            size: resolved.size,
            slots: resolved.slots,
        })
    }

    /// Returns `true` when the address refers to a live allocation with a
    /// matching generation.
    pub fn contains(&self, address: LogicalAddress) -> bool {
        match self.regions.get(address.region() as usize) {
            Some(region) => region.contains(address),
            None => false,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the space that owns the allocation at `address`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`MemoryManager::lookup`].
    pub fn owner(&self, address: LogicalAddress) -> Result<SpaceId> {
        self.lookup(address).map(|info| info.space())
    }

    /// Returns the size in bytes of the allocation at `address`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`MemoryManager::lookup`].
    pub fn size(&self, address: LogicalAddress) -> Result<usize> {
        self.lookup(address).map(|info| info.size())
    }

    /// Copies bytes from the allocation at `address` into `buf`.
    ///
    /// `offset` is relative to the start of the allocation.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`MemoryManager::lookup`].
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when the requested range extends past the end
    ///   of the allocation.
    pub fn read(&self, address: LogicalAddress, offset: usize, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<()> {
        let region = self
            .regions
            .get(address.region() as usize)
            .ok_or(Error::NotAllocated { address })?;
        region.read(address, offset, buf)
    }

    /// Copies `data` into the allocation at `address`.
    ///
    /// `offset` is relative to the start of the allocation.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`MemoryManager::read`].
    pub fn write(&mut self, address: LogicalAddress, offset: usize, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
        let region = self
            .regions
            .get_mut(address.region() as usize)
            .ok_or(Error::NotAllocated { address })?;
        region.write(address, offset, data)
    }

    /// Fills `len` bytes at `offset` of the allocation at `address` with
    /// `value`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`MemoryManager::read`].
    pub fn fill(
        &mut self,
        address: LogicalAddress,
        offset: usize,
        len: usize,
        value: u8,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let region = self
            .regions
            .get_mut(address.region() as usize)
            .ok_or(Error::NotAllocated { address })?;
        region.fill(address, offset, len, value)
    }

    // ---- ownership tracking and statistics ----

    /// Returns the number of regions currently backing this manager.
    pub fn region_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.regions.len()
    }

    /// Returns the total byte capacity of all regions.
    pub fn total_capacity(&self) -> u64 {
        self.regions
            .iter()
            .map(|region| region.capacity_bytes())
            .sum()
    }

    /// Returns the number of bytes held by live allocations (slot
    /// granularity).
    pub fn bytes_in_use(&self) -> u64 {
        self.regions.iter().map(|region| region.live_bytes()).sum()
    }

    /// Returns the number of bytes currently free for allocation.
    pub fn bytes_free(&self) -> u64 {
        self.regions.iter().map(|region| region.free_bytes()).sum()
    }

    /// Returns the total number of live allocations.
    pub fn allocation_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.regions
            .iter()
            .map(|region| region.allocation_count())
            .sum()
    }

    /// Returns the usage of `space`: how many allocations it owns and how
    /// many bytes they hold.
    ///
    /// A space that is not registered (or owns nothing) reports zero usage.
    pub fn space_usage(&self, space: SpaceId) -> SpaceUsage {
        let mut allocations = 0usize;
        let mut bytes = 0u64;
        for region in &self.regions {
            for meta in region.allocations() {
                if meta.space == space {
                    allocations += 1;
                    bytes += u64::from(meta.slots) * self.config.slot_size() as u64;
                }
            }
        }
        SpaceUsage::new(allocations, bytes)
    }

    /// Returns idle regions at the end of the pool to the host.
    ///
    /// Only **trailing** regions that hold no live allocations are released,
    /// so addresses already handed out remain valid. Returns the number of
    /// bytes returned to the host. Compaction of non-trailing idle regions is
    /// intentionally left open by the Memory Architecture (§13).
    pub fn release_idle_regions(&mut self) -> u64 {
        let mut released = 0u64;
        while let Some(region) = self.regions.last() {
            if !region.is_idle() {
                break;
            }
            released += region.capacity_bytes();
            self.regions.pop();
        }
        released
    }
}

impl Default for MemoryManager {
    fn default() -> MemoryManager {
        MemoryManager::new()
    }
}

/// Metadata describing one resolved live allocation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AllocationInfo {
    address: LogicalAddress,
    space: SpaceId,
    size: usize,
    slots: u32,
}

impl AllocationInfo {
    /// Returns the address of the allocation.
    pub fn address(self) -> LogicalAddress {
        self.address
    }

    /// Returns the space that owns the allocation.
    pub fn space(self) -> SpaceId {
        self.space
    }

    /// Returns the size of the allocation in bytes (slot granularity).
    pub fn size(self) -> usize {
        self.size
    }

    /// Returns the number of slots the allocation occupies.
    pub fn slots(self) -> u32 {
        self.slots
    }
}

/// The allocation and byte usage of a space.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct SpaceUsage {
    allocations: usize,
    bytes: u64,
}

impl SpaceUsage {
    /// Creates a usage summary.
    pub(crate) fn new(allocations: usize, bytes: u64) -> SpaceUsage {
        SpaceUsage { allocations, bytes }
    }

    /// Returns the number of live allocations.
    pub fn allocations(self) -> usize {
        self.allocations
    }

    /// Returns the number of live bytes.
    pub fn bytes(self) -> u64 {
        self.bytes
    }
}

/// The state of the memory system at shutdown.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ShutdownReport {
    spaces: usize,
    regions: usize,
    capacity_bytes: u64,
    live_allocations: usize,
    live_bytes: u64,
}

impl ShutdownReport {
    /// Returns the number of registered spaces at shutdown.
    pub fn spaces(self) -> usize {
        self.spaces
    }

    /// Returns the number of regions at shutdown.
    pub fn regions(self) -> usize {
        self.regions
    }

    /// Returns the total byte capacity at shutdown.
    pub fn capacity_bytes(self) -> u64 {
        self.capacity_bytes
    }

    /// Returns the number of live allocations at shutdown.
    pub fn live_allocations(self) -> usize {
        self.live_allocations
    }

    /// Returns the number of live bytes at shutdown.
    pub fn live_bytes(self) -> u64 {
        self.live_bytes
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn manager() -> MemoryManager {
        MemoryManager::with_config(
            MemoryManagerConfig::new()
                .with_region_size(256)
                .with_slot_size(64)
                .with_max_regions(2),
        )
        .expect("test config is valid")
    }

    fn small_region_manager() -> MemoryManager {
        MemoryManager::with_config(
            MemoryManagerConfig::new()
                .with_region_size(512)
                .with_slot_size(64),
        )
        .expect("test config is valid")
    }

    #[test]
    fn new_manager_is_empty() {
        let memory = manager();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.total_capacity(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.allocation_count(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn register_lookup_and_unregister_spaces() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let program = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Program);
        let entity = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);

        assert_eq!(memory.space_count(), 2);
        assert_ne!(program, entity);
        assert_eq!(
            memory.lookup_space(program).unwrap().kind(),
            SpaceKind::Program
        );
        assert_eq!(
            memory.lookup_space(entity).unwrap().kind(),
            SpaceKind::Entity
        );
        assert!(memory.lookup_space(SpaceId::from_u32(99)).is_err());

        // Spaces register in the order they were added.
        let kinds: Vec<SpaceKind> = memory.spaces().map(|record| record.kind()).collect();
        assert_eq!(kinds, vec![SpaceKind::Program, SpaceKind::Entity]);

        // An empty space can be unregistered.
        memory.unregister_space(program).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_count(), 1);
        assert!(memory.lookup_space(program).is_err());
        assert!(memory.unregister_space(SpaceId::from_u32(42)).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn allocate_and_access_round_trip() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let entity = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);

        let address = memory.allocate(entity, 8).unwrap();
        assert!(memory.contains(address));
        // Sizes are reported at slot granularity (one 64-byte slot here).
        assert_eq!(memory.size(address).unwrap(), 64);
        assert_eq!(memory.owner(address).unwrap(), entity);
        assert_eq!(memory.lookup(address).unwrap().space(), entity);

        memory.write(address, 0, &42u64.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();
        let mut raw = [0u8; 8];
        memory.read(address, 0, &mut raw).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(u64::from_le_bytes(raw), 42);

        memory.fill(address, 4, 2, 0xEE).unwrap();
        let mut mid = [0u8; 2];
        memory.read(address, 4, &mut mid).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(mid, [0xEE; 2]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn allocate_rejects_bad_input() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let space = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);

        assert!(matches!(
            memory.allocate(space, 0),
            Err(Error::EmptyAllocation)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.allocate(space, 257),
            Err(Error::AllocationTooLarge { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.allocate(SpaceId::from_u32(777), 8),
            Err(Error::UnknownSpace(_))
        ));
        assert!(!memory.contains(LogicalAddress::from_parts(5, 0, 1)));
        assert!(memory.lookup(LogicalAddress::from_parts(5, 0, 1)).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn access_checks_bounds_and_liveness() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let space = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Work);

        let address = memory.allocate(space, 64).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.write(address, 1, &[0u8; 64]),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.read(address, 63, &mut [0u8; 2]),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.fill(address, usize::MAX, 1, 0),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));

        memory.deallocate(address).unwrap();
        assert!(!memory.contains(address));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.lookup(address),
            Err(Error::NotAllocated { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.read(address, 0, &mut [0u8; 1]),
            Err(Error::NotAllocated { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.deallocate(address),
            Err(Error::NotAllocated { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn stale_addresses_are_detected_after_reuse() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let space = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);

        let first = memory.allocate(space, 64).unwrap();
        memory.write(first, 0, b"first").unwrap();
        memory.deallocate(first).unwrap();

        let second = memory.allocate(space, 64).unwrap();
        // The slot was reused: same region and slot, newer generation.
        assert_eq!(second.region(), first.region());
        assert_eq!(second.slot(), first.slot());
        assert_ne!(second.generation(), first.generation());

        assert!(matches!(
            memory.lookup(first),
            Err(Error::StaleAddress { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.read(first, 0, &mut [0u8; 1]),
            Err(Error::StaleAddress { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.deallocate(first),
            Err(Error::StaleAddress { .. })
        ));

        // The fresh address still works.
        memory.write(second, 0, b"second").unwrap();
        let mut buf = [0u8; 6];
        memory.read(second, 0, &mut buf).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&buf, b"second");
    }

    #[test]
    fn slots_are_reused_before_growing() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let space = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);

        // Region holds 4 slots: two 2-slot allocations fill it.
        let a = memory.allocate(space, 128).unwrap();
        let _b = memory.allocate(space, 128).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 1);

        memory.deallocate(a).unwrap();
        let c = memory.allocate(space, 128).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.slot(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(memory.allocation_count(), 2);
        assert_eq!(memory.bytes_in_use(), 256);
        // The freed slots were reused, so the region is full again.
        assert_eq!(memory.bytes_free(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn regions_grow_on_demand_and_stop_at_the_limit() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let space = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);

        // 2 regions × 4 slots each = 8 one-slot allocations.
        let mut addresses = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..8 {
            addresses.push(memory.allocate(space, 64).unwrap());
        }
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 2);
        assert_eq!(memory.total_capacity(), 512);

        // The ninth allocation must fail: the region limit is reached.
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.allocate(space, 64),
            Err(Error::RegionLimitReached { regions: 2, max: 2 })
        ));

        // Freeing room in an existing region unlocks allocation again.
        memory.deallocate(addresses.remove(0)).unwrap();
        assert!(memory.allocate(space, 64).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn zeroing_on_deallocate_is_configurable() {
        let mut zeroing = small_region_manager();
        let space = zeroing.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);
        let address = zeroing.allocate(space, 64).unwrap();
        zeroing.write(address, 0, &[0xAB; 64]).unwrap();
        zeroing.deallocate(address).unwrap();

        let reused = zeroing.allocate(space, 64).unwrap();
        let mut buf = [0xFF; 64];
        zeroing.read(reused, 0, &mut buf).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(buf, [0u8; 64]);

        let mut preserving = MemoryManager::with_config(
            MemoryManagerConfig::new()
                .with_region_size(512)
                .with_slot_size(64)
                .with_zero_on_deallocate(false),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let space = preserving.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);
        let address = preserving.allocate(space, 64).unwrap();
        preserving.write(address, 0, &[0xAB; 64]).unwrap();
        preserving.deallocate(address).unwrap();

        let reused = preserving.allocate(space, 64).unwrap();
        let mut kept = [0u8; 64];
        preserving.read(reused, 0, &mut kept).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(kept, [0xAB; 64]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ownership_tracking_counts_per_space() {
        let mut memory = small_region_manager();
        let program = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Program);
        let entity = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);

        let p1 = memory.allocate(program, 128).unwrap();
        let p2 = memory.allocate(program, 64).unwrap();
        let e1 = memory.allocate(entity, 64).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(memory.owner(p1).unwrap(), program);
        assert_eq!(memory.owner(p2).unwrap(), program);
        assert_eq!(memory.owner(e1).unwrap(), entity);

        let program_usage = memory.space_usage(program);
        assert_eq!(program_usage.allocations(), 2);
        assert_eq!(program_usage.bytes(), 192);
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(entity).allocations(), 1);
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(SpaceId::from_u32(99)).allocations(), 0);

        // A space with live allocations cannot be unregistered.
        assert!(matches!(
            memory.unregister_space(program),
            Err(Error::SpaceInUse { .. })
        ));

        memory.deallocate(p1).unwrap();
        memory.deallocate(p2).unwrap();
        memory.unregister_space(program).unwrap();
        assert!(memory.lookup_space(program).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn idle_trailing_regions_are_returned_to_the_host() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let space = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);

        // Fill region 0 completely (4 one-slot allocations).
        let first_batch: Vec<_> = (0..4)
            .map(|_| memory.allocate(space, 64).unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 1);

        // Force a second region and keep one allocation alive in it.
        let keep = memory.allocate(space, 64).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 2);

        // Free region 0 entirely: it is idle but not trailing.
        for address in &first_batch {
            memory.deallocate(*address).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(memory.release_idle_regions(), 0);

        // Free the trailing allocation: the trailing region is released.
        memory.deallocate(keep).unwrap();
        let released = memory.release_idle_regions();
        assert_eq!(released, 512);
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.total_capacity(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shutdown_reports_the_final_state() {
        let mut memory = manager();
        let program = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Program);
        let entity = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity);
        let a = memory.allocate(program, 128).unwrap();
        let _b = memory.allocate(entity, 64).unwrap();
        memory.deallocate(a).unwrap();

        let report = memory.shutdown();
        assert_eq!(report.spaces(), 2);
        assert_eq!(report.regions(), 1);
        assert_eq!(report.capacity_bytes(), 256);
        assert_eq!(report.live_allocations(), 1);
        assert_eq!(report.live_bytes(), 64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_manager_begins_with_zero_committed_regions() {
        let memory = MemoryManager::new();
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.config().region_size(), 64 * 1024);
        assert_eq!(memory.config().slot_size(), 64);
        assert_eq!(memory.config().max_regions(), 65_536);
        assert!(memory.config().zero_on_deallocate());
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_configs_are_rejected() {
        let bad = [
            MemoryManagerConfig::new().with_region_size(0),
            MemoryManagerConfig::new().with_slot_size(0),
            MemoryManagerConfig::new()
                .with_region_size(100)
                .with_slot_size(64),
            MemoryManagerConfig::new().with_max_regions(0),
        ];
        for config in bad {
            assert!(config.validate().is_err());
            assert!(MemoryManager::with_config(config).is_err());
        }
        assert!(MemoryManagerConfig::new().validate().is_ok());
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn manager_types_are_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<MemoryManager>();
        assert_send_sync::<MemoryManagerConfig>();
        assert_send_sync::<AllocationInfo>();
        assert_send_sync::<SpaceUsage>();
        assert_send_sync::<ShutdownReport>();
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\module_table.rs
//! Internal Module Table — the module-record storage of Program Space.
//!
//! This private component implements the **Module Metadata / Module Table**
//! logical structure of the frozen Program Space V1 architecture: it tracks
//! loaded `.ra` modules and maps each module to its REI instruction range,
//! constant area, code map and name.
//!
//! [`ProgramSpace`](crate::program_space::ProgramSpace) delegates **all**
//! module-table responsibilities here — record storage, module lookup,
//! duplicate detection, vacant-slot reuse, table growth, iteration, module
//! removal and record encoding/decoding — while Program Space itself keeps
//! responsibility for the REI area, the constant area, the code map, its
//! lifecycle and high-level program operations.
//!
//! The table is a fixed-slot array of fixed-size records held in a single
//! [`MemoryManager`] allocation — the same byte-oriented V1 storage style as
//! the rest of the crate. Like the manager's internal region allocator, this
//! component is **not** part of the public API and may be reorganized in a
//! future version without an architecture change.

use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::codec::{get_u32, put_u32};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::manager::MemoryManager;
use crate::program_space::{ModuleId, ModuleRecord};
use crate::space::SpaceId;

/// Byte size of one module-table record.
const RECORD_SIZE: usize = 68;
/// Marks a vacant module-table slot; `u32::MAX` is never a live module id.
const VACANT_ID: u32 = u32::MAX;
/// The initial module-table capacity, in records.
const INITIAL_TABLE_CAPACITY: usize = 4;

// Field offsets inside a fixed-size module-table record (little-endian).
// Every [`LogicalAddress`] occupies three consecutive `u32`s starting at its
// `*_REGION` offset: region at +0, slot at +4, generation at +8.
const RECORD_ID: usize = 0;
const RECORD_NAME_REGION: usize = 4;
const RECORD_NAME_LEN: usize = 16;
const RECORD_REI_REGION: usize = 20;
const RECORD_REI_LEN: usize = 32;
const RECORD_CONSTANTS_REGION: usize = 36;
const RECORD_CONSTANTS_LEN: usize = 48;
const RECORD_CODE_MAP_REGION: usize = 52;
const RECORD_CODE_MAP_ENTRIES: usize = 64;

/// The module table of a Program Space.
///
/// A fixed-slot array of [`ModuleRecord`]s stored in a single
/// [`MemoryManager`] allocation. Identifiers are assigned monotonically from
/// `0` and never reused, so a stale [`ModuleId`] always fails to resolve.
///
/// The table grows on demand (doubling, copying the live records) and
/// reuses vacant slots left by [`ModuleTable::remove`] before growing.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct ModuleTable {
    /// The space that owns the table storage.
    space_id: SpaceId,
    /// The logical address of the table storage.
    address: LogicalAddress,
    /// The number of record slots in the table.
    capacity: usize,
    /// The next fresh module id to hand out.
    next_id: u32,
    /// The number of live (loaded) modules.
    live: u32,
}

impl ModuleTable {
    /// Allocates and initializes the table storage for `space_id`.
    ///
    /// The table starts with [`INITIAL_TABLE_CAPACITY`] vacant record slots
    /// and zero loaded modules.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when the table storage cannot be allocated or
    /// initialized.
    pub(crate) fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager, space_id: SpaceId) -> Result<ModuleTable> {
        let capacity = INITIAL_TABLE_CAPACITY;
        let bytes = capacity * RECORD_SIZE;
        let address = memory.allocate(space_id, bytes)?;
        // Mark every record vacant: 0xFF makes the id field u32::MAX.
        memory.fill(address, 0, bytes, 0xFF)?;
        Ok(ModuleTable {
            space_id,
            address,
            capacity,
            next_id: 0,
            live: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Returns the number of currently loaded modules.
    pub(crate) fn live_count(&self) -> u32 {
        self.live
    }

    /// Returns `true` when the module identifier space is exhausted.
    ///
    /// Checked before every insert; inserting while exhausted would collide
    /// with the vacant-slot marker [`VACANT_ID`].
    pub(crate) fn id_space_exhausted(&self) -> bool {
        self.next_id == VACANT_ID
    }

    /// Stores `record` in a table slot, assigning it a fresh module id, and
    /// returns that id.
    ///
    /// A vacant slot is reused when one exists; otherwise the table grows.
    /// The caller must have ensured [`ModuleTable::id_space_exhausted`] is
    /// false and that the module name is not already present.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when a table read or write fails.
    pub(crate) fn insert(
        &mut self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        record: ModuleRecord,
    ) -> Result<ModuleId> {
        debug_assert!(
            !self.id_space_exhausted(),
            "id space must be checked before insert"
        );
        let id = ModuleId::from_u32(self.next_id);
        self.next_id += 1;
        let bytes = encode_record(&record.with_id(id));
        let index = match self.find_vacant_index(memory)? {
            Some(index) => index,
            None => self.grow(memory)?,
        };
        self.write_record(memory, index, &bytes)?;
        self.live += 1;
        Ok(id)
    }

    /// Returns the decoded record of the module with `id`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`Error::UnknownModule`] when `id` is not loaded.
    pub(crate) fn record(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, id: ModuleId) -> Result<ModuleRecord> {
        let index = self.find_index_of(memory, id)?;
        decode_record(memory, self.read_record(memory, index)?)
    }

    /// Finds the id of the loaded module with `name`.
    ///
    /// Returns `Ok(None)` when no loaded module has that name.
    pub(crate) fn find_by_name(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<ModuleId>> {
        for index in 0..self.capacity {
            let bytes = self.read_record(memory, index)?;
            if decode_id(&bytes) == VACANT_ID {
                continue;
            }
            let record = decode_record(memory, bytes)?;
            if record.name() == name {
                return Ok(Some(record.id()));
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Removes the module with `id`, vacating its table slot, and returns
    /// its record so the caller can reclaim the module's payload storage.
    ///
    /// The slot is already vacant and the live count already updated when
    /// this returns; the caller must reclaim the returned record's payload
    /// allocations.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`Error::UnknownModule`] when `id` is not loaded.
    pub(crate) fn remove(
        &mut self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        id: ModuleId,
    ) -> Result<ModuleRecord> {
        let index = self.find_index_of(memory, id)?;
        let bytes = self.read_record(memory, index)?;
        self.write_record(memory, index, &vacant_record())?;
        self.live -= 1;
        decode_record(memory, bytes)
    }

    /// Returns the decoded records of all loaded modules, in table order.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when a table read fails.
    pub(crate) fn records(&self, memory: &MemoryManager) -> Result<Vec<ModuleRecord>> {
        let mut records = Vec::new();
        for index in 0..self.capacity {
            let bytes = self.read_record(memory, index)?;
            if decode_id(&bytes) == VACANT_ID {
                continue;
            }
            records.push(decode_record(memory, bytes)?);
        }
        Ok(records)
    }

    /// Deallocates the table storage.
    ///
    /// Consumes the table; no further operations are valid.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when the storage cannot be reclaimed.
    pub(crate) fn reclaim(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        memory.deallocate(self.address)
    }

    // ---- table internals ----

    /// Finds the index of the first vacant table slot.
    fn find_vacant_index(&self, memory: &MemoryManager) -> Result<Option<usize>> {
        for index in 0..self.capacity {
            if decode_id(&self.read_record(memory, index)?) == VACANT_ID {
                return Ok(Some(index));
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Finds the table index of the module with `id`.
    fn find_index_of(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, id: ModuleId) -> Result<usize> {
        for index in 0..self.capacity {
            if decode_id(&self.read_record(memory, index)?) == id.as_u32() {
                return Ok(index);
            }
        }
        Err(Error::UnknownModule(id))
    }

    /// Doubles the table, copying the live records, and returns the index of
    /// the first newly added (vacant) slot.
    fn grow(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<usize> {
        let old_capacity = self.capacity;
        let new_capacity = old_capacity * 2;
        let new_bytes = new_capacity * RECORD_SIZE;
        let new_address = memory.allocate(self.space_id, new_bytes)?;
        memory.fill(new_address, 0, new_bytes, 0xFF)?;
        for index in 0..old_capacity {
            let bytes = self.read_record(memory, index)?;
            self.write_record_at(memory, new_address, index, &bytes)?;
        }
        memory.deallocate(self.address)?;
        self.address = new_address;
        self.capacity = new_capacity;
        Ok(old_capacity)
    }

    /// Reads one raw table record at `index` from the table storage.
    fn read_record(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, index: usize) -> Result<[u8; RECORD_SIZE]> {
        let mut buf = [0u8; RECORD_SIZE];
        memory.read(self.address, index * RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(buf)
    }

    /// Writes one raw table record at `index` into the table storage.
    fn write_record(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        index: usize,
        record: &[u8; RECORD_SIZE],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        memory.write(self.address, index * RECORD_SIZE, record)
    }

    /// Writes one raw table record at `index` into the storage at
    /// `address` (used while copying into a grown table).
    fn write_record_at(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        address: LogicalAddress,
        index: usize,
        record: &[u8; RECORD_SIZE],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        memory.write(address, index * RECORD_SIZE, record)
    }
}

// ---- record codecs ----

/// Writes a [`LogicalAddress`] at `offset` of `buf` (region, slot,
/// generation).
fn put_address(buf: &mut [u8], offset: usize, address: LogicalAddress) {
    put_u32(buf, offset, address.region());
    put_u32(buf, offset + 4, address.slot());
    put_u32(buf, offset + 8, address.generation());
}

/// Reads a [`LogicalAddress`] at `offset` of `buf`.
fn get_address(buf: &[u8], offset: usize) -> LogicalAddress {
    LogicalAddress::from_parts(
        get_u32(buf, offset),
        get_u32(buf, offset + 4),
        get_u32(buf, offset + 8),
    )
}

/// Returns the module id field of a raw table record.
fn decode_id(bytes: &[u8; RECORD_SIZE]) -> u32 {
    get_u32(bytes, RECORD_ID)
}

/// Returns a table record marking a vacant slot.
fn vacant_record() -> [u8; RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; RECORD_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, RECORD_ID, VACANT_ID);
    buf
}

/// Encodes a module record as raw table bytes.
fn encode_record(record: &ModuleRecord) -> [u8; RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut bytes = [0u8; RECORD_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut bytes, RECORD_ID, record.id().as_u32());
    put_address(&mut bytes, RECORD_NAME_REGION, record.name_address());
    put_u32(&mut bytes, RECORD_NAME_LEN, record.name_len() as u32);
    put_address(&mut bytes, RECORD_REI_REGION, record.rei_address());
    put_u32(&mut bytes, RECORD_REI_LEN, record.rei_len() as u32);
    put_address(
        &mut bytes,
        RECORD_CONSTANTS_REGION,
        record.constants_address(),
    );
    put_u32(
        &mut bytes,
        RECORD_CONSTANTS_LEN,
        record.constants_len() as u32,
    );
    put_address(
        &mut bytes,
        RECORD_CODE_MAP_REGION,
        record.code_map_address(),
    );
    put_u32(
        &mut bytes,
        RECORD_CODE_MAP_ENTRIES,
        record.code_map_entries() as u32,
    );
    bytes
}

/// Decodes a module record, reading the module name from Program Space
/// storage.
fn decode_record(memory: &MemoryManager, bytes: [u8; RECORD_SIZE]) -> Result<ModuleRecord> {
    let name_address = get_address(&bytes, RECORD_NAME_REGION);
    let name_len = get_u32(&bytes, RECORD_NAME_LEN) as usize;
    let mut name_bytes = vec![0u8; name_len];
    if name_len > 0 {
        memory.read(name_address, 0, &mut name_bytes)?;
    }
    let name = String::from_utf8(name_bytes)
        .map_err(|_| Error::InvalidData("module name is not valid UTF-8".into()))?;
    Ok(ModuleRecord::from_parts(
        name,
        name_address,
        name_len,
        get_address(&bytes, RECORD_REI_REGION),
        get_u32(&bytes, RECORD_REI_LEN) as usize,
        get_address(&bytes, RECORD_CONSTANTS_REGION),
        get_u32(&bytes, RECORD_CONSTANTS_LEN) as usize,
        get_address(&bytes, RECORD_CODE_MAP_REGION),
        get_u32(&bytes, RECORD_CODE_MAP_ENTRIES) as usize,
    )
    .with_id(ModuleId::from_u32(get_u32(&bytes, RECORD_ID))))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::space::SpaceKind;

    /// Stores `bytes` in a fresh manager allocation for `space` and returns
    /// its address.
    fn store(memory: &mut MemoryManager, space: SpaceId, bytes: &[u8]) -> LogicalAddress {
        let address = memory.allocate(space, bytes.len()).unwrap();
        memory.write(address, 0, bytes).unwrap();
        address
    }

    /// Builds a module record with a stored name and REI payload.
    fn record_with(
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        space: SpaceId,
        name: &str,
        rei: &[u8],
    ) -> ModuleRecord {
        let name_address = store(memory, space, name.as_bytes());
        let rei_address = store(memory, space, rei);
        ModuleRecord::from_parts(
            name.to_string(),
            name_address,
            name.len(),
            rei_address,
            rei.len(),
            LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 0, 0),
            0,
            LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 0, 0),
            0,
        )
    }

    /// Creates a fresh manager and a table registered under a new space.
    fn new_table() -> (MemoryManager, SpaceId, ModuleTable) {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Program);
        let table = ModuleTable::new(&mut memory, space).unwrap();
        (memory, space, table)
    }

    /// Frees the payload allocations of `record` and the table storage.
    fn teardown(memory: &mut MemoryManager, table: ModuleTable, record: &ModuleRecord) {
        memory.deallocate(record.name_address()).unwrap();
        memory.deallocate(record.rei_address()).unwrap();
        table.reclaim(memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn insert_assigns_fresh_ids_and_reuses_vacant_slots() {
        let (mut memory, space, mut table) = new_table();
        assert_eq!(table.live_count(), 0);

        let record = record_with(&mut memory, space, "a", &[1]);
        let first = table.insert(&mut memory, record).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(first.as_u32(), 0);
        let record = record_with(&mut memory, space, "b", &[2]);
        let second = table.insert(&mut memory, record).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(second.as_u32(), 1);
        assert_eq!(table.live_count(), 2);

        let removed = table.remove(&mut memory, first).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(removed.name(), "a");
        assert_eq!(table.live_count(), 1);

        // The vacant slot is reused before the table grows.
        let record = record_with(&mut memory, space, "c", &[3]);
        let third = table.insert(&mut memory, record).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(third.as_u32(), 2);
        assert_eq!(table.live_count(), 2);

        // Free every payload allocation and the table storage.
        let remaining = table.records(&memory).unwrap();
        for record in remaining.iter().chain(std::iter::once(&removed)) {
            memory.deallocate(record.name_address()).unwrap();
            memory.deallocate(record.rei_address()).unwrap();
        }
        table.reclaim(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn record_codec_round_trips_through_storage() {
        let (mut memory, space, mut table) = new_table();

        let record = record_with(&mut memory, space, "main", &[0x01, 0x02]);
        let id = table.insert(&mut memory, record).unwrap();
        let decoded = table.record(&memory, id).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decoded.id(), id);
        assert_eq!(decoded.name(), "main");
        assert_eq!(decoded.rei_len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(table.find_by_name(&memory, "main").unwrap(), Some(id));
        assert_eq!(table.find_by_name(&memory, "other").unwrap(), None);

        teardown(&mut memory, table, &decoded);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn growth_preserves_records() {
        let (mut memory, space, mut table) = new_table();

        let mut ids = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..10u8 {
            let name = format!("m{i}");
            let record = record_with(&mut memory, space, &name, &[i]);
            let id = table.insert(&mut memory, record).unwrap();
            ids.push(id);
        }
        assert_eq!(table.live_count(), 10);
        assert_eq!(table.capacity, 16); // 4 -> 8 -> 16
        for (i, id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {
            let record = table.record(&memory, *id).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(record.name(), format!("m{i}"));
            assert_eq!(record.rei_len(), 1);
        }
        assert_eq!(table.records(&memory).unwrap().len(), 10);

        for record in table.records(&memory).unwrap() {
            memory.deallocate(record.name_address()).unwrap();
            memory.deallocate(record.rei_address()).unwrap();
        }
        table.reclaim(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\program_space.rs
//! Program Space (PS) — the ready-to-execute program representation.
//!
//! Per the Program Space V1 architecture document, *"Program Space is the RA
//! Memory area that stores a program's ready-to-execute code so RA Execution
//! can run it quickly."* A `.ra` source module is validated by RA Core,
//! lowered to **RA Executable Instructions (REI)**, and loaded here so that
//! RA Execution never re-parses or re-analyzes source.
//!
//! Program Space has four logical structures, all implemented here as
//! **clients of the frozen [`MemoryManager`]**:
//!
//! 1. **Module Metadata / Module Table** — maps each loaded `.ra` module to
//!    its REI instruction range, constant area, code map and name. The
//!    module-table responsibilities (record storage, lookup, duplicate
//!    detection, vacant-slot reuse, growth, removal and record
//!    encoding/decoding) are delegated to the internal [`ModuleTable`]
//!    component; this module keeps the public loading API.
//! 2. **REI Instruction Area** — the module's executable instructions. The
//!    exact REI encoding is intentionally open in the architecture, so REI
//!    is stored as an opaque byte stream whose length is tracked;
//! 3. **Constant Area** — immutable constants/literals shared by reference
//!    instead of re-allocated;
//! 4. **Code Map** — a compact REI↔`.ra` source mapping for diagnostics,
//!    debugging and source navigation, stored as fixed-size entries.
//!
//! # Client of the Memory Manager
//!
//! Program Space **never allocates host memory directly**. Every structure —
//! including the module table itself — lives in allocations obtained from
//! the [`MemoryManager`] and is referenced by [`LogicalAddress`]. The
//! [`ProgramSpace`] value holds only bookkeeping: its registered
//! [`SpaceId`] and the internal [`ModuleTable`] (which in turn holds the
//! table address and counters). Decoded values (module names, records) are
//! returned to callers as transient copies and are not Program Space
//! storage.
//!
//! The space is created with a [`MemoryManager`] via
//! [`ProgramSpace::new`] (which registers [`SpaceKind::Program`]) and every
//! operation takes the manager so the same manager can later serve Active,
//! Entity, Work and Registry Spaces. When the program/session lifetime ends,
//! [`ProgramSpace::destroy`] reclaims all storage and unregisters the space.
//!
//! # No knowledge of Entity Space Value Lists
//!
//! Program Space **owns executable structure**: module metadata, REI
//! instructions, constants and the code map. It stores ready-to-execute code
//! only and has **no knowledge of Entity Space Value Lists**, runtime values
//! or bindings — execution values belong to Entity Space and execution
//! identity to Active Space. Executing the loaded REI is the Runtime's
//! responsibility, not this crate's.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_common::SourcePos;
//! use ra_memory::{CodeMapEntry, LoadedModule, MemoryManager, ProgramSpace};
//!
//! let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
//! let mut program = ProgramSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
//!
//! let main = program
//!     .load_module(
//!         &mut memory,
//!         &LoadedModule::new(
//!             "main",
//!             &[0x01, 0x02, 0x03],
//!             &[0xCA, 0xFE],
//!             &[CodeMapEntry::new(0, SourcePos::from(0u32))],
//!         ),
//!     )
//!     .unwrap();
//!
//! let mut rei = [0u8; 3];
//! program.read_rei(&memory, main, 0, &mut rei).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(&rei, &[0x01, 0x02, 0x03]);
//!
//! program.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
//! ```

use std::fmt;

use ra_common::SourcePos;

use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::codec::{get_u32, put_u32};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::manager::MemoryManager;
use crate::module_table::ModuleTable;
use crate::space::{SpaceId, SpaceKind};

/// Byte size of one code-map entry (`rei_offset` + source position).
const CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE: usize = 8;

/// A unique handle to a module loaded into Program Space.
///
/// Identifiers are monotonic and never reused within a [`ProgramSpace`]
/// lifetime, so a stale [`ModuleId`] always fails to resolve.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct ModuleId(u32);

impl ModuleId {
    /// Returns the raw identifier value.
    pub fn as_u32(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Creates an identifier from a raw value.
    pub(crate) fn from_u32(value: u32) -> ModuleId {
        ModuleId(value)
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for ModuleId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let id = self.0;
        write!(f, "module#{id}")
    }
}

/// One entry of the compact REI↔`.ra` source code map.
///
/// Maps an REI byte offset to the `.ra` source position of the instruction
/// that starts there. Entries are expected to be in ascending [`rei_offset`]
/// order.
///
/// [`rei_offset`]: CodeMapEntry::rei_offset
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CodeMapEntry {
    rei_offset: u32,
    source: SourcePos,
}

impl CodeMapEntry {
    /// Creates a code-map entry mapping an REI byte offset to a source
    /// position.
    pub const fn new(rei_offset: u32, source: SourcePos) -> CodeMapEntry {
        CodeMapEntry { rei_offset, source }
    }

    /// Returns the REI byte offset of the mapped instruction.
    pub fn rei_offset(self) -> u32 {
        self.rei_offset
    }

    /// Returns the `.ra` source position of the mapped instruction.
    pub fn source(self) -> SourcePos {
        self.source
    }
}

/// A decoded snapshot of one loaded module's Program Space record.
///
/// This is a transient value copy: the authoritative record lives in
/// Program Space storage inside the [`MemoryManager`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ModuleRecord {
    id: ModuleId,
    name: String,
    name_address: LogicalAddress,
    name_len: usize,
    rei: LogicalAddress,
    rei_len: usize,
    constants: LogicalAddress,
    constants_len: usize,
    code_map: LogicalAddress,
    code_map_entries: usize,
}

impl ModuleRecord {
    /// Creates a decoded module record from its parts.
    ///
    /// The identifier is provisional and is replaced with the definitive
    /// value when the record is inserted into a module table or decoded
    /// from one.
    // The parameters mirror the fixed-size record layout one-to-one;
    // bundling them would add an intermediate type without improving
    // clarity.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn from_parts(
        name: String,
        name_address: LogicalAddress,
        name_len: usize,
        rei: LogicalAddress,
        rei_len: usize,
        constants: LogicalAddress,
        constants_len: usize,
        code_map: LogicalAddress,
        code_map_entries: usize,
    ) -> ModuleRecord {
        ModuleRecord {
            id: ModuleId::from_u32(0),
            name,
            name_address,
            name_len,
            rei,
            rei_len,
            constants,
            constants_len,
            code_map,
            code_map_entries,
        }
    }

    /// Returns a copy of the record with `id` substituted.
    pub(crate) fn with_id(mut self, id: ModuleId) -> ModuleRecord {
        self.id = id;
        self
    }

    /// Returns the module identifier.
    pub fn id(&self) -> ModuleId {
        self.id
    }

    /// Returns the module name (the `.ra` module name).
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }

    /// Returns the logical address of the module's name bytes.
    pub fn name_address(&self) -> LogicalAddress {
        self.name_address
    }

    /// Returns the byte length of the module name.
    pub fn name_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.name_len
    }

    /// Returns the logical address of the module's REI instruction area.
    pub fn rei_address(&self) -> LogicalAddress {
        self.rei
    }

    /// Returns the byte length of the module's REI instruction area.
    pub fn rei_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.rei_len
    }

    /// Returns the logical address of the module's constant area.
    pub fn constants_address(&self) -> LogicalAddress {
        self.constants
    }

    /// Returns the byte length of the module's constant area.
    pub fn constants_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.constants_len
    }

    /// Returns the logical address of the module's code map.
    pub fn code_map_address(&self) -> LogicalAddress {
        self.code_map
    }

    /// Returns the number of code-map entries of the module.
    pub fn code_map_entries(&self) -> usize {
        self.code_map_entries
    }
}

/// The inputs for loading one `.ra` module into Program Space.
///
/// The buffers are transient inputs: Program Space copies them into
/// manager-backed storage. An empty `rei`, `constants` or `code_map` is
/// allowed and means the module has none of that area.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LoadedModule<'a> {
    name: &'a str,
    rei: &'a [u8],
    constants: &'a [u8],
    code_map: &'a [CodeMapEntry],
}

impl<'a> LoadedModule<'a> {
    /// Creates a module-loading payload.
    pub fn new(
        name: &'a str,
        rei: &'a [u8],
        constants: &'a [u8],
        code_map: &'a [CodeMapEntry],
    ) -> LoadedModule<'a> {
        LoadedModule {
            name,
            rei,
            constants,
            code_map,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the module name.
    pub fn name(&self) -> &'a str {
        self.name
    }

    /// Returns the REI instruction bytes.
    pub fn rei(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
        self.rei
    }

    /// Returns the constant bytes.
    pub fn constants(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
        self.constants
    }

    /// Returns the code-map entries.
    pub fn code_map(&self) -> &'a [CodeMapEntry] {
        self.code_map
    }
}

/// Program Space (PS) — the ready-to-execute program representation.
///
/// A client of the [`MemoryManager`]: it registers [`SpaceKind::Program`],
/// obtains **all** of its storage through manager allocations, and never
/// allocates host memory directly. Program Space contains only the four
/// logical structures of the architecture document — the module table, REI
/// instruction areas, constant areas and code maps. It does **not** hold
/// ASTs, RA IR, runtime entities, temporaries or execution state; those
/// belong to later phases or other spaces.
///
/// All module-table responsibilities (record storage, lookup, duplicate
/// detection, vacant-slot reuse, growth, removal and record
/// encoding/decoding) are delegated to the internal [`ModuleTable`]
/// component. Program Space itself keeps responsibility for the REI area,
/// the constant area, the code map, its lifecycle and the high-level
/// program operations.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ProgramSpace {
    space_id: SpaceId,
    table: ModuleTable,
}

impl ProgramSpace {
    /// Creates a Program Space within `memory`.
    ///
    /// Registers [`SpaceKind::Program`] and allocates the module table from
    /// the manager. The space begins with zero loaded modules.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when the module table cannot be allocated.
    pub fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<ProgramSpace> {
        let space_id = memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Program);
        let table = ModuleTable::new(memory, space_id)?;
        Ok(ProgramSpace { space_id, table })
    }

    /// Returns the [`SpaceId`] this Program Space registered with the
    /// manager.
    pub fn space_id(&self) -> SpaceId {
        self.space_id
    }

    /// Returns the number of currently loaded modules.
    pub fn module_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.table.live_count() as usize
    }

    // ---- module table ----

    /// Loads a module into Program Space and returns its fresh identifier.
    ///
    /// The module's name, REI bytes, constants and code map are copied into
    /// manager-backed storage and a record is appended to the module table
    /// (growing the table on demand). Released table slots are reused before
    /// the table grows.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when the name is empty or the module
    ///   identifier space is exhausted.
    /// * [`Error::DuplicateModule`] when a module with the same name is
    ///   already loaded.
    /// * Manager errors when storage cannot be allocated or written.
    pub fn load_module<'a>(
        &mut self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        module: &LoadedModule<'a>,
    ) -> Result<ModuleId> {
        if module.name().is_empty() {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "module name must not be empty".into(),
            ));
        }
        if self.table.id_space_exhausted() {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "module identifier space exhausted".into(),
            ));
        }
        if self.table.find_by_name(memory, module.name())?.is_some() {
            return Err(Error::DuplicateModule(module.name().to_string()));
        }

        let (name_address, name_len) =
            store_bytes(memory, self.space_id, module.name().as_bytes())?;
        let (rei, rei_len) = store_bytes(memory, self.space_id, module.rei())?;
        let (constants, constants_len) = store_bytes(memory, self.space_id, module.constants())?;
        let (code_map, code_map_entries) =
            store_code_map(memory, self.space_id, module.code_map())?;

        let record = ModuleRecord::from_parts(
            module.name().to_string(),
            name_address,
            name_len,
            rei,
            rei_len,
            constants,
            constants_len,
            code_map,
            code_map_entries,
        );
        self.table.insert(memory, record)
    }

    /// Unloads a module, reclaiming all of its storage and freeing its
    /// table slot for reuse.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::UnknownModule`] when `id` is not loaded.
    /// * Manager errors when storage cannot be reclaimed.
    pub fn unload_module(&mut self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, id: ModuleId) -> Result<()> {
        let record = self.table.remove(memory, id)?;
        deallocate_optional(memory, record.name_address())?;
        deallocate_optional(memory, record.rei_address())?;
        deallocate_optional(memory, record.constants_address())?;
        deallocate_optional(memory, record.code_map_address())?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Destroys Program Space, reclaiming every module's storage and the
    /// module table, and unregisters the space.
    ///
    /// After this, the [`SpaceId`] is no longer registered. Dropping a
    /// [`ProgramSpace`] without calling this leaks its allocations until the
    /// owning manager is shut down.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when storage cannot be reclaimed or the space
    /// cannot be unregistered.
    pub fn destroy(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        let ProgramSpace { space_id, table } = self;
        for record in table.records(memory)? {
            deallocate_optional(memory, record.name_address())?;
            deallocate_optional(memory, record.rei_address())?;
            deallocate_optional(memory, record.constants_address())?;
            deallocate_optional(memory, record.code_map_address())?;
        }
        table.reclaim(memory)?;
        memory.unregister_space(space_id)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    // ---- lookups ----

    /// Returns the decoded record of the module with `id`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`Error::UnknownModule`] when `id` is not loaded.
    pub fn module(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, id: ModuleId) -> Result<ModuleRecord> {
        self.table.record(memory, id)
    }

    /// Finds a module by name.
    ///
    /// Returns `Ok(None)` when no loaded module has that name.
    pub fn module_by_name(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, name: &str) -> Result<Option<ModuleId>> {
        self.table.find_by_name(memory, name)
    }

    // ---- REI instruction area ----

    /// Returns the REI byte length of the module with `id`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`ProgramSpace::module`].
    pub fn rei_len(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, id: ModuleId) -> Result<usize> {
        Ok(self.module(memory, id)?.rei_len())
    }

    /// Copies REI bytes out of Program Space into `buf`.
    ///
    /// `offset` is relative to the start of the module's REI instruction
    /// area. Reading an empty area succeeds only with an empty `buf`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`ProgramSpace::module`].
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when the requested range extends past the
    ///   end of the module's REI area.
    pub fn read_rei(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        id: ModuleId,
        offset: usize,
        buf: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let record = self.module(memory, id)?;
        check_range(record.rei, offset, buf.len(), record.rei_len)?;
        if !buf.is_empty() {
            memory.read(record.rei, offset, buf)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // ---- constant area ----

    /// Returns the constant byte length of the module with `id`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`ProgramSpace::module`].
    pub fn constants_len(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, id: ModuleId) -> Result<usize> {
        Ok(self.module(memory, id)?.constants_len())
    }

    /// Copies constant bytes out of Program Space into `buf`.
    ///
    /// `offset` is relative to the start of the module's constant area.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`ProgramSpace::module`].
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when the requested range extends past the
    ///   end of the module's constant area.
    pub fn read_constants(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        id: ModuleId,
        offset: usize,
        buf: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let record = self.module(memory, id)?;
        check_range(record.constants, offset, buf.len(), record.constants_len)?;
        if !buf.is_empty() {
            memory.read(record.constants, offset, buf)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // ---- code map ----

    /// Returns the number of code-map entries of the module with `id`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`ProgramSpace::module`].
    pub fn code_map_entries(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, id: ModuleId) -> Result<usize> {
        Ok(self.module(memory, id)?.code_map_entries())
    }

    /// Returns the code-map entry at `index` of the module with `id`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * The errors of [`ProgramSpace::module`].
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `index` is out of range.
    pub fn code_map_entry(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        id: ModuleId,
        index: usize,
    ) -> Result<CodeMapEntry> {
        let record = self.module(memory, id)?;
        self.code_map_entry_from_record(memory, &record, index)
    }

    /// Returns an iterator over the code-map entries of the module with
    /// `id`, decoded on demand from Program Space storage.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`ProgramSpace::module`].
    pub fn code_map<'a>(&self, memory: &'a MemoryManager, id: ModuleId) -> Result<CodeMapIter<'a>> {
        let record = self.module(memory, id)?;
        Ok(CodeMapIter::new(
            memory,
            record.code_map,
            record.code_map_entries,
        ))
    }

    /// Resolves an REI byte offset to the `.ra` source position of the
    /// instruction that covers it.
    ///
    /// Returns the source position of the last entry whose
    /// [`rei_offset`](CodeMapEntry::rei_offset) is at or before `rei_offset`
    /// — the entry that starts at or before the given instruction — and
    /// `Ok(None)` when no entry applies. Entries are expected to be
    /// ascending by `rei_offset`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`ProgramSpace::module`].
    pub fn source_for_rei_offset(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        id: ModuleId,
        rei_offset: u32,
    ) -> Result<Option<SourcePos>> {
        let record = self.module(memory, id)?;
        let mut best = None;
        for index in 0..record.code_map_entries {
            let entry = self.code_map_entry_from_record(memory, &record, index)?;
            if entry.rei_offset() <= rei_offset {
                best = Some(entry.source());
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        Ok(best)
    }

    /// Decodes the code-map entry at `index` of the given record.
    fn code_map_entry_from_record(
        &self,
        memory: &MemoryManager,
        record: &ModuleRecord,
        index: usize,
    ) -> Result<CodeMapEntry> {
        if index >= record.code_map_entries {
            return Err(Error::OutOfBounds {
                address: record.code_map,
                offset: index * CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE,
                length: CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE,
                available: record.code_map_entries * CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE,
            });
        }
        let mut buf = [0u8; CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE];
        memory.read(record.code_map, index * CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(decode_entry(buf))
    }
}

/// An iterator over the code-map entries of one module.
///
/// Entries are decoded on demand from Program Space storage through the
/// [`MemoryManager`]. Iteration stops after the first read failure, which is
/// reported as the final item.
pub struct CodeMapIter<'a> {
    memory: &'a MemoryManager,
    address: LogicalAddress,
    entries: usize,
    position: usize,
}

impl fmt::Debug for CodeMapIter<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("CodeMapIter")
            .field("address", &self.address)
            .field("entries", &self.entries)
            .field("position", &self.position)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl<'a> CodeMapIter<'a> {
    /// Creates a code-map iterator over `entries` at `address`.
    pub(crate) fn new(
        memory: &'a MemoryManager,
        address: LogicalAddress,
        entries: usize,
    ) -> CodeMapIter<'a> {
        CodeMapIter {
            memory,
            address,
            entries,
            position: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl Iterator for CodeMapIter<'_> {
    type Item = Result<CodeMapEntry>;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
        if self.position >= self.entries {
            return None;
        }
        let mut buf = [0u8; CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE];
        match self
            .memory
            .read(self.address, self.position * CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE, &mut buf)
        {
            Ok(()) => {
                self.position += 1;
                Some(Ok(decode_entry(buf)))
            }
            Err(error) => {
                self.position = self.entries;
                Some(Err(error))
            }
        }
    }
}

// ---- payload codecs ----

/// The address used to represent an absent (empty) payload area.
fn null_address() -> LogicalAddress {
    LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 0, 0)
}

/// Returns `true` when `address` is the absent-payload marker.
fn is_null(address: LogicalAddress) -> bool {
    address == null_address()
}

/// Encodes one code-map entry as eight little-endian bytes.
fn encode_entry(entry: CodeMapEntry) -> [u8; CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE] {
