    let mut buf = [0u8; CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE];
    put_u32(&mut buf, 0, entry.rei_offset());
    put_u32(&mut buf, 4, entry.source().as_u32());
    buf
}

/// Decodes one code-map entry from eight little-endian bytes.
fn decode_entry(buf: [u8; CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE]) -> CodeMapEntry {
    CodeMapEntry::new(get_u32(&buf, 0), SourcePos::from(get_u32(&buf, 4)))
}

/// Copies `bytes` into a fresh manager allocation for `space`.
///
/// An empty slice is stored as the absent marker (a null address with length
/// zero).
fn store_bytes(
    memory: &mut MemoryManager,
    space: SpaceId,
    bytes: &[u8],
) -> Result<(LogicalAddress, usize)> {
    if bytes.is_empty() {
        return Ok((null_address(), 0));
    }
    let address = memory.allocate(space, bytes.len())?;
    memory.write(address, 0, bytes)?;
    Ok((address, bytes.len()))
}

/// Copies a code map into a fresh manager allocation for `space`.
fn store_code_map(
    memory: &mut MemoryManager,
    space: SpaceId,
    entries: &[CodeMapEntry],
) -> Result<(LogicalAddress, usize)> {
    if entries.is_empty() {
        return Ok((null_address(), 0));
    }
    let address = memory.allocate(space, entries.len() * CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE)?;
    for (index, entry) in entries.iter().enumerate() {
        let bytes = encode_entry(*entry);
        memory.write(address, index * CODE_MAP_ENTRY_SIZE, &bytes)?;
    }
    Ok((address, entries.len()))
}

/// Deallocates `address` unless it is the absent-payload marker.
fn deallocate_optional(memory: &mut MemoryManager, address: LogicalAddress) -> Result<()> {
    if !is_null(address) {
        memory.deallocate(address)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Validates that `[offset, offset + length)` fits within `available` bytes,
/// without overflowing on the addition.
fn check_range(
    address: LogicalAddress,
    offset: usize,
    length: usize,
    available: usize,
) -> Result<()> {
    if offset > available || length > available - offset {
        return Err(Error::OutOfBounds {
            address,
            offset,
            length,
            available,
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const SAMPLE_REI: &[u8] = &[0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04];
    const SAMPLE_CONSTANTS: &[u8] = &[0xAA, 0xBB];
    const SAMPLE_CODE_MAP: &[CodeMapEntry] = &[
        CodeMapEntry::new(0, SourcePos::MIN),
        CodeMapEntry::new(4, SourcePos::MIN),
    ];

    fn sample_module(name: &str) -> LoadedModule<'_> {
        LoadedModule::new(name, SAMPLE_REI, SAMPLE_CONSTANTS, SAMPLE_CODE_MAP)
    }

    #[test]
    fn new_registers_program_space() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let program = ProgramSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            memory.lookup_space(program.space_id()).unwrap().kind(),
            SpaceKind::Program
        );
        assert_eq!(program.module_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.region_count(), 1); // the module table
        program.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn load_and_query_module() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut program = ProgramSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let id = program
            .load_module(&mut memory, &sample_module("main"))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(id.as_u32(), 0);
        assert_eq!(program.module_count(), 1);

        let record = program.module(&memory, id).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(record.id(), id);
        assert_eq!(record.name(), "main");
        assert_eq!(record.rei_len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(record.constants_len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(record.code_map_entries(), 2);
        assert!(memory.contains(record.rei_address()));
        assert!(memory.contains(record.constants_address()));
        assert!(memory.contains(record.code_map_address()));

        let mut rei = [0u8; 4];
        program.read_rei(&memory, id, 0, &mut rei).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rei, [0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04]);

        let mut constants = [0u8; 2];
        program
            .read_constants(&memory, id, 0, &mut constants)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(constants, [0xAA, 0xBB]);

        assert_eq!(
            program.code_map_entry(&memory, id, 0).unwrap(),
            CodeMapEntry::new(0, SourcePos::MIN)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            program.code_map_entry(&memory, id, 1).unwrap(),
            CodeMapEntry::new(4, SourcePos::MIN)
        );

        assert_eq!(program.module_by_name(&memory, "main").unwrap(), Some(id));
        assert_eq!(program.module_by_name(&memory, "other").unwrap(), None);

        program.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn source_for_rei_offset_maps_to_last_entry_at_or_before() {

    #[test]

        assert!(matches!(

            Err(Error::UnknownModule(m)) if m.as_u32() == 99

    #[test]
    fn table_grows_beyond_initial_capacity() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut program = ProgramSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        for i in 0..10u8 {
            let name = format!("module_{i}");
            let id = program
                .load_module(&mut memory, &LoadedModule::new(&name, &[i], &[], &[]))
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(id.as_u32(), u32::from(i));
        }
        assert_eq!(program.module_count(), 10);
        for i in 0..10u8 {
            let record = program
                .module(&memory, ModuleId::from_u32(u32::from(i)))
                .unwrap();
            let mut one = [0u8; 1];
            program.read_rei(&memory, record.id(), 0, &mut one).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(one[0], i);
        }
        program.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn unload_frees_storage_and_reuses_table_slots() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut program = ProgramSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let id = program
            .load_module(&mut memory, &sample_module("main"))
            .unwrap();
        let rei = program.module(&memory, id).unwrap().rei_address();
        assert!(memory.contains(rei));

        program.unload_module(&mut memory, id).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(program.module_count(), 0);
        assert!(matches!(program.module(&memory, id), Err(Error::UnknownModule(m)) if m == id));
        assert!(!memory.contains(rei));
        // Only the module table remains allocated to the space.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(program.space_id()).allocations(), 1);

        // The vacant table slot is reused by the next load.
        let next = program
            .load_module(&mut memory, &sample_module("next"))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(next.as_u32(), 1);
        assert_eq!(program.module_count(), 1);
        program.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn destroy_releases_all_storage_and_unregisters() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut program = ProgramSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        program
            .load_module(&mut memory, &sample_module("a"))
            .unwrap();
        program
            .load_module(&mut memory, &sample_module("b"))
            .unwrap();
        let space_id = program.space_id();
        // 2 modules × 4 payload areas + the module table.
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space_id).allocations(), 9);

        program.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert!(memory.lookup_space(space_id).is_err());
        assert_eq!(memory.allocation_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn code_map_iterator_yields_entries_in_order() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let mut program = ProgramSpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
        let id = program
            .load_module(&mut memory, &sample_module("main"))
            .unwrap();
        let entries: Vec<_> = program
            .code_map(&memory, id)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|entry| entry.unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            entries,
            vec![
                CodeMapEntry::new(0, SourcePos::MIN),
                CodeMapEntry::new(4, SourcePos::MIN)
            ]
        );
        program.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn module_id_display_and_ordering() {
        let a = ModuleId::from_u32(0);
        let b = ModuleId::from_u32(1);
        assert_eq!(a.to_string(), "module#0");
        assert_eq!(a.as_u32(), 0);
        assert!(a < b);
        assert_eq!(a, ModuleId::from_u32(0));
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn program_space_types_are_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<ProgramSpace>();
        assert_send_sync::<ModuleId>();
        assert_send_sync::<CodeMapEntry>();
        assert_send_sync::<ModuleRecord>();
        assert_send_sync::<LoadedModule<'static>>();
        assert_send_sync::<CodeMapIter<'static>>();
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\region.rs
//! Internal region pool backing the memory manager.
//!
//! A [`Region`] is a contiguous block of host memory (a `Vec<u8>`) divided
//! into fixed-size **slots**. Allocations are contiguous runs of slots — the
//! cache-local, index-resolvable layout the Memory Architecture asks for —
//! tracked in a [`BTreeMap`] keyed by start slot. Released runs are coalesced
//! back into a free list and reused before the manager grows.
//!
//! Every slot carries a **generation** counter that is bumped on release, so
//! an address issued against a slot that has since been reused is detected as
//! stale. This is the `[Region | Slot / Index | Generation]` protection the
//! Memory Architecture describes in §9.
//!
//! Generations are `u32` counters that wrap on overflow; a stale address
//! could only validate again after 2³² release/reuse cycles of the very same
//! slot, which is not a practical concern for a session-scoped manager.
//!
//! # Status
//!
//! This module is the **internal Region Allocator** of the Memory Manager: it
//! is currently a private component. The architecture allows it to become a
//! separate internal component in a future version **without affecting the
//! public API**. It is deliberately **not exposed publicly**.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::space::SpaceId;

/// Metadata of one live allocation (a contiguous run of slots).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct AllocMeta {
    /// Number of contiguous slots occupied by the allocation.
    pub(crate) slots: u32,
    /// Generation recorded in the issued address.
    pub(crate) generation: u32,
    /// The space that owns this allocation.
    pub(crate) space: SpaceId,
}

/// A resolved allocation, ready for byte-level access.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct Resolved {
    /// Byte offset of the allocation within the region buffer.
    pub(crate) byte_start: usize,
    /// Size of the allocation in bytes (slot granularity).
    pub(crate) size: usize,
    /// The space that owns the allocation.
    pub(crate) space: SpaceId,
    /// Number of slots occupied by the allocation.
    pub(crate) slots: u32,
}

/// A contiguous block of host memory divided into fixed-size slots.
pub(crate) struct Region {
    data: Vec<u8>,
    slot_size: usize,
    slots: u32,
    generations: Vec<u32>,
    allocations: BTreeMap<u32, AllocMeta>,
    free: BTreeMap<u32, u32>,
    zero_on_deallocate: bool,
    live_slots: u64,
}

impl Region {
    /// Creates a region of `region_size` bytes divided into `slot_size` slots.
    ///
    /// The caller guarantees that `slot_size` divides `region_size` (the
    /// configuration is validated by the manager).
    pub(crate) fn new(region_size: usize, slot_size: usize, zero_on_deallocate: bool) -> Region {
        debug_assert_eq!(
            region_size % slot_size,
            0,
            "slot size must divide region size"
        );
        let slots = (region_size / slot_size) as u32;
        Region {
            data: vec![0; region_size],
            slot_size,
            slots,
            generations: vec![0; slots as usize],
            allocations: BTreeMap::new(),
            free: BTreeMap::from([(0, slots)]),
            zero_on_deallocate,
            live_slots: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the total byte capacity of this region.
    pub(crate) fn capacity_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.data.len() as u64
    }

    /// Returns the number of bytes held by live allocations.
    pub(crate) fn live_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.live_slots * self.slot_size as u64
    }

    /// Returns the number of bytes currently free for allocation.
    pub(crate) fn free_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        (u64::from(self.slots) - self.live_slots) * self.slot_size as u64
    }

    /// Returns the number of live allocations in this region.
    pub(crate) fn allocation_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.allocations.len()
    }

    /// Returns `true` when the region holds no live allocations.
    pub(crate) fn is_idle(&self) -> bool {
        self.allocations.is_empty()
    }

    /// Yields the metadata of every live allocation in this region.
    pub(crate) fn allocations(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &AllocMeta> {
        self.allocations.values()
    }

    /// Attempts a first-fit allocation of `slots` contiguous slots.
    ///
    /// Returns the start slot and the generation issued to the new
    /// allocation, or `None` when no free run fits.
    pub(crate) fn alloc(&mut self, slots: u32, space: SpaceId) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
        debug_assert!(slots > 0 && slots <= self.slots, "invalid slot run request");
        let (start, run) = self.find_run(slots)?;
        self.split_run(start, run, slots);
        let generation = self.generations[start as usize].wrapping_add(1);
        for slot in &mut self.generations[start as usize..start as usize + slots as usize] {
            *slot = generation;
        }
        self.allocations.insert(
            start,
            AllocMeta {
                slots,
                generation,
                space,
            },
        );
        self.live_slots += u64::from(slots);
        Some((start, generation))
    }

    /// Finds the first free run that fits `slots` slots (first-fit policy).
    fn find_run(&self, slots: u32) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
        self.free
            .iter()
            .find_map(|(&start, &run)| (run >= slots).then_some((start, run)))
    }

    /// Removes `take` slots from the front of the free run at `start`,
    /// reinserting any remainder into the free list.
    fn split_run(&mut self, start: u32, run: u32, take: u32) {
        self.free.remove(&start);
        if run > take {
            self.free.insert(start + take, run - take);
        }
    }

    /// Releases the allocation addressed by `address`.
    ///
    /// The slot generations are bumped so older addresses become stale, the
    /// bytes are zeroed when configured, and the freed run is coalesced back
    /// into the free list for immediate reuse.
    pub(crate) fn dealloc(&mut self, address: LogicalAddress) -> Result<()> {
        let meta = self.take_allocation(address)?;
        let start = address.slot();
        let slots = meta.slots;
        for slot in &mut self.generations[start as usize..start as usize + slots as usize] {
            *slot = slot.wrapping_add(1);
        }
        if self.zero_on_deallocate {
            let byte_start = start as usize * self.slot_size;
            let byte_len = slots as usize * self.slot_size;
            self.data[byte_start..byte_start + byte_len].fill(0);
        }
        self.insert_free(start, slots);
        self.live_slots -= u64::from(slots);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Removes and returns the allocation at `address`, validating it.
    fn take_allocation(&mut self, address: LogicalAddress) -> Result<AllocMeta> {
        let start = address.slot();
        match self.allocations.get(&start) {
            Some(meta) if meta.generation == address.generation() => {
                let meta = *meta;
                self.allocations.remove(&start);
                Ok(meta)
            }
            Some(meta) => Err(Error::StaleAddress {
                address,
                current: meta.generation,
            }),
            None => Err(Error::NotAllocated { address }),
        }
    }

    /// Inserts the freed run `[start, start + slots)` into the free list,
    /// coalescing it with any adjacent free runs.
    fn insert_free(&mut self, start: u32, slots: u32) {
        let (mut start, mut len) = (start, slots);
        if let Some((&prev_start, &prev_len)) = self.free.range(..start).next_back() {
            if prev_start + prev_len == start {
                self.free.remove(&prev_start);
                start = prev_start;
                len += prev_len;
            }
        }
        if let Some(&next_len) = self.free.get(&(start + len)) {
            self.free.remove(&(start + len));
            len += next_len;
        }
        self.free.insert(start, len);
    }

    /// Resolves `address` to a byte range, validating liveness and generation.
    pub(crate) fn resolve(&self, address: LogicalAddress) -> Result<Resolved> {
        let start = address.slot();
        let meta = match self.allocations.get(&start) {
            Some(meta) if meta.generation == address.generation() => meta,
            Some(meta) => {
                return Err(Error::StaleAddress {
                    address,
                    current: meta.generation,
                });
            }
            None => return Err(Error::NotAllocated { address }),
        };
        Ok(Resolved {
            byte_start: start as usize * self.slot_size,
            size: meta.slots as usize * self.slot_size,
            space: meta.space,
            slots: meta.slots,
        })
    }

    /// Returns `true` when `address` refers to a live allocation with a
    /// matching generation.
    pub(crate) fn contains(&self, address: LogicalAddress) -> bool {
        match self.allocations.get(&address.slot()) {
            Some(meta) => meta.generation == address.generation(),
            None => false,
        }
    }

    /// Copies bytes from the allocation at `address` into `buf`.
    pub(crate) fn read(
        &self,
        address: LogicalAddress,
        offset: usize,
        buf: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let resolved = self.resolve(address)?;
        Self::check_range(address, offset, buf.len(), resolved.size)?;
        let from = resolved.byte_start + offset;
        buf.copy_from_slice(&self.data[from..from + buf.len()]);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Copies `data` into the allocation at `address`.
    pub(crate) fn write(
        &mut self,
        address: LogicalAddress,
        offset: usize,
        data: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let resolved = self.resolve(address)?;
        Self::check_range(address, offset, data.len(), resolved.size)?;
        let to = resolved.byte_start + offset;
        self.data[to..to + data.len()].copy_from_slice(data);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Fills `len` bytes at `offset` of the allocation at `address` with
    /// `value`.
    pub(crate) fn fill(
        &mut self,
        address: LogicalAddress,
        offset: usize,
        len: usize,
        value: u8,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let resolved = self.resolve(address)?;
        Self::check_range(address, offset, len, resolved.size)?;
        let to = resolved.byte_start + offset;
        self.data[to..to + len].fill(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Validates that `[offset, offset + length)` fits within `available`
    /// bytes, without overflowing on the addition.
    fn check_range(
        address: LogicalAddress,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
        available: usize,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        if offset > available || length > available - offset {
            return Err(Error::OutOfBounds {
                address,
                offset,
                length,
                available,
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const SLOT: usize = 64;

    fn region() -> Region {
        Region::new(1024, SLOT, true)
    }

    fn alloc(region: &mut Region, slots: u32, space: u32) -> LogicalAddress {
        let (start, generation) = region
            .alloc(slots, SpaceId::from_u32(space))
            .expect("allocation fits");
        LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, start, generation)
    }

    #[test]
    fn alloc_splits_runs_and_reports_capacity() {
        let mut region = region();
        assert_eq!(region.capacity_bytes(), 1024);
        assert_eq!(region.free_bytes(), 1024);

        let a = alloc(&mut region, 4, 1);
        assert_eq!(a.slot(), 0);
        assert_eq!(a.generation(), 1);
        let b = alloc(&mut region, 2, 1);
        assert_eq!(b.slot(), 4);
        assert_eq!(region.allocation_count(), 2);
        assert_eq!(region.live_bytes(), 6 * SLOT as u64);
        assert_eq!(region.free_bytes(), 10 * SLOT as u64);

        // No run fits 11 slots.
        assert!(region.alloc(11, SpaceId::from_u32(1)).is_none());
        // The tail run of 10 slots fits exactly 10.
        assert!(region.alloc(10, SpaceId::from_u32(1)).is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn dealloc_coalesces_adjacent_runs() {
        let mut region = region();
        let a = alloc(&mut region, 4, 1); // slots 0..4
        let b = alloc(&mut region, 2, 1); // slots 4..6
        let c = alloc(&mut region, 2, 1); // slots 6..8
        assert_eq!(b.slot(), 4);
        assert_eq!(c.slot(), 6);

        // Freeing the middle run leaves two separate free runs (4..6, 8..16).
        region.dealloc(b).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(region.free_bytes(), 10 * SLOT as u64);
        assert_eq!(region.live_bytes(), 6 * SLOT as u64);

        // Freeing the first run merges it with the middle run (0..6, 8..16).
        region.dealloc(a).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(region.free_bytes(), 14 * SLOT as u64);

        // Freeing the last run coalesces everything into one free run again.
        region.dealloc(c).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(region.free_bytes(), 1024);
        assert_eq!(region.live_bytes(), 0);
        assert!(region.is_idle());

        // The coalesced region can be fully reallocated as one run.
        let d = alloc(&mut region, 16, 1);
        assert_eq!(d.slot(), 0);
        assert_eq!(region.allocation_count(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn generations_bump_on_reuse_and_catch_stale_addresses() {
        let mut region = region();
        let a = alloc(&mut region, 1, 1);
        assert_eq!(a.generation(), 1);

        region.dealloc(a).unwrap();

        let b = alloc(&mut region, 1, 1);
        assert_eq!(b.slot(), 0);
        // Released (bump to 2) then reallocated (bump to 3).
        assert_eq!(b.generation(), 3);

        // The old address is stale; the new one resolves.
        assert!(matches!(
            region.resolve(a),
            Err(Error::StaleAddress { address, .. }) if address == a
        ));
        assert!(!region.contains(a));
        assert!(region.contains(b));
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolve_rejects_unknown_and_freed_addresses() {
        let mut region = region();
        let a = alloc(&mut region, 2, 1);
        region.dealloc(a).unwrap();

        // Freed address: not allocated anymore.
        assert!(matches!(region.resolve(a), Err(Error::NotAllocated { .. })));
        // Never-allocated slot.
        let bogus = LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 12, 1);
        assert!(matches!(
            region.resolve(bogus),
            Err(Error::NotAllocated { .. })
        ));
        // Foreign region index is rejected by the manager, not the region.
        assert!(matches!(region.dealloc(a), Err(Error::NotAllocated { .. })));
    }

    #[test]
    fn read_write_and_fill_obey_bounds() {
        let mut region = region();
        let a = alloc(&mut region, 2, 1);
        assert_eq!(region.resolve(a).unwrap().size, 2 * SLOT);

        region.write(a, 0, b"hello").unwrap();
        let mut buf = [0u8; 5];
        region.read(a, 0, &mut buf).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&buf, b"hello");

        region.fill(a, 5, 3, 0xAB).unwrap();
        let mut tail = [0u8; 3];
        region.read(a, 5, &mut tail).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(tail, [0xAB; 3]);

        assert!(matches!(
            region.write(a, 128, b"x"),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            region.read(a, 128, &mut [0u8; 1]),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            region.fill(a, usize::MAX, 1, 0),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn partial_reuse_of_a_freed_run_invalidates_old_addresses() {
        let mut region = region();
        let whole = alloc(&mut region, 4, 1); // slots 0..4, generation 1
        assert_eq!(whole.generation(), 1);
        region.dealloc(whole).unwrap();

        // Reallocate only the first two slots of the freed run.
        let part = alloc(&mut region, 2, 1); // slots 0..2, generation 3
        assert_eq!(part.slot(), 0);
        assert_ne!(part.generation(), whole.generation());

        // The old address is stale: same start slot, newer generation.
        assert!(matches!(
            region.resolve(whole),
            Err(Error::StaleAddress { .. })
        ));

        // An address pointing into the tail of the old run no longer refers
        // to a run start and is simply not allocated.
        let tail = LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 2, whole.generation());
        assert!(matches!(
            region.resolve(tail),
            Err(Error::NotAllocated { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn zeroing_on_deallocate_is_optional() {
        let mut zeroing = Region::new(256, SLOT, true);
        let a = alloc(&mut zeroing, 1, 1);
        zeroing.write(a, 0, &[0xFF; 64]).unwrap();
        zeroing.dealloc(a).unwrap();
        let b = alloc(&mut zeroing, 1, 1);
        assert_eq!(b.slot(), 0);
        let mut buf = [0xFFu8; 64];
        zeroing.read(b, 0, &mut buf).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(buf, [0u8; 64]);

        let mut preserving = Region::new(256, SLOT, false);
        let c = alloc(&mut preserving, 1, 1);
        preserving.write(c, 0, &[0xFF; 64]).unwrap();
        preserving.dealloc(c).unwrap();
        let d = alloc(&mut preserving, 1, 1);
        let mut kept = [0u8; 64];
        preserving.read(d, 0, &mut kept).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(kept, [0xFF; 64]);
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\space.rs
//! Memory spaces and their registration identities.
//!
//! The RA architecture freezes five memory spaces: Program, Active, Entity,
//! Work and Registry. The memory manager does **not** implement the internal
//! layout of any space — that is the responsibility of later phases — but it
//! registers and tracks them, and every allocation belongs to exactly one
//! registered space.

use std::fmt;

/// The five frozen RA memory spaces.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum SpaceKind {
    /// Program Space (PS) — ready-to-execute program representation: REI,
    /// module metadata, constants and code map.
    Program,
    /// Active Space (AS) — the execution-tracking grid of active records.
    Active,
    /// Entity Space (ES) — runtime entities: variables, arrays, strings,
    /// objects.
    Entity,
    /// Work Space (WS) — temporary calculations and intermediate results.
    Work,
    /// Registry Space (RS) — the identity, relationship and metadata layer.
    Registry,
}

impl SpaceKind {
    /// All five frozen spaces, in canonical order.
    pub const ALL: [SpaceKind; 5] = [
        SpaceKind::Program,
        SpaceKind::Active,
        SpaceKind::Entity,
        SpaceKind::Work,
        SpaceKind::Registry,
    ];

    /// Returns the lowercase canonical name of this space.
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            SpaceKind::Program => "program",
            SpaceKind::Active => "active",
            SpaceKind::Entity => "entity",
            SpaceKind::Work => "work",
            SpaceKind::Registry => "registry",
        }
    }

    /// Returns a one-line description of this space's responsibility.
    pub fn description(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            SpaceKind::Program => "ready-to-execute program representation and constants",
            SpaceKind::Active => "current calls and execution-tracking state",
            SpaceKind::Entity => "runtime entities: variables, arrays, strings, objects",
            SpaceKind::Work => "temporary calculations and intermediate results",
            SpaceKind::Registry => "identity, relationship and metadata layer",
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for SpaceKind {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.name())
    }
}

/// A unique handle to a registered space, assigned by the memory manager.
///
/// Identifiers are never reused within a manager's lifetime, so a stale
/// [`SpaceId`] can always be detected by the manager.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct SpaceId(u32);

impl SpaceId {
    /// Returns the raw identifier value.
    pub fn as_u32(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Creates an identifier from a raw value.
    pub(crate) fn from_u32(value: u32) -> SpaceId {
        SpaceId(value)
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for SpaceId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let id = self.0;
        write!(f, "space#{id}")
    }
}

/// The registration record of one space inside the memory manager.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SpaceRecord {
    id: SpaceId,
    kind: SpaceKind,
}

impl SpaceRecord {
    /// Creates a new registration record.
    pub(crate) fn new(id: SpaceId, kind: SpaceKind) -> SpaceRecord {
        SpaceRecord { id, kind }
    }

    /// Returns the unique identifier of this space.
    pub fn id(self) -> SpaceId {
        self.id
    }

    /// Returns the kind of this space.
    pub fn kind(self) -> SpaceKind {
        self.kind
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn all_spaces_have_names_and_descriptions() {
        assert_eq!(SpaceKind::ALL.len(), 5);
        for kind in SpaceKind::ALL {
            assert!(!kind.name().is_empty());
            assert!(!kind.description().is_empty());
        }
        assert_eq!(SpaceKind::Program.name(), "program");
        assert_eq!(SpaceKind::Registry.name(), "registry");
        assert_eq!(SpaceKind::Entity.to_string(), "entity");
    }

    #[test]
    fn space_ids_are_distinct_values() {
        let a = SpaceId::from_u32(0);
        let b = SpaceId::from_u32(1);
        assert_eq!(a.as_u32(), 0);
        assert_eq!(b.as_u32(), 1);
        assert_eq!(a, SpaceId::from_u32(0));
        assert_ne!(a, b);
        assert!(a < b);
        assert_eq!(a.to_string(), "space#0");
    }

    #[test]
    fn space_records_expose_identity() {
        let record = SpaceRecord::new(SpaceId::from_u32(3), SpaceKind::Work);
        assert_eq!(record.id(), SpaceId::from_u32(3));
        assert_eq!(record.kind(), SpaceKind::Work);
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn space_types_are_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<SpaceKind>();
        assert_send_sync::<SpaceId>();
        assert_send_sync::<SpaceRecord>();
    }
}

### F:\RA_01\software\memory\src\value_list.rs
//! ✅ Indexed Value List — the per-cell value storage of Entity Space (Phase
//! 3D-2), extended with ✅ **Phase 3D-3 — Extended Value Storage**.
//!
//! Per the frozen Entity Space V1 architecture document, *"each Entity Cell
//! contains an ordered, indexed Value List"* (§3, §12): the Grid groups
//! entities by runtime ownership, while the **List gives deterministic
//! ordering inside an Entity Cell** and **compiled slots permit direct
//! positional access instead of repeated variable-name searches** (§11).
//! Source entity names are compiled to slots (e.g. `x → slot 0, y → slot 1,
//! z → slot 2`, §4); this module provides exactly that positional storage.
//!
//! The frozen roadmap divides Entity Space into six phases; this module
//! implements ✅ **Phase 3D-2 — Indexed Value List** and ✅ **Phase 3D-3 —
//! Extended Value Storage** (the storage representation for strings, arrays
//! and objects). Binding a list to an Entity Grid cell is provided by
//! [`EntitySpace::bind_value_list`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::bind_value_list),
//! which owns the `EntityCell → ValueList` binding. This module deliberately
//! does **not** implement:
//!
//! * local entity resolution through Active Space — ✅ Phase 3D-4,
//!   implemented in the [`local_entity`](crate::local_entity) module;
//! * ✅ the global entity area (Phase 3D-5) — implemented in the
//!   [`global_entity`](crate::global_entity) module;
//! * ⏳ name→slot debug metadata (Phase 3D-6);
//! * name/scope lookup and execution semantics — those belong to later
//!   phases or to the Runtime.
//!
//! # Phase 3D-3 — Extended Value Storage
//!
//! Phase 3D-3 adds the value categories of the Entity Space architecture
//! beyond the primitive V1 set — **strings, arrays and objects** — as
//! *storage representation only*. There is no lookup, no binding and no
//! execution semantics here.
//!
//! An extended value's **content** lives in its own manager allocation
//! (addressed by a [`LogicalAddress`]); the **slot record** embeds a compact
//! [`ValueStorage`] handle — the content's logical address plus a semantic
//! length (UTF-8 byte length for strings, element count for arrays, entry
//! count for objects). The slot itself stays fixed-width, so compiled-slot
//! ordering and direct positional access are unchanged: slot `i` still lives
//! at byte offset `i × 24`.
//!
//! Content encodings are deterministic and manager-backed only:
//!
//! * a **string** is the raw UTF-8 bytes of its text;
//! * an **array** is the sequence of its encoded element records (each one
//!   a `24`-byte slot record), element `i` at byte offset `i × 24`;
//! * an **object** is the ordered sequence of its entries, each entry a
//!   `u32` key-byte-length prefix, the UTF-8 key bytes, and the encoded
//!   value record — insertion order is preserved.
//!
//! Ownership is exclusive and deterministic: a slot **owns** its content, so
//! overwriting, clearing or destroying a slot releases the previous content
//! allocation through the manager (no leaks, no aliasing). Handles cannot be
//! fabricated or copied between slots: [`ValueList::set`] rejects extended
//! handles and arrays/objects accept primitive elements only, so no two
//! slots ever share one content allocation.
//!
//! # Values and encoding
//!
//! Slots hold **primitive values** ([`Value`]: `Nil`, `Int`, `Float`,
//! `Bool`) and **extended-value handles** (`String`, `Array`, `Object`). The
//! exact physical value representation is open in the architecture (§13), so
//! this module defines it: each slot is a fixed-width 24-byte record — a tag
//! byte, an 8-byte primitive payload, and (for extended values) the embedded
//! 12-byte storage [`LogicalAddress`] plus a `u32` semantic length. `Nil` is
//! the cleared state of a slot.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```
//! use ra_memory::{EntitySpace, MemoryManager, Value, ValueList};
//!
//! let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
//! // The Entity Space owns runtime-data storage; lists live under its id.
//! let entity = EntitySpace::new(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, entity.space_id(), 3).unwrap();
//!
//! // Compiled slots: x → 0, y → 1, z → 2.
//! list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(5)).unwrap();
//! list.set(&mut memory, 1, Value::Int(3)).unwrap();
//! list.set(&mut memory, 2, Value::Int(8)).unwrap();
//!
//! // Extended values (Phase 3D-3): storage representation only.
//! list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "greeting").unwrap();
//! list.set_array(&mut memory, 1, &[Value::Int(1), Value::Bool(true)]).unwrap();
//! list.set_object(&mut memory, 2, &[("name", Value::Float(2.5))]).unwrap();
//!
//! assert_eq!(list.read_string(&memory, 0).unwrap(), "greeting");
//! assert_eq!(
//!     list.read_array(&memory, 1).unwrap(),
//!     vec![Value::Int(1), Value::Bool(true)]
//! );
//! assert_eq!(
//!     list.read_object(&memory, 2).unwrap(),
//!     vec![("name".to_string(), Value::Float(2.5))]
//! );
//!
//! list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! entity.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
//! assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
//! ```

use std::fmt;

use crate::address::LogicalAddress;
use crate::codec::{get_u32, put_u32};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::manager::MemoryManager;
use crate::space::SpaceId;

/// Byte width of one value-slot record: a tag byte, an 8-byte primitive
/// payload, and (for extended values) the embedded 12-byte storage address
/// plus a `u32` semantic length.
const VALUE_RECORD_SIZE: usize = 24;
/// Record tag for a cleared (`Nil`) slot.
const TAG_NIL: u8 = 0;
/// Record tag for a signed 64-bit integer value.
const TAG_INT: u8 = 1;
/// Record tag for a 64-bit IEEE-754 float value.
const TAG_FLOAT: u8 = 2;
/// Record tag for a boolean value.
const TAG_BOOL: u8 = 3;
/// Record tag for an extended string value (Phase 3D-3).
const TAG_STRING: u8 = 4;
/// Record tag for an extended array value (Phase 3D-3).
const TAG_ARRAY: u8 = 5;
/// Record tag for an extended object value (Phase 3D-3).
const TAG_OBJECT: u8 = 6;
/// Byte offset of the tag within a slot record.
const TAG_OFFSET: usize = 0;
/// Byte offset of the 8-byte primitive payload within a slot record.
const PAYLOAD_OFFSET: usize = 4;
/// Payload byte width.
const PAYLOAD_SIZE: usize = 8;
/// Byte offset of the embedded extended-value storage address within a slot
/// record (12 bytes: region, slot, generation). The first `u32` overlaps the
/// primitive payload start — a record uses one or the other, never both.
const EXT_ADDRESS: usize = 4;
/// Byte offset of the extended-value semantic length within a slot record.
const EXT_LENGTH: usize = 16;
/// Byte width of one encoded element record inside an array's content
/// storage (the same fixed-width record the ValueList slots use).
const EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE: usize = VALUE_RECORD_SIZE;
/// Byte width of the `u32` key-length prefix of one object entry.
const OBJECT_KEY_LENGTH: usize = 4;

/// A reference to the manager-backed content storage of an extended value.
///
/// Phase 3D-3 stores the *content* of a string, array or object in its own
/// [`MemoryManager`] allocation and embeds this compact handle — the content
/// [`LogicalAddress`] plus a semantic length — in the owning slot record.
/// Handles are read-only observations: they are produced by
/// [`ValueList::get`], [`ValueList::values`] and the `read_*` methods, and
/// cannot be fabricated or copied into another slot, so every content
/// allocation is owned by exactly one slot.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValueStorage {
    /// The logical address of the content allocation.
    address: LogicalAddress,
    /// The semantic length: UTF-8 byte length for strings, element count for
    /// arrays, entry count for objects.
    length: u32,
}

impl ValueStorage {
    /// Returns the logical address of the content allocation.
    pub fn address(self) -> LogicalAddress {
        self.address
    }

    /// Returns the semantic length of the content.
    ///
    /// The meaning depends on the value category: UTF-8 byte length for
    /// strings, element count for arrays, entry count for objects.
    pub fn length(self) -> u32 {
        self.length
    }
}

/// A primitive or extended value stored in an Entity Space value list.
///
/// `Nil` is the cleared state of a slot. The exact physical value
/// representation is open in the architecture (§13); this is the Phase 3D-2
/// primitive set extended by Phase 3D-3's [`ValueStorage`]-backed string,
/// array and object categories.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum Value {
    /// An empty / cleared slot.
    Nil,
    /// A signed 64-bit integer value.
    Int(i64),
    /// A 64-bit IEEE-754 floating-point value.
    Float(f64),
    /// A boolean value.
    Bool(bool),
    /// An extended string value; the text is stored in manager-backed
    /// storage and referenced by the embedded [`ValueStorage`].
    String(ValueStorage),
    /// An extended array value; the ordered element records are stored in
    /// manager-backed storage and referenced by the embedded
    /// [`ValueStorage`].
    Array(ValueStorage),
    /// An extended object value; the ordered key→value entries are stored in
    /// manager-backed storage and referenced by the embedded
    /// [`ValueStorage`].
    Object(ValueStorage),
}

impl Value {
    /// Returns the canonical name of this value's category (e.g. `"string"`,
    /// `"int"`), matching the category names used in
    /// [`Error::ValueMismatch`].
    pub fn category(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Value::Nil => "nil",
            Value::Int(_) => "int",
            Value::Float(_) => "float",
            Value::Bool(_) => "bool",
            Value::String(_) => "string",
            Value::Array(_) => "array",
            Value::Object(_) => "object",
        }
    }

    /// Returns `true` when this is an extended value (string, array or
    /// object) backed by manager storage.
    fn is_extended(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Value::String(_) | Value::Array(_) | Value::Object(_))
    }
}

/// An ordered, indexed list of values stored in one manager allocation (the
/// indexed Value List of the frozen ES architecture, extended by Phase 3D-3).
///
/// Slots are positional and deterministic: compiled slot `i` lives at byte
/// offset `i × 24` of the list storage, so reads and writes are direct with
/// no name lookup. All operations are bounds-checked.
///
/// Extended values (Phase 3D-3) keep this model: a slot holds a
/// [`ValueStorage`] handle, and the content lives in a separate manager
/// allocation owned by the slot. Content is released automatically when a
/// slot is overwritten or cleared, and when the list is destroyed.
///
/// The list is created under a caller-supplied [`SpaceId`] with
/// [`ValueList::new`] and is then bound to an Entity Grid cell through
/// [`EntitySpace::bind_value_list`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::bind_value_list).
/// Entity Space is the **exclusive owner** of the cell↔list binding: a
/// `ValueList` handle over an existing list can only be constructed
/// internally from a cell's embedded binding metadata, so external callers
/// can never fabricate a list over arbitrary storage.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ValueList {
    /// The space that owns the list storage and any extended-value content.
    space_id: SpaceId,
    /// The logical address of the list storage.
    address: LogicalAddress,
    /// The number of positional slots.
    capacity: usize,
}

impl ValueList {
    /// Creates a value list with `capacity` slots under `space`.
    ///
    /// Every slot starts cleared (`Nil`). `space` is typically the Entity
    /// Space's id (see
    /// [`EntitySpace::space_id`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::space_id)).
    /// Extended-value content is allocated under the same space.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `capacity` is zero.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be allocated.
    pub fn new(memory: &mut MemoryManager, space: SpaceId, capacity: usize) -> Result<ValueList> {
        if capacity == 0 {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "value list capacity must be non-zero".into(),
            ));
        }
        let bytes = capacity
            .checked_mul(VALUE_RECORD_SIZE)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::InvalidArgument("value list capacity is too large".into()))?;
        let address = memory.allocate(space, bytes)?;
        // Deterministic initial state: every slot is Nil.
        memory.fill(address, 0, bytes, 0)?;
        Ok(ValueList {
            space_id: space,
            address,
            capacity,
        })
    }

    /// Constructs a handle over existing manager-backed list storage without
    /// allocating anything.
    ///
    /// Internal to the crate: only Entity Space builds handles this way, from
    /// the metadata embedded in a live cell's record, so a `ValueList` can
    /// never be fabricated over arbitrary storage by external callers.
    pub(crate) fn adopt(space: SpaceId, address: LogicalAddress, capacity: usize) -> ValueList {
        ValueList {
            space_id: space,
            address,
            capacity,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the number of positional slots in this list.
    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.capacity
    }

    /// Returns the space that owns the list storage.
    ///
    /// Binding-only metadata, exposed internally so Entity Space can verify a
    /// list belongs to it before embedding it in a cell record.
    pub(crate) fn space_id(&self) -> SpaceId {
        self.space_id
    }

    /// Returns the logical address of the list storage.
    ///
    /// Binding-only metadata, exposed internally so Entity Space can embed
    /// the address in a cell record. The Runtime never obtains raw list
    /// addresses.
    pub(crate) fn address(&self) -> LogicalAddress {
        self.address
    }

    /// Writes `value` into the compiled `slot`.
    ///
    /// Slot numbers correspond to compiled entity slots (e.g. `x → 0`), so
    /// this is direct positional storage with no name lookup.
    ///
    /// Extended values must be written with [`ValueList::set_string`],
    /// [`ValueList::set_array`] or [`ValueList::set_object`]; passing an
    /// extended handle here is rejected so that no slot ever aliases another
    /// slot's content.
    ///
    /// Any extended content previously stored in the slot is released
    /// (before the new record is written).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when `value` is an extended handle.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be read or written.
    pub fn set(&self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, slot: usize, value: Value) -> Result<()> {
        if value.is_extended() {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "extended values must be stored with set_string, set_array or set_object".into(),
            ));
        }
        self.check_slot(slot)?;
        let old = self.read_record(memory, slot)?;
        self.release_extended(memory, &old)?;
        self.write_record(memory, slot, &encode_value(value))
    }

    /// Reads the value stored in the compiled `slot`.
    ///
    /// Extended slots return a [`ValueStorage`] handle; use
    /// [`ValueList::read_string`], [`ValueList::read_array`] or
    /// [`ValueList::read_object`] to read the actual content.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidData`] when the stored record is corrupt.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be read.
    pub fn get(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, slot: usize) -> Result<Value> {
        self.check_slot(slot)?;
        decode_value(self.read_record(memory, slot)?)
    }

    /// Clears `slot`, resetting it to [`Value::Nil`] and releasing any
    /// extended content the slot owned.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Same as [`ValueList::set`].
    pub fn clear(&self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, slot: usize) -> Result<()> {
        self.set(memory, slot, Value::Nil)
    }

    /// Stores `text` in the compiled `slot` as an extended string value.
    ///
    /// The UTF-8 bytes are copied into a fresh manager allocation and the
    /// slot embeds a [`ValueStorage`] handle to it. An empty string is
    /// stored as a one-byte content allocation with semantic length `0`.
    /// Any extended content previously stored in the slot is released.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the list.
    /// * Manager errors when the content or record cannot be written.
    pub fn set_string(&self, memory: &mut MemoryManager, slot: usize, text: &str) -> Result<()> {
        self.check_slot(slot)?;
        let byte_length = text.len();
        if byte_length > u32::MAX as usize {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "string content is too large to address".into(),
            ));
        }
        let address = memory.allocate(self.space_id, byte_length.max(1))?;
        if byte_length > 0 {
            memory.write(address, 0, text.as_bytes())?;
        }
        self.commit_extended(memory, slot, TAG_STRING, address, byte_length as u32)
    }

    /// Stores `values` in the compiled `slot` as an extended array value.
    ///
    /// The element records (in order) are copied into a fresh manager
    /// allocation; the slot embeds a [`ValueStorage`] handle whose length is
    /// the element count. Elements must be primitive values — nested
    /// extended values are out of scope for this phase. An empty array is
    /// stored as a one-byte content allocation with length `0`. Any extended
    /// content previously stored in the slot is released.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when an element is an extended value.
    /// * Manager errors when the content or record cannot be written.
    pub fn set_array(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        slot: usize,
        values: &[Value],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        self.check_slot(slot)?;
        if values.iter().any(|value| value.is_extended()) {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "array elements must be primitive values in Phase 3D-3".into(),
            ));
        }
        let count = values.len();
        if count > u32::MAX as usize {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "array is too large to address".into(),
            ));
        }
        let bytes = count
            .checked_mul(EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::InvalidArgument("array content is too large".into()))?;
        let address = memory.allocate(self.space_id, bytes.max(1))?;
        for (index, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
            memory.write(address, index * EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE, &encode_value(*value))?;
        }
        self.commit_extended(memory, slot, TAG_ARRAY, address, count as u32)
    }

    /// Stores `entries` in the compiled `slot` as an extended object value.
    ///
    /// The entries (in insertion order) are copied into a fresh manager
    /// allocation; the slot embeds a [`ValueStorage`] handle whose length is
    /// the entry count. Values must be primitive values — nested extended
    /// values are out of scope for this phase. An empty object is stored as
    /// a one-byte content allocation with length `0`. Any extended content
    /// previously stored in the slot is released.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the list.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidArgument`] when a value is an extended value.
    /// * Manager errors when the content or record cannot be written.
    pub fn set_object(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        slot: usize,
        entries: &[(&str, Value)],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        self.check_slot(slot)?;
        if entries.iter().any(|(_, value)| value.is_extended()) {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "object values must be primitive values in Phase 3D-3".into(),
            ));
        }
        let count = entries.len();
        if count > u32::MAX as usize {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                "object is too large to address".into(),
            ));
        }
        let mut total = 0usize;
        for (key, _) in entries {
            if key.len() > u32::MAX as usize {
                return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(
                    "object key is too large to address".into(),
                ));
            }
            total = total
                .checked_add(OBJECT_KEY_LENGTH)
                .and_then(|sum| sum.checked_add(key.len()))
                .and_then(|sum| sum.checked_add(EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE))
                .ok_or_else(|| Error::InvalidArgument("object content is too large".into()))?;
        }
        let address = memory.allocate(self.space_id, total.max(1))?;
        let mut offset = 0usize;
        for (key, value) in entries {
            let mut key_length = [0u8; OBJECT_KEY_LENGTH];
            put_u32(&mut key_length, 0, key.len() as u32);
            memory.write(address, offset, &key_length)?;
            offset += OBJECT_KEY_LENGTH;
            memory.write(address, offset, key.as_bytes())?;
            offset += key.len();
            memory.write(address, offset, &encode_value(*value))?;
            offset += EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE;
        }
        self.commit_extended(memory, slot, TAG_OBJECT, address, count as u32)
    }

    /// Reads the string content of an extended string slot.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the list.
    /// * [`Error::ValueMismatch`] when the slot does not hold a string.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidData`] when the stored bytes are not valid UTF-8.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be read.
    pub fn read_string(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, slot: usize) -> Result<String> {
        self.check_slot(slot)?;
        let value = decode_value(self.read_record(memory, slot)?)?;
        match value {
            Value::String(storage) => {
                let length = storage.length() as usize;
                // Bound the read by the actual allocation before sizing any
                // host buffer (a corrupt handle must not trigger a huge
                // allocation). The manager reports slot-granular sizes, an
                // upper bound on the content bytes.
                if length > memory.size(storage.address())? {
                    return Err(Error::InvalidData(
                        "stored string length exceeds its allocation".into(),
                    ));
                }
                let mut bytes = vec![0u8; length];
                if length > 0 {
                    memory.read(storage.address(), 0, &mut bytes)?;
                }
                String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|error| {
                    Error::InvalidData(format!("stored string is not valid UTF-8: {error}"))
                })
            }
            other => Err(Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot,
                expected: "string",
                found: other.category(),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Reads the element records of an extended array slot, in order.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the list.
    /// * [`Error::ValueMismatch`] when the slot does not hold an array.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidData`] when a stored element record is corrupt.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be read.
    pub fn read_array(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, slot: usize) -> Result<Vec<Value>> {
        self.check_slot(slot)?;
        let value = decode_value(self.read_record(memory, slot)?)?;
        match value {
            Value::Array(storage) => {
                let count = storage.length() as usize;
                // Every element occupies EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE bytes; reject a
                // corrupt count before sizing any host buffer.
                let size = memory.size(storage.address())?;
                let required = count.checked_mul(EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE);
                if required.is_none_or(|bytes| bytes > size) {
                    return Err(Error::InvalidData(
                        "stored array element count exceeds its allocation".into(),
                    ));
                }
                let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(count);
                for index in 0..count {
                    let mut element = [0u8; EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE];
                    memory.read(storage.address(), index * EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE, &mut element)?;
                    values.push(decode_value(element)?);
                }
                Ok(values)
            }
            other => Err(Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot,
                expected: "array",
                found: other.category(),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Reads the entries of an extended object slot, in insertion order.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// * [`Error::OutOfBounds`] when `slot` is outside the list.
    /// * [`Error::ValueMismatch`] when the slot does not hold an object.
    /// * [`Error::InvalidData`] when a stored key is not valid UTF-8 or a
    ///   value record is corrupt.
    /// * Manager errors when the storage cannot be read.
    pub fn read_object(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, slot: usize) -> Result<Vec<(String, Value)>> {
        self.check_slot(slot)?;
        let value = decode_value(self.read_record(memory, slot)?)?;
        match value {
            Value::Object(storage) => {
                let count = storage.length() as usize;
                // Every entry occupies at least OBJECT_KEY_LENGTH +
                // EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE bytes; reject a corrupt count before
                // sizing any host buffer.
                let size = memory.size(storage.address())?;
                let minimum = count.checked_mul(OBJECT_KEY_LENGTH + EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE);
                if minimum.is_none_or(|bytes| bytes > size) {
                    return Err(Error::InvalidData(
                        "stored object entry count exceeds its allocation".into(),
                    ));
                }
                let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(count);
                let mut offset = 0usize;
                for _ in 0..count {
                    let mut key_length = [0u8; OBJECT_KEY_LENGTH];
                    memory.read(storage.address(), offset, &mut key_length)?;
                    offset += OBJECT_KEY_LENGTH;
                    let key_bytes_len = get_u32(&key_length, 0) as usize;
                    if offset + key_bytes_len > size {
                        return Err(Error::InvalidData(
                            "stored object key exceeds its allocation".into(),
                        ));
                    }
                    let mut key_bytes = vec![0u8; key_bytes_len];
                    if key_bytes_len > 0 {
                        memory.read(storage.address(), offset, &mut key_bytes)?;
                        offset += key_bytes_len;
                    }
                    let key = String::from_utf8(key_bytes).map_err(|error| {
                        Error::InvalidData(format!("stored object key is not valid UTF-8: {error}"))
                    })?;
                    let mut value_buf = [0u8; EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE];
                    memory.read(storage.address(), offset, &mut value_buf)?;
                    offset += EXT_ELEMENT_SIZE;
                    entries.push((key, decode_value(value_buf)?));
                }
                Ok(entries)
            }
            other => Err(Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot,
                expected: "object",
                found: other.category(),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Returns an iterator over the slot values in positional order, from
    /// slot 0 to `capacity - 1`.
    ///
    /// Extended slots yield their [`ValueStorage`] handles; the content is
    /// read on demand with the `read_*` methods.
    ///
    /// Construction cannot fail; the `Result` mirrors the crate's other
    /// iterator constructors and reserves room for future validation.
    pub fn values<'a>(&self, memory: &'a MemoryManager) -> Result<ValueIter<'a>> {
        Ok(ValueIter::new(memory, self.address, self.capacity))
    }

    /// Deallocates the list storage and every extended-value content
    /// allocation the slots owned.
    ///
    /// Consumes the list; no further operations are valid. This method is
    /// for lists that were **never bound** to an Entity Grid cell. For a
    /// bound list, destruction must flow through
    /// [`EntitySpace::destroy_value_list`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::destroy_value_list):
    /// calling `destroy` on a view resolved by
    /// [`EntitySpace::value_list`](crate::entity_space::EntitySpace::value_list)
    /// reclaims the storage behind Entity Space's back, leaving the cell's
    /// embedded binding pointing at reclaimed storage (a stale binding that
    /// later resolution detects, but that violates Entity Space's exclusive
    /// ownership of the `EntityCell → ValueList` binding).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error when the storage cannot be reclaimed.
    pub fn destroy(self, memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> Result<()> {
        for slot in 0..self.capacity {
            let record = self.read_record(memory, slot)?;
            self.release_extended(memory, &record)?;
        }
        memory.deallocate(self.address)
    }

    /// Validates that `slot` is within the list.
    fn check_slot(&self, slot: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if slot >= self.capacity {
            return Err(Error::OutOfBounds {
                address: self.address,
                offset: slot.saturating_mul(VALUE_RECORD_SIZE),
                length: VALUE_RECORD_SIZE,
                available: self.capacity * VALUE_RECORD_SIZE,
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reads the raw record of the compiled `slot`.
    fn read_record(&self, memory: &MemoryManager, slot: usize) -> Result<[u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE]> {
        let mut buf = [0u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE];
        memory.read(self.address, slot * VALUE_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(buf)
    }

    /// Writes `record` into the compiled `slot`.
    fn write_record(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        slot: usize,
        record: &[u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        memory.write(self.address, slot * VALUE_RECORD_SIZE, record)
    }

    /// Commits a freshly allocated content allocation to `slot` as an
    /// extended value, releasing any content the slot owned before.
    ///
    /// The previous content is released before the new record is written.
    /// On any failure after allocation the fresh content is deallocated
    /// again, so nothing leaks unless the underlying storage is itself
    /// corrupt.
    fn commit_extended(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        slot: usize,
        tag: u8,
        address: LogicalAddress,
        length: u32,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let record = encode_extended(tag, address, length);
        let old = self.read_record(memory, slot)?;
        match self.release_extended(memory, &old) {
            Ok(()) => match self.write_record(memory, slot, &record) {
                Ok(()) => Ok(()),
                Err(error) => {
                    memory.deallocate(address)?;
                    Err(error)
                }
            },
            Err(error) => {
                memory.deallocate(address)?;
                Err(error)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Releases the content allocation of an extended slot record.
    ///
    /// Primitive and `Nil` records own no content and are left untouched.
    fn release_extended(
        &self,
        memory: &mut MemoryManager,
        record: &[u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        match record[TAG_OFFSET] {
            TAG_STRING | TAG_ARRAY | TAG_OBJECT => {
                let (address, _) = decode_extended(record);
                memory.deallocate(address)
            }
            _ => Ok(()),
        }
    }
}

/// An iterator over the slot values of a value list, in positional order.
///
/// Values are decoded on demand from list storage. Extended slots yield
/// their [`ValueStorage`] handles. Iteration stops after the first read
/// failure, which is reported as the final item.
pub struct ValueIter<'a> {
    memory: &'a MemoryManager,
    address: LogicalAddress,
    capacity: usize,
    position: usize,
}

impl fmt::Debug for ValueIter<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("ValueIter")
            .field("address", &self.address)
            .field("capacity", &self.capacity)
            .field("position", &self.position)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl<'a> ValueIter<'a> {
    /// Creates a value iterator over `capacity` slots at `address`.
    fn new(memory: &'a MemoryManager, address: LogicalAddress, capacity: usize) -> ValueIter<'a> {
        ValueIter {
            memory,
            address,
            capacity,
            position: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl Iterator for ValueIter<'_> {
    type Item = Result<Value>;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
        if self.position >= self.capacity {
            return None;
        }
        let mut buf = [0u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE];
        match self
            .memory
            .read(self.address, self.position * VALUE_RECORD_SIZE, &mut buf)
        {
            Ok(()) => {
                self.position += 1;
                Some(decode_value(buf))
            }
            Err(error) => {
                self.position = self.capacity;
                Some(Err(error))
            }
        }
    }
}

// ---- value codec ----

/// Encodes a value as one fixed-width slot record.
fn encode_value(value: Value) -> [u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE];
    match value {
        Value::Nil => {}
        Value::Int(int) => {
            buf[TAG_OFFSET] = TAG_INT;
            buf[PAYLOAD_OFFSET..PAYLOAD_OFFSET + PAYLOAD_SIZE].copy_from_slice(&int.to_le_bytes());
        }
        Value::Float(float) => {
            buf[TAG_OFFSET] = TAG_FLOAT;
            buf[PAYLOAD_OFFSET..PAYLOAD_OFFSET + PAYLOAD_SIZE]
                .copy_from_slice(&float.to_bits().to_le_bytes());
        }
        Value::Bool(flag) => {
            buf[TAG_OFFSET] = TAG_BOOL;
            buf[PAYLOAD_OFFSET] = u8::from(flag);
        }
        Value::String(storage) => encode_extended_into(&mut buf, TAG_STRING, storage),
        Value::Array(storage) => encode_extended_into(&mut buf, TAG_ARRAY, storage),
        Value::Object(storage) => encode_extended_into(&mut buf, TAG_OBJECT, storage),
    }
    buf
}

/// Encodes an extended value's storage handle into a slot record.
fn encode_extended(tag: u8, address: LogicalAddress, length: u32) -> [u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE] {
    let mut buf = [0u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE];
    encode_extended_into(&mut buf, tag, ValueStorage { address, length });
    buf
}

/// Writes the storage handle fields of an extended value into `buf`.
fn encode_extended_into(buf: &mut [u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE], tag: u8, storage: ValueStorage) {
    buf[TAG_OFFSET] = tag;
    put_u32(buf, EXT_ADDRESS, storage.address.region());
    put_u32(buf, EXT_ADDRESS + 4, storage.address.slot());
    put_u32(buf, EXT_ADDRESS + 8, storage.address.generation());
    put_u32(buf, EXT_LENGTH, storage.length);
}

/// Decodes the storage handle fields of an extended slot record.
fn decode_extended(buf: &[u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE]) -> (LogicalAddress, u32) {
    let address = LogicalAddress::from_parts(
        get_u32(buf, EXT_ADDRESS),
        get_u32(buf, EXT_ADDRESS + 4),
        get_u32(buf, EXT_ADDRESS + 8),
    );
    (address, get_u32(buf, EXT_LENGTH))
}

/// Decodes a value from one fixed-width slot record.
fn decode_value(buf: [u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE]) -> Result<Value> {
    match buf[TAG_OFFSET] {
        TAG_NIL => Ok(Value::Nil),
        TAG_INT => Ok(Value::Int(i64::from_le_bytes(read_payload(&buf)))),
        TAG_FLOAT => Ok(Value::Float(f64::from_bits(u64::from_le_bytes(
            read_payload(&buf),
        )))),
        TAG_BOOL => Ok(Value::Bool(buf[PAYLOAD_OFFSET] != 0)),
        TAG_STRING => {
            let (address, length) = decode_extended(&buf);
            Ok(Value::String(ValueStorage { address, length }))
        }
        TAG_ARRAY => {
            let (address, length) = decode_extended(&buf);
            Ok(Value::Array(ValueStorage { address, length }))
        }
        TAG_OBJECT => {
            let (address, length) = decode_extended(&buf);
            Ok(Value::Object(ValueStorage { address, length }))
        }
        tag => Err(Error::InvalidData(format!("unknown value tag {tag}"))),
    }
}

/// Reads the 8-byte payload of a slot record.
fn read_payload(buf: &[u8; VALUE_RECORD_SIZE]) -> [u8; PAYLOAD_SIZE] {
    let mut payload = [0u8; PAYLOAD_SIZE];
    payload.copy_from_slice(&buf[PAYLOAD_OFFSET..PAYLOAD_OFFSET + PAYLOAD_SIZE]);
    payload
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::space::SpaceKind;

    /// Registers a fresh Entity space for list storage.
    fn entity_space(memory: &mut MemoryManager) -> SpaceId {
        memory.register_space(SpaceKind::Entity)
    }

    #[test]
    fn new_allocates_under_space_with_all_nil_slots() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 4).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(list.capacity(), 4);
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 1);

        let values: Vec<_> = list
            .values(&memory)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|value| value.unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(values, vec![Value::Nil, Value::Nil, Value::Nil, Value::Nil]);

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_and_get_round_trip_all_value_kinds() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 4).unwrap();

        list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(i64::MIN)).unwrap();
        list.set(&mut memory, 1, Value::Int(i64::MAX)).unwrap();
        list.set(&mut memory, 2, Value::Bool(true)).unwrap();
        list.set(&mut memory, 3, Value::Nil).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(i64::MIN));
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 1).unwrap(), Value::Int(i64::MAX));
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 2).unwrap(), Value::Bool(true));
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 3).unwrap(), Value::Nil);

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        memory.shutdown();
    }

    #[test]
    fn float_values_round_trip_bit_exactly() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();

        for float in [
            0.0f64,
            -0.0,
            std::f64::consts::PI,
            f64::MAX,
            f64::MIN,
            f64::NAN,
        ] {
            list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Float(float)).unwrap();
            match list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap() {
                Value::Float(got) => assert_eq!(got.to_bits(), float.to_bits()),
                other => panic!("expected Float, got {other:?}"),
            }
        }

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        memory.shutdown();
    }

    #[test]
    fn positional_order_is_deterministic() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 3).unwrap();

        // Compiled slots: x → 0, y → 1, z → 2.
        list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(5)).unwrap();
        list.set(&mut memory, 1, Value::Int(3)).unwrap();
        list.set(&mut memory, 2, Value::Int(8)).unwrap();

        let values: Vec<_> = list
            .values(&memory)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|value| value.unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(values, vec![Value::Int(5), Value::Int(3), Value::Int(8)]);

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        memory.shutdown();
    }

    #[test]
    fn slots_are_bounds_checked() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();

        assert!(matches!(
            list.set(&mut memory, 2, Value::Int(1)),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            list.get(&memory, 5),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            list.clear(&mut memory, 2),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            list.set_string(&mut memory, 2, "x"),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            list.set_array(&mut memory, 2, &[Value::Int(1)]),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            list.set_object(&mut memory, 2, &[("k", Value::Int(1))]),
            Err(Error::OutOfBounds { .. })
        ));

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        memory.shutdown();
    }

    #[test]
    fn zero_capacity_is_rejected() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        assert!(matches!(
            ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 0),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        memory.shutdown();
    }

    #[test]
    fn clear_resets_slot_to_nil() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();

        list.set(&mut memory, 1, Value::Int(42)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 1).unwrap(), Value::Int(42));
        list.clear(&mut memory, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 1).unwrap(), Value::Nil);
        // Writing Nil directly is the same as clearing.
        list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(1)).unwrap();
        list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Nil).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Nil);

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        memory.shutdown();
    }

    #[test]
    fn lists_are_isolated_from_each_other() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let first = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();
        let second = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();

        first.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(10)).unwrap();
        second.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(20)).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(first.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(10));
        assert_eq!(second.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(20));

        first.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        second.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    // ---- Phase 3D-3: extended value storage ----

    #[test]
    fn strings_round_trip_through_manager_storage() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();

        list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "hello world").unwrap();
        list.set_string(&mut memory, 1, "").unwrap();

        // The slot holds a storage handle; the content lives separately.
        let storage = match list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap() {
            Value::String(storage) => storage,
            other => panic!("expected String handle, got {other:?}"),
        };
        assert_eq!(storage.length(), 11);
        assert!(memory.contains(storage.address()));
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap().category(), "string");

        assert_eq!(list.read_string(&memory, 0).unwrap(), "hello world");
        assert_eq!(list.read_string(&memory, 1).unwrap(), "");

        // List allocation + two content allocations (1 byte for the empty
        // string).
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 3);

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn arrays_round_trip_preserving_order() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();

        list.set_array(
            &mut memory,
            0,
            &[Value::Int(5), Value::Bool(true), Value::Float(1.5)],
        )
        .unwrap();
        list.set_array(&mut memory, 1, &[]).unwrap();

        let storage = match list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap() {
            Value::Array(storage) => storage,
            other => panic!("expected Array handle, got {other:?}"),
        };
        assert_eq!(storage.length(), 3);
        assert_eq!(
            list.read_array(&memory, 0).unwrap(),
            vec![Value::Int(5), Value::Bool(true), Value::Float(1.5)]
        );
        // Empty array round-trips with length zero.
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 1).unwrap().category(), "array");
        assert_eq!(list.read_array(&memory, 1).unwrap(), Vec::<Value>::new());

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
