        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn objects_round_trip_preserving_entry_order() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();

        let entries = [
            ("x", Value::Int(1)),
            ("y", Value::Int(2)),
            ("flag", Value::Bool(false)),
            ("", Value::Nil),
        ];
        list.set_object(&mut memory, 0, &entries).unwrap();
        list.set_object(&mut memory, 1, &[]).unwrap();

        let storage = match list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap() {
            Value::Object(storage) => storage,
            other => panic!("expected Object handle, got {other:?}"),
        };
        assert_eq!(storage.length(), 4);
        assert_eq!(
            list.read_object(&memory, 0).unwrap(),
            vec![
                ("x".to_string(), Value::Int(1)),
                ("y".to_string(), Value::Int(2)),
                ("flag".to_string(), Value::Bool(false)),
                (String::new(), Value::Nil),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            list.read_object(&memory, 1).unwrap(),
            Vec::<(String, Value)>::new()
        );

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn overwriting_releases_previous_extended_storage() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 2).unwrap();

        list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "first").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 2);
        // Replacing an extended value releases the previous content.
        list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "second").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 2);
        assert_eq!(list.read_string(&memory, 0).unwrap(), "second");

        // Replacing with a primitive also releases the content.
        list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(7)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 1);
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap(), Value::Int(7));

        // Clearing releases the content.
        list.set_array(&mut memory, 1, &[Value::Bool(true)])
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 2);
        list.clear(&mut memory, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 1);
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 1).unwrap(), Value::Nil);

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn destroy_releases_all_extended_storage() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 3).unwrap();

        list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "a string").unwrap();
        list.set_array(&mut memory, 1, &[Value::Int(1), Value::Int(2)])
            .unwrap();
        list.set_object(&mut memory, 2, &[("k", Value::Float(0.5))])
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 4);

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.space_usage(space).allocations(), 0);
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn extended_values_survive_iteration_in_order() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 3).unwrap();

        list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "s").unwrap();
        list.set(&mut memory, 1, Value::Int(3)).unwrap();
        list.set_array(&mut memory, 2, &[Value::Bool(true)])
            .unwrap();

        let values: Vec<_> = list
            .values(&memory)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|value| value.unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(values.len(), 3);
        assert_eq!(values[0].category(), "string");
        assert_eq!(values[1], Value::Int(3));
        assert_eq!(values[2].category(), "array");

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        memory.shutdown();
    }

    #[test]
    fn extended_handles_cannot_be_stored_directly_or_nested() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 3).unwrap();

        list.set_string(&mut memory, 0, "abc").unwrap();
        let handle = list.get(&memory, 0).unwrap();

        // `set` rejects extended handles: no aliasing between slots.
        assert!(matches!(
            list.set(&mut memory, 1, handle),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        // Arrays and objects accept primitive elements/values only.
        assert!(matches!(
            list.set_array(&mut memory, 1, &[handle]),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            list.set_object(&mut memory, 1, &[("k", handle)]),
            Err(Error::InvalidArgument(_))
        ));

        // The rejected writes left the slots untouched.
        assert_eq!(list.get(&memory, 1).unwrap(), Value::Nil);
        assert_eq!(list.read_string(&memory, 0).unwrap(), "abc");

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(memory.shutdown().live_allocations(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn readers_reject_wrong_categories() {
        let mut memory = MemoryManager::new();
        let space = entity_space(&mut memory);
        let list = ValueList::new(&mut memory, space, 4).unwrap();

        list.set(&mut memory, 0, Value::Int(1)).unwrap();
        list.set(&mut memory, 1, Value::Nil).unwrap();
        list.set_string(&mut memory, 2, "s").unwrap();
        list.set_array(&mut memory, 3, &[Value::Int(1)]).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            list.read_string(&memory, 0).unwrap_err(),
            Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot: 0,
                expected: "string",
                found: "int",
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            list.read_array(&memory, 1).unwrap_err(),
            Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot: 1,
                expected: "array",
                found: "nil",
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            list.read_object(&memory, 0).unwrap_err(),
            Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot: 0,
                expected: "object",
                found: "int",
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            list.read_object(&memory, 3).unwrap_err(),
            Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot: 3,
                expected: "object",
                found: "array",
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            list.read_array(&memory, 2).unwrap_err(),
            Error::ValueMismatch {
                slot: 2,
                expected: "array",
                found: "string",
            }
        );

        list.destroy(&mut memory).unwrap();
        memory.shutdown();
    }

    #[test]
    fn encoded_extended_records_round_trip() {
        let storage = ValueStorage {
            address: LogicalAddress::from_parts(3, 9, 2),
            length: 4,
        };
        for value in [
            Value::String(storage),
            Value::Array(storage),
            Value::Object(storage),
        ] {
            let buf = encode_value(value);
            assert_eq!(decode_value(buf).unwrap(), value);
        }
        // The record layout: tag, then the 12-byte address, then the length.
        let buf = encode_extended(TAG_ARRAY, storage.address, storage.length);
        assert_eq!(buf[TAG_OFFSET], TAG_ARRAY);
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&buf, EXT_ADDRESS), 3);
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&buf, EXT_ADDRESS + 4), 9);
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&buf, EXT_ADDRESS + 8), 2);
        assert_eq!(get_u32(&buf, EXT_LENGTH), 4);
        assert_eq!(decode_extended(&buf), (storage.address, 4));
    }

    #[test]
    fn value_categories_are_descriptive() {
        assert_eq!(Value::Nil.category(), "nil");
        assert_eq!(Value::Int(1).category(), "int");
        assert_eq!(Value::Float(1.0).category(), "float");
        assert_eq!(Value::Bool(true).category(), "bool");
        let storage = ValueStorage {
            address: LogicalAddress::from_parts(0, 0, 0),
            length: 0,
        };
        assert_eq!(Value::String(storage).category(), "string");
        assert_eq!(Value::Array(storage).category(), "array");
        assert_eq!(Value::Object(storage).category(), "object");
    }

    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}

    #[test]
    fn value_list_types_are_send_and_sync() {
        assert_send_sync::<ValueList>();
        assert_send_sync::<ValueIter<'static>>();
        assert_send_sync::<Value>();
        assert_send_sync::<ValueStorage>();
    }
